News.title: Man shot dead in London street at memorial service as murder probe launched
News.content:
Man shot dead in London street at memorial service as murder probe launched

The victim was pronounced dead after multiple shots were heard at the junction of Braybrook Street and Erconwald Street in East Acton

View Image Braybrook Street, Acton (Image: Google Street View)

A man has been shot dead at a memorial service in London in front of 50 people, as a murder investigation was launched.

Met Police detectives are investigating after the 40-year-old was found at the junction of Braybrook Street and Erconwald Street in East Acton on Friday evening. Officers were called at around 7.47pm after members of the public reported hearing multiple shots.

Around 50-people - including children - had been gathered in the area for a memorial service when the incident occurred.

Police and London Ambulance Service crews attended the scene and treated the man, but despite the efforts of medical staff, he was pronounced dead.

The Metropolitan Police said that, while a post-mortem examination is yet to take place, the victim is "believed to have sustained a gunshot wound".

No arrests have been made yet. The police added that the man's family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

Detectives are now working to establish the full circumstances of the incident and a crime scene was still in place on Braybrook Street as of 5pm. Detective Chief Inspector Brian Howie, who is leading the investigation, said the incident happened as a "large number of people had gathered for a memorial service".

He said: "Our thoughts are with the family and friends of a man whose life was taken in a senseless act of violence. We understand a large number of people had gathered for a memorial service and what should have been a time to come together in remembrance has instead left a family devastated.

"We believe between 40 and 50 people, including children, were present when this incident occurred. Someone knows what happened and we need them to come forward.

Article continues below

"If you were around Erconwald Street, Braybrook Street, the surrounding roads or Wormwood Scrubs playground between 18:00hrs and 20:00hrs, please think carefully about what you saw. Did you see anyone carrying or concealing weapons, people on bicycles acting suspiciously, or vehicles being driven at speed?

"We also want to hear from anyone with photographs, video, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage or who has seen anything relevant on social media. However insignificant it may seem, the smallest piece of information could prove crucial in helping us establish what happened and identify those responsible."

Anyone holding information about this incident is asked to contact the police quoting CAD 7011/2Oct.

News.title: Christa Pike's lawyers give brutally honest reaction to prison chief quitting
News.content:
Christa Pike's lawyers give brutally honest reaction to prison chief quitting

Frank Strada handed in his resignation amid intensifying scrutiny of Tennessee’s execution procedures after Christa Pike survived two lethal injections and was rushed to hospital

View 3 Images Tennessee's Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada has quit (Image: AP Photo/George Walker IV)

Lawyers representing Christa Pike have responded to the news Tennessee's head of prisons is resigning following her extraordinary botched execution.

‌



‌



The death-row prisoner survived two lethal injections and has been left fighting for her life. She was supposed to be put to death on Wednesday evening for the brutal murder of Colleen Slemmer, 19, back in 1995 but she was hospitalised after becoming the first person in the US to undergo such an execution attempt and live.

‌



It was announced today that Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada has quit, a decision he said is "in the best interests" of the state. He called the ongoing investigation into the incident "entirely appropriate and necessary".

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Christa Pike, sentenced to death for the murder of Colleen Slemmer three decades ago, survived two injections (Image: WVLT 8)

Christa Pike: Everything we know as killer left unconscious and on ventilator READ MORE :

Pike's attorneys welcomed Strada's departure, but said it "does nothing to help Christa now.”

‌



Her four-lawyer team said in a statement: “What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person. We hope the governor’s call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee’s entire death penalty system.”

Her legal team said they believed problems with the IV lines caused the pentobarbital to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream.

Strada took over the Correction Department in January 2023 after serving as deputy director of the Arizona Department of Corrections. In late 2024, he announced that Tennessee was changing its lethal injection protocol and would use only pentobarbital.

‌



View 3 Images The prisoner remains unconscious and on a ventilator at a hospital (Image: Tennessee Department of Correction/AFP via Getty Images)

Pike was scheduled to be executed at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, where witnesses were present for the administration of the injections.

One of her lawyers, Stephen Ferrell, said Pike had "small veins that make insertion of a needle more difficult". The execution went ahead, however, and Pike was given two doses of pentobarbital. Witnesses said she was heard crying, gasping and breathing loudly as her right arm turned purple.

Article continues below

An independent review into the failed execution has been ordered by Tennessee governor Bill Lee. Mr Strada said: "I believe this review is entirely appropriate and necessary, and I look forward to doing everything I can to help determine exactly what occurred."

Departing Strada said in his resignation statement: “Serving as commissioner of the Tennessee department of correction has been a great honor, and I continue to believe the department carried out its responsibilities in accordance with the established protocol.

"I look forward to doing everything I can to help determine exactly what occurred.”

News.title: Sir Kevin Sinfield delivers Super League final trophy after completing latest epic challenge
News.content:
Sir Kevin Sinfield delivers Super League final trophy after completing latest epic challenge

Charity hero Sir Kevin Sinfield has completed seven super marathons in seven days ahead of watching son Jack for Wakefield Trinity in the final against Warrington Wolves

View 5 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield carries out the Super League Grand Final trophy (Image: Getty Images)

Charity hero Sir Kevin Sinfield delivered the trophy for the Super League Grand Final in front of 70,000 cheering fans — after completing another epic motor neurone disease (MND) fundraising challenge.

‌



‌



His son Jack, 22, featured in his first final for Wakefield Trinity in the clash with Warrington Wolves at Old Trafford.

‌



It comes as his dad finished running seven ultra marathons in seven days - stopping at all 12 English Super League clubs along the way.

‌



View 5 Images Marathon man Kevin Sinfield arrives at Old Trafford (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

Sir Kevin, 46, who was knighted in the King’s Birthday Honours for his extraordinary fundraising for motor neurone disease and his services to rugby league, finished his gruelling challenge by coming onto the pitch in Manchester with the trophy.

Since 2020 the rugby icon has helped raise more than £11m for charities in memory of former teammate Rob Burrow who died from motor neurone disease in 2024.

‌



As he stood on the pitch, he said: "It's great to be back, thank you to everyone's played a part this week. Rob would be so proud to everyone who's cared and showed the love."

View 5 Images Kevin Sinfield walks out with the Super League trophy (Image: Getty Images)

Setting off on the final leg of his challenge from St Helens, Sir Kevin said: “It’s just been the best week, really special for all of us.”

‌



Thanking his support team, he said: “These guys have been incredible, but the support along the route has been overwhelming, it's been better than we ever thought.

“And to meet all the MND families along the route, right across this stretch, we’ve had people from all the home nations visit and be a part of the extra miles, for them to see the love and care and support that’s out there for them has been wonderful for us.”

He added: “We set out to raise £77,000 that first year and we ended up with £2.8 million, so we could feel some momentum behind us … all the sponsors and charities we represent , the people who’ve been roadside for us have just driven us forward.

‌



“It’s been a wonderful thing to be part of for seven years and we’ll see so many great people and families today, we’ve just got to keep helping.”

View 5 Images Sir Kevin at the end of his latest challenge (Image: Mike EgertonPA Wire)

Jack admitted he has been missing his dad. He said: “I've spoke to him a little bit, but obviously he's been really tired.

‌



“I think I’ve said already that when he planned this last challenge and for it to finish at Old Trafford, I don't think even he could have imagined that I would be playing in it. So it’s worked out pretty well.

“I’ve obviously missed him a lot when he’s been away because I’m still living at home, so it’s really weird around the house without him.”

View 5 Images Sir Kevin in Hull at the start of the 7 in 7: The Grand Finale 2026 Challenge (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

‌



Jack grew up watching the Leeds Rhinos legend win the Super League seven times and knows it’s his moment to try and “emulate” his dad.

He said: “My first ever rugby league game was the 2004 Grand Final when I was three weeks old. I have been to every single one of the Grand Finals my dad has played in but the last one really stands out in 2015.

“I had just turned 11 then so that's the one I really remember the most, knowing it was his last game as well.”

Article continues below

Sir Kevin has raised more than £1 million for the MND Foundation with his seven-day run this week. The number seven is in honour of the shirt number his ex-team mate Rob wore for Leeds Rhinos.

The rugby legend and his team also got a visit from the Prince and Princess of Wales on their stop at Wakefield Trinity, West Yorkshire, on Tuesday.

News.title: Russia vows to continue retaliatory strikes in Ukraine and urge people to leave Kyiv
News.content:
Russia vows to continue retaliatory strikes in Ukraine and urge people to leave Kyiv

As Moscow escalate attacks on the infrastructure of Ukraine's capital, Russia's President Vladimir Putin has sent an ominous warning that attacks have only just begun

View 3 Images It has been another week of deadly attacks in Ukraine (Image: Aleksandr Gusev/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

Russia has warned foreign nationals ‌and diplomats to leave Ukraine’s capital after vowing that there will be no let up in its bombardment of Kyiv.

In Moscow's latest menacing message, says it will continue to carry out targeted retaliatory strikes on Ukraine. The Kremlin had warned all foreigners against visiting or staying in the capital in May.

This morning, another Russian strike has hit a second major bridge, Kyiv's Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko confirmed, as Vladimir Putin ramps up his offensive on critical Ukrainian infrastructure, injuring two people.

It comes days after the Pivdennyi Bridge was hit multiple times by Russian drones, paralyzing much of the city, leaving Klitschko claiming that "the enemy is tearing Kyiv apart".

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Damage to the Pivdennyi Bridge following a Russian strike (Image: Getty Images)

Vladimir Putin threatens nuclear strike on NATO countries over hoax 'blockade' claim READ MORE :

Today's chilling statement from Russia read: "In response to the Ukrainian Armed Forces' terrorist acts against the civilian population and civilian infrastructure of our country, the ‌Armed Forces of the Russian Federation are continuing to systematically carry out targeted strikes on military facilities in Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.

"Responsibility for any adverse consequences lies entirely with those who ignore ‌this warning."

While some nations had cautioned their citizens against travelling to Ukraine this summer, Russia noted "that not everyone has heeded these warnings and is knowingly exposing their lives to mortal danger".

The ministry added: "The ⁠Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs once again warns foreign nationals, including diplomatic mission staff, against staying in Ukraine or travelling to its territory.

View 3 Images Russia's President Vladimir Putin has sent an ominous warning (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

"Responsibility for any adverse consequences lies entirely with those who ignore this warning."

On Thursday, NATO appeared to call Russia's bluff after being sent an ominous nuclear attack warning as tensions escalate.

Putin dispatched a letter threatening to unleash the weapons should it feel its Baltic territory is coming under threat. In the diplomatic memo, Moscow said it has been made aware of 'information that NATO is preparing an air and naval blockade of Kaliningrad'.

In the alarming letter sent to Brussels , the Kremlin warn it "will be ready to use the entire arsenal of forces and capabilities at its disposal, including nuclear weapons, in order to defend its territory", according to a document sent to member states.

NATO has responded, dismissing the threat as "irresponsible nuclear rhetoric" with Secretary General Mark Rutte stating he doesn't believe Putin will follow through on the latest outrageous threat.

Andy Burnham said days before that he will “stand up to” Russian and Iranian “threats”, adding that his economic and social plans will improve the UK’s security.

He told the Labour party conference: “A country which invests in people’s success, rather than abandoning them and paying for failure.

“A country like that will be much more resilient to the shocks we will undoubtedly face in the rest of this century, and more able to meet its Nato obligations on defence.

“I will be steadfast in my support for Ukraine and stand up to threats wherever they come from, whether Russia, Iran, or anywhere.”

He continued: “We will be principled in our leadership in securing a two-state solution between Israel and Palestine, as Ed Miliband has done.

Article continues below

“A plan for Britain will enhance our social security and our national security. You don’t make Britain safer by leaving a younger generation without hope for the future and stuck at home looking at screens.

“You do it by giving young people hope again. And you do it by getting our economy growing again.”

News.title: Kemi Badenoch branded 'out of touch' for stance on fox hunting after gruesome video
News.content:
Kemi Badenoch branded 'out of touch' for stance on fox hunting after gruesome video

EXCLUSIVE: Footage shows a Heythrop Hunt kennel huntsman climbing into woodland near the village of Lower Swell to recover the body of the fox and then running away with it

View 3 Images Kemi Badenoch attended the Cocklebarrow Point to Point race, a fundraiser for the Heythrop Hunt

Kemi Badenoch was last night savaged for supporting a hunt that has a member being probed over an alleged fox-killing by hounds.

‌



‌



Footage of the apparent incident - deemed too distressing for Mirror to publish - emerged as Ms Badenoch prepares for her keynote speech at the Tory party conference. It shows a huntsman climbing into woodland near the village of Lower Swell, Gloucestershire, to recover the body of a fox on the morning of Friday, September 18, then running off with it.

‌



Blood and internal fox body parts were found at the scene.

‌



Boxing day hunts to be thing of the past with trail hunting set to be banned READ MORE :

View 3 Images A member of the hunt was seen recovering the body of a fox

The man is a member of the Heythrop Hunt – a group whose fundraiser Ms Badenoch spoke at in January.

She used her speech to criticise Labour’s proposed ban on trail hunting, in which hounds follow a pre-laid scent trail. The ban was put forward amid fears that trail hunting was used as a smokescreen for genuine fox hunting.

‌



The top Tory said: “A ban is completely the wrong priority for the country, and the Conservatives would oppose it. This is not about animal welfare; it is a political gesture driven by pressure from a small group of hard-left MPs.”

The British Hound Sports Association, hunting’s governing body, confirmed to us yesterday that it was probing the Heythrop member.

View 3 Images David Cameron previously rode with the Heythrop Hunt (Image: Max Mumby/Indigo, Getty Images)

‌



A spokesman said: “We will review the footage and seek an account from those present to establish the facts.

“The BHSA requires all recognised hunts and its members to comply with the law and its core principles and rules.

“Any evidence of suspected unlawful activity is a matter for the police to assess.” It is not the first time Heythrop Hunt members have been suspected of illegal activity. In 2012, two were convicted of hunting foxes illegally, in a prosecution brought by the RSPCA.

‌



Labour MP Ruth Jones MP said: “Kemi Badenoch saying the ban is unnecessary only shows how out of touch she is with public opinion. Over 80% of the general public, including farmers and rural communities support a ban on fox hunting. It is cruel and barbaric.”

Fellow Labour MP Irene Campbell said of Ms Badenoch supporting the Hunt: “This certainly does not bode well for the future of animal welfare in the UK, and perhaps indicates the path the Tories may be taking us down.”

Rowan Hughes of the Hunt Saboteurs Association, which obtained the Lower Swell video, said: “Every week we hear from rural people who want to bring an end to hunting. Rural communities are far from being united by a love of animal cruelty and blood sports, that is just a vocal minority.”

Article continues below

Emma Slawinski, Chief Executive of the League Against Cruel Sports, said: “The government is absolutely right to strengthen fox hunting laws and to ban trail hunting.” Defra is currently weighing up the responses to a public consultation on a trail hunting ban.

Gloucestershire Constabulary said a rural crime officer was told of the Lower Swell allegation. The Tory party declined to comment.

News.title: Tennessee prison chief resigns after failed Christa Pike execution attempt
News.content:
Tennessee prison chief resigns after failed Christa Pike execution attempt

Christa Pike survived two lethal injections in a failed execution attempt in Tennessee, leaving her fighting for her life in hospital

View 2 Images Christa Pike (Image: Tennessee Department of Correction/AFP via Getty Images)

Tennessee's head of prisons is resigning following the botched execution of Christa Pike.

Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada is stepping down, a decision he said is "in the best interests" of the state. Christa Pike survived two lethal injections in a failed execution attempt that left her fighting for her life in hospital.

The US convicted murderer was set to be executed on Wednesday evening for the brutal murder of Colleen Slemmer, 19, in 1995 and would have become the first woman to be executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. A statement released by Mr Strada said he believes "the Department carried out its responsibilities in accordance with the established protocol."

An independent review into the failed execution has been ordered by Tennessee governor Bill Lee. Mr Strada said: "I believe this review is entirely appropriate and necessary, and I look forward to doing everything I can to help determine exactly what occurred."

View 2 Images Emergency services arriving at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution after Pike's failed execution (Image: AP Photo/George Walker IV)

Pike had spent three decades waiting for her execution following the horrific killing, which is also known as the "Satanic Panic Murder". Ms Slemmer was tortured by pike and her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, as the pair carved a pentagram into the teen’s chest, while Pike also took a piece of her skull as a souvenir, according to investigators.

Pike remains hospitalised, unconscious and on a ventilator following her failed execution, her lawyers have said in a court filing. As of late Thursday, hospital staff were working to save her life and clear the two doses of the lethal drugs administered from her system.

Pike's lawyer, Stephen Ferrell, said Pike had "small veins that make insertion of a needle more difficult". The execution went ahead, however, and Pike was given two doses of pentobarbital.

Article continues below

Witnesses said she was heard crying, gasping and breathing loudly as her right arm turned purple. One said: "Her mouth fell open a few times, and she began to loudly snore. She gasped a few times."

The death row prisoner reportedly complained: “My arm feels like it’s about to burst open.” She begun to snore despite receiving the drugs, with neither dose stopping her heart.

News.title: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle 'treated like locals' on first UK outing together since return
News.content:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle 'treated like locals' on first UK outing together since return

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex's bargain pub grub set them back just over £35 as they begin blending in with locals after heading to The Falkland Arms in between the school run

View 3 Images Prince Harry and his wife Meghan headed out for a bargain lunch (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle were treated like regular customers as the couple enjoyed a relaxed £36 pub lunch together in the Cotswolds.

‌



‌



The outing marked the couple's first joint public appearance in Britain since relocating from the United States at the end of the summer. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex were captured walking hand-in-hand as they made their way to the historic 16th-century pub The Falkland Arms, in the Oxfordshire village of Great Tew.

‌



They enjoyed some time to themselves as they stopped for a meal while their children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, were at school. Meghan enjoyed a gluten-free beer-battered haddock and chips while Harry opted for chicken, ham and leek pie as they spent some valuable time together.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images The historic establishment welcomed the royal couple for lunch last week (Image: Falkland Arms)

Harry and Meghan spotted enjoying pub lunch date as couple seen together for first time since UK return READ MORE :

They didn't feel at all out of place and enjoyed their lunch unbothered as they settle into their new surroundings, it is said. The royals blended in effortlessly and clearly loved the charming pub, which was even referenced in MobLand by Pierce Brosnan's character Conrad Harrigan, who said they pour a great pint.

‌



The Falkland Arm is just a short distance from Soho Farmhouse, the private members' club where Meghan, 45, is known to have already begun Pilates sessions.

“Everyone here gets the royal treatment; it doesn’t matter who you are," a pub worker told The Sun.

"We’re lucky to get lots of different people visiting us, and everyone is treated like a local. When they visited, Harry and Meghan just acted like locals.”

‌



They added: "We're a proper traditional English pub with black Labradors, but our ale is served cold. We have folk nights and Sunday roasts."

View 3 Images The couple were seen wearing shades before heading into the pub (stock image) (Image: ANP/AFP via Getty Images)

Both donned sunglasses as they arrived, with Meghan wearing a casual all-black outfit with white shoes, while Harry wore a Santa Barbara fire department cap - a nod to their former home near Montecito, California.

‌



The trip came after Meghan has so far largely stayed out of the public eye following the family’s move back to Britain in August.

But it wasn't her first visit to the Oxfordshire pub. Last week she stopped b with close friend Kelly McKee Zajfen and her young son, and was also spotted at The Three Horseshoes in Asthall, roughly 16 miles away, in the company of chat show host Ellen DeGeneres and her wife Portia de Rossi.

Harry, meanwhile, has made a string of public appearances since the move, including attending the WellChild Awards and the Invictus Spirit Gala Dinner and Awards. The Duke also attended a black-tie gala supporting Ukraine before making a brief trip back to the US for engagements in New York.

Article continues below

The Sussexes’ return to Britain has come as their long-running dispute over security arrangements continues. The issue was brought back into focus after two men, believed to have been working for a European photo agency, were reportedly seen in a white van outside Archie and Lilibet’s school.

News.title: Donald Trump's wild week as he won't rule out declaring midterms state of emergency
News.content:
Donald Trump's wild week as he won't rule out declaring midterms state of emergency

Everything you need to know about Donald Trump's bizarre golf lies, the fact that he's having to campaign in places he shouldn't, JD Vance doing his best to help but dropping some clangers - and we explain the whole Jack Smith basketball thing for the British reader. Buckle up.

View Image Donald Trump is having to campaign in some unusal places... (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump revealed how far he's willing to go to undermine next month's Midterm elections in a deeply chilling interview this week. In the space of one hour with Time Magazine, Donald Trump failed to rule out declaring a state of emergency, claimed to have the highest IQ, insisted his dismal polls were "fake" and launched a furious and sweary rant about what he sees as unfair press coverage.

‌



‌



And that was just Wednesday. We'll also cover Trump's bizarre golf lies, the fact that he's having to campaign in places he shouldn't, JD Vance doing his best to help but dropping some clangers - and we explain the whole Jack Smith basketball thing for the British reader. Here's more on that and the rest of the wild and troubling things happening in Trumpworld this week. Buckle up.

‌



For more of our coverage of Trump's America: Subscribe to The Trump Update on YouTube

Subscribe to the US Dispatch - our weekly newsletter exclusively for Mirror+ readers - following all the gossip and intrigue from Trump's DC swamp

- following all the gossip and intrigue from Trump's DC swamp Follow Mikey Smith on Twitter, TikTok, Bluesky or Facebook.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Trump is campaigning in unexpected places

Starting at the end, Donald Trump held a rally in Alabama last night - one of a series of appearances in states that should be super-safe for Republicans. Last night's speech in Mobile, AL, saw him stump for Tommy Tuberville, who is stepping down as a senator to run for Governor. Tuberville won his senate seat by 20 points, and Trump won the state by 30 in 2024 - so he should be a slam dunk.

Then why is Trump there? Well, because a poll last month put Tuberville just 8 points ahead, with another this week putting him 13 points ahead with 8% undecided - still in the lead, but a massive collapse in support in one of America's reddest states. And it wasn't just Alabama. On Wednesday, Trump stumped in Oklahoma, which Trump won in 2024 by 34 points and has never voted for a Democrat in a single district for 26 years. No statewide polling there yet, but it's a weird place for a president to spend time this close to an election. From there he went to Texas. TEXAS. Where Democrat senate candidate James Talarico is ahead of Trump-backed Republican Ken Paxton by seven points. IN TEXAS.

‌



And that's despite a massive ad blitz by Texas Republicans. Trump is going back to Texas next week - and he was only there a couple of weeks ago for his weird midterm party convention - which Paxton has allegedly said privately did him more harm than good. He'll pay another visit to Alabama on Saturday to watch a football game. If I were reading the tea leaves of this from a campaign strategy point of view, I'd think it was someone who had given up on the battleground states as lost, and was trying to shore up the base to try and head off a massacre. But we'll see.

Trump himself said during the speech in Alabama: "I don't need the votes. I'm not running. But you're going to think of me as on the ballot right? Promise?" Problem with that is across the country Trump's average net approval rating is -26. At the same point in his first term, he was -10. At the same point in Biden's first term, he was -8.

Trump's golf boasts would make Kim Jong Un blush

Speaking of Tommy Tuberville, during his guest spot at last night's rally, the famously a bit mad and very outspoken senator buttered his boss up by bigging up his prowess as a golfer: "Trump has won 40 club championships. I want you to think about that. 40 club championships."

‌



So I took his advice and thought about it. And luckily, sportswriter Rick Reilly recently did so in The Washington Post, from which I learned the following. In 2000, Trump admitted to Reilly that whenever he buys or builds a golf club, he plays the first round on his own and calls that winning a club championship.

At the time he was claiming to have won 12. By 2013, he was claiming to have won 18, all on his own courses, many of them dubious. By 2024 he claimed he'd won 26. That's 8 in 11 years, which in itself is a feat. In April 2025 he claimed on Truth Social to have won 36. 10 in less than a year. While in office. Earlier this year he claimed to have won 43. Another 7 while in office. Kim Jong Un would blush.

JD Vance is helping

JD Vance has been doing his bit on the trail with a speech in Lakeland, Florida - which I only mention because he dropped some serious clangers. For a start, he accused Florida Democrat Governor candidate David Jolly of having "contorted himself like a pretzel to pander to the crazies" and added: "He'll do and say whatever it takes to stay relevant. He flips any flops with the wind because he's so desperate to be relevant. He is desperate to have a job where he gets to tell you how to live your life. He wants power."

‌



This from a man who said he went "back and forth between thinking Trump is a cynical a**hole like Nixon who wouldn't be that bad (and might even prove useful) or that he's America's Hitler" less than a decade before becoming the Vice President. He also took aim at Angie Nixon, a woman of colour and member of the House of Representatives. "When Angie Nixon calls herself a socialist," he said, "I think the right response is to say, then get the hell out of here. You don't belong in America." The Vice President, there, calling for a US citizen, born in Jacksonville, Florida, to be kicked out of the country because of her political views.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Trump attacks 'dirty' Obama and won't rule out declaring a state of emergency before the midterms

Trump gave an interview to Time Magazine this week, and I implore everyone to read the full transcript. It starts wild and only gets wilder. During the hour-long chat he suggests Supreme Court justices should be loyal to him - not to the law, not to the country...to him. He confirms he will absolutely be pardoning his entire staff before he leaves office.

‌



He claims Barack Obama didn't refurbish the White House because he "doesn't know if something's dirty or clean". A quick side note on this - it's not the first time, Trump has accused someone of not being able to see dirt. He said this in response to ABC News White House Correspondent Rachel Scott back in May.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

I'll let you guess what Rachel Scott and Barack Obama have in common. Anyway, he also spiralled into a sweary meltdown at the interviewer because - and I quote - "You haven't asked me one f-ing positive question". But to me the most alarming section was when he was asked a series of questions about what he had planned for the run-up to the midterms.

‌



He was asked a series of questions that should be pretty easy for the leader of a functioning democracy to say "no" to. First he was asked if he planned to dispatch ICE agents to polling places in the midterms. "Haven't thought of it," he said. Which is in itself, patently untrue, because people have asked him and his team about it a load of times. And, well, you might think, if you're voting, you're a US citizen, so why would you be worried about ICE agents being at polling places? Well, ask the friends and relatives of all the US citizens who have been wrongly arrested, disappeared, shot or killed in the last 18 months whether they'd feel comfortable walking past a line of ICE agents to cast their ballot?

And then he's asked whether he would declare a state of emergency ahead of the midterms other than in the case of widespread violence in the streets. "No, there would be no reason to do that..." ...is what any sane person would say in answer to that question. What he actually said was: "I don't rule anything out or in. We'll see."

Trump strong-arms Europe into releasing emergency reserves with threat of diesel export ban

Trump backed down on threats to ban the export of diesel from the US. But only after G7 leaders agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from their emergency reserves to bring global oil prices down. That's the spike in prices that he caused when he started bombing Iran, in case anyone was unsure.

‌



BBC unimpressed by Trump team slow-walking lawsuit discovery

Trump's team are seriously dragging their feet in the BBC lawsuit - and the beeb are not happy. Long story short, Trump is suing the BBC for $10billion (£7.5billion) over a slightly clumsily edited passage in a Panorama documentary, which Trump claims had materially damaged him ahead of of the 2024 election, an election he WON - despite having been watched, statistically speaking, by nobody who could vote in America.

Anyway, the BBC's lawyers this week lodged a complaint, because they have on twelve occasions provided documents to Trump's lawyers - including internal emails and amounting to more than 100,000 pages...and Trump's team have only sent one set of files to them. They accused trump's team of choosing to "ignore the instructions of this court and his obligations under the rules," and called for the court to issue a firm order threatening sanctions against the president if they don't comply in a timely manner.

Meanwhile, there's been a slight setback on the BBC's end. They wanted to interview Cassidy Hutchinson, who was a top aide to Trump's former chief of staff Mark Meadows at the time of the January 6th riots. She had previously testified to Congress in 2022 that Trump had ignored warnings that some of the crowd at the capitol were armed, and had said: "I'm the f***ing president, take me up to the capitol now" The beeb argued her testimony would be highly relevant to Trump's state of mind - given they're demanding Trump must prove he did not “foment or incite” the riot. The judge in the case, whose name I'm not going to say out loud because it sounds like a very rude word, disagreed, saying it was a "fishing expedition" - but said her sworn testimony to congress was available to them to refer to in court. And in any case, she'd almost certainly plead the fifth if she was subpoenaed, so it would be an unnecessary burden on her.

‌



Trump's £20 million propaganda blitz

Last week, we looked at the Trump ads that have started airing in the states, which despite clearly being Trump campaign ads - one of them was literally a 2024 campaign ad with the badges removed - are "paid for by the US Government". The White House has insisted they're not campaign ads, because there's no call to action to vote a certain way. In fact, they insist, they're "Public Service Announcements". Which conveniently means they don't have to declare how much they've spent on them. Even though it's taxpayers' cash.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The New York Times has a story out today suggesting Trump himself, personally, ordered the ads and said they should be paid for by taxpayers in a $20million (£15million) contract that used funds from the Department of Homeland Security. I imagine this will see the inside of a courtroom before too long - and that Trump's repeated statements telling voters to "pretend I'm on the ballot" in the midterms will do nothing to help the administration defend its assertion that the ads were legal because there was no call to action.

‌



Let me explain the Jack Smith thing

So if you're still hanging around the dystopian hellscape that everyone still calls "Twitter" despite Elon Musk's best efforts, you might have seen a bunch of videos of a Republican congressman trying to "gotcha" someone, but being humiliated because he got something wrong about a basketball game. Like an episode of "I'm Sorry I Haven't A Clue," it was truly hilarious, but relied on quite a lot of prior knowledge. So let's fill everyone in.

Jack Smith was the special consel nominated by the Justice Department to oversee the investigations into Trump's role in January 6th and his stash of documents at Mar A Lago. Donald Trump, as you can imagine, hates this guy. And a lot of Republicans in the Senate really like pleasing Donald Trump. Still.

For some reason. Anyway at about the same time, in 2023/24, there was a separate, parallel case being brought by prosecutors in Georgia - aimed, among other things, at his attempts to get Georgia's Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger to "find" 11,780 votes so he could win the state and overturn the 2020 election result. It stalled after Fulton County district attorney Fani Willis admitted she'd been having an affair with Nathan Wade, the special prosecutor who was leading the case against Trump in Georgia.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

So on Tuesday Jack Smith came for questioning before the Senate Judiciary Committee, and Republican Senator Eric Schmitt thought he had a blockbuster gotcha. Something that he could use to paint Smith as a corrupt official colluding with others in the deep state to weaponise the justice system into vindictive prosecutions of the then-former President. Schmitt asked Smith if he'd attended an NBA game between the Golden State Warriors and the Atlanta Hawks on February 3, 2024 - the day before Willis admitted the affair. The implication being that he - a DoJ employee - had been colluding with Georgia prosecutors to co-ordinate the prosecutions. A big no-no. Smith said no, he had not - and that he had never met with Willis or Wade. Schmitt suggested smugly that Smith had already committed perjury, and his produced a poster board that he claimed showed text messages from Smith's team discussing his plans to go to the game - before immediately pulling it down again. Smith asked for it to be held up a little longer so he could read it, to which Schmitt refused and called him a "dirtbag."

A little later, Smith clarified that he remembered attending a basketball game that month...but it was a women's college game, between the University of Maryland and the University of Iowa. He remembered the game because Caitlin Clark - now a WNBA superstar - had played.

Article continues below

Content cannot be displayed without consent

It was then that Senator Amy Klobuchar came with the missing piece of the puzzle...and noted that the University of Iowa's basketball team is called...the Hawkeyes. The game was in College Park, Maryland - just a few minutes' drive from Washington DC, but about 700 miles and a ten hour drive from Georgia.

"I think people should have their facts straight before they accuse someone of being a dirtbag, and not get the teams wrong," Klobuchar said. "I would just say, for a U.S. senator to have false information and imply, based on a confusion about the name of a team, which I knew knowing my Midwestern sports, and imply that you were in another city, that you were somehow involved that day in what was happening in Georgia and then call you a dirtbag is something that deserves an apology." So far, no apology has been forthcoming.

News.title: UK-Iranian dual national arrested over RAF Fairford released on bail
News.content:
A UK-Iranian dual national arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with an incident at RAF Fairford has been released on bail.

The 25-year-old man was arrested in the London borough of Westminster on Thursday. Searches of two properties in the same area have now finished.

A major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated after police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase in Gloucestershire last weekend.

Five other men in their twenties were arrested and were subsequently released on police bail. All five were UK nationals from London.

The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the events are continuing, police said.

Last weekend, the five men aged between 23 and 25 were arrested in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base operated by the US Air Force (USAF), sparking a major security incident.

The BBC understands that one of the men had dialled 999 himself, about an hour before a local farmer alerted police to a "large group" of masked men near the vehicles.

They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail on Monday in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".

Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired a Cobra meeting that afternoon in response. He later said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident, but did not provide any more details.

Tehran has strongly denied any involvement. The Iranian embassy in London said on Monday that it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" what it called "unfounded and malicious speculations" linking Iran to the incident.

News.title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage
News.content:
The 2026 Conservative conference is big enough to justify using Birmingham's Symphony Hall as its main stage again.

So, Kemi Badenoch will tread the same stage ageing rockers Marillion took last month - and where sequinned soprano Katherine Jenkins will perform next week. She'll also avoid the humiliation of a national party leader being squashed into a side room at a corporate conference centre (with drapes portioning off the empty space). Simply, the party is able to put bums on seats again - and by that measure, things are looking up.

Badenoch goes into the conference with her own position secure in the party. One senior Tory says "she has actually defied cynics like me" who initially disapproved of her leadership. Her standing with the public has improved and she is now, again on a very simple but crucial measure, much better known. Her allies are sure she has developed a clear identity among the public, confiding: "People now know who she is and they enjoy her interventions - the thing we hear most is I don't always agree with her but I know where she stands."

News.title: Man shot dead as families gather for memorial in London
News.content:
A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a "senseless act of violence" as up to 50 people â including children â gathered for a memorial service in west London.

The Met Police said it was called to the scene at 19:47 GMT on Friday after multiple shots had been heard by members of the public at the junction of Braybrook Street and Erconwald Street in East Acton.

Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service but the man was pronounced dead at the scene, despite the efforts of medics.

No arrests have been made and a police cordon remains in place in Braybrook Street. Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward.

The victim's family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

A post-mortem examination is scheduled to establish the cause of death, but the victim is believed to have sustained a gunshot wound, the force said.

Det Ch Insp Brian Howie, who is leading the investigation, said: "Our thoughts are with the family and friends of a man whose life was taken in a senseless act of violence.

"We understand a large number of people had gathered for a memorial service and what should have been a time to come together in remembrance has instead left a family devastated.

"We believe between 40 and 50 people, including children, were present when this incident occurred. Someone knows what happened and we need them to come forward."

He has asked anyone who was around Erconwald Street, Braybrook Street, the surrounding roads or Wormwood Scrubs playground between 18:00 and 20:00, to "please think carefully about what you saw".

He added: "Did you see anyone carrying or concealing weapons, people on bicycles acting suspiciously, or vehicles being driven at speed?

"We also want to hear from anyone with photographs, video, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage or who has seen anything relevant on social media.

"However insignificant it may seem, the smallest piece of information could prove crucial in helping us establish what happened and identify those responsible."

News.title: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises?
News.content:
Months before you have a chance to see your favourite artist, chances are you already know some of the big moments they have planned.

You'll also probably know the set list, the stage design, and - if you've really been paying attention - where to stand to get the best view.

When it comes to films and TV series, spoilers tend to be guarded against with warnings.

But for many major gigs, there's no escaping a stream of fan videos from the shows if you're online, whether you like it or not.

Last week, US pop star Olivia Rodrigo kicked off her Unraveled tour, and surprises from the show, which scores of fans have paid a lot of money to see, have already been dissected online.

Tours by Harry Styles, Charli XCX and Ariana Grande have also been filmed from every angle and shared over the past few months.

While some fans lap up the opportunity to see what's coming, others are taking extreme measures to preserve the element of surprise.

News.title: EV drivers love their cars, but some passengers feel sick - this could be why
News.content:
Lola Baird has just asked her boyfriend to pull over. Forty minutes into a journey and she's feeling "overwhelmed" by nausea - and can't stop herself throwing up on the ground next to his car.

Lola, 24, from north London, had never experienced motion sickness until her boyfriend bought an electric vehicle (EV) two years ago. Ever since, she's been feeling "very nauseous" when he takes her on long car journeys.

It's become so severe she's even asked him to change his car.

Lola isn't alone. Other people told BBC News that they or their children notice feeling more car sick when sitting as a passenger in an electric vehicle. But at the same time, many EV drivers say it's not been a concern.

So what could explain these reports of motion sickness?

Dr Irene Di Giulio, senior lecturer in anatomy and biomechanics at King's College London whose research includes motion sickness, says research so far suggests some people experience more severe motion sickness in electric vehicles than in non-electric vehicles.

It's something Dr Nicholas Hac, a neurologist at Northwestern Medicine in Chicago who specialises in dizziness and vertigo, has also heard from some of his patients. "They just notice that they're much more likely or prone to be motion sick" in electric vehicles, he says.

"I've heard about it many, many, many times," he adds, saying about two patients a month specifically reference feeling motion sick in electric vehicles.

News.title: Traitors claim their first victim as Richard E Grant tries to save his skin
News.content:
Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the second episode of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.

A comedian, a journalist, an actor and a TV presenter walk into a church. But sadly, the punchline for one of them was becoming the first victim of this year's Celebrity Traitors.

As Friday's episode got under way, a delicious new twist saw traitors Richard E Grant and Maya Jama invite James Acaster to join them in the turret, and simultaneously murder a fellow player.

Unfortunately, it fell to Amol Rajan to become the Paloma Faith of this series - being taken away in a coffin in episode two before even having the chance to take part in a banishment.

"It's gutting to be the first out," Rajan said afterwards, noting that perhaps it was because he had been "a bit bullish with Richard" earlier in the day.

"But you know what, games are games, and just as there are winners, so there have to be losers."

The episode drew in a peak audience of 8.6 million viewers, just short of the debut episode with an average of 8.9 million viewers.

The morning following Rajan's banishment, presenter Claudia Winkleman confirmed the University Challenge host's murder to the other players, joking: "That's what I call a starter for 10."

Acaster, meanwhile, reflected: "I'm gutted to not be a faithful anymore, I don't like lying. But if I don't join them, they'll kill me." You can't fault his logic.

The decision meant that Grant, an Oscar-nominated actor with a Razzie-worthy traitor strategy, did at least manage to commit one successful murder despite his shambolic first day.

News.title: Why thousands of couples are choosing Scotland to say 'I do'
News.content:
Hayden Kuhn and Savannah Aanderud had never set foot in Scotland before they decided it was the perfect place to get married last May.

The couple, from Pennsylvania in the US, wanted a destination wedding that would take their family and friends on an adventure with them.

They considered locations across Europe, before deciding on Scotland after Savannah saw photographs of a castle wedding online.

"I think it was on Pinterest," she said. "Somebody got married in a castle and I was like 'Oh, I have to do that'."

The pair are far from alone in seeing Scotland as the ultimate romantic destination.

News.title: Sinfield completes fundraising challenge of seven ultramarathons in a week
News.content:
Sir Kevin Sinfield has completed his latest endurance challenge raising money for motor neurone disease (MND) causes in memory of his friend and teammate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024.

Sinfield completed seven ultramarathons in seven days, crossing the finish line at Old Trafford Stadium in Manchester ahead of the Super League Grand Final.

The fundraiser and his team have raised more than Â£13m for the MND community since his first annual challenge in 2020.

Speaking to the crowd, Sinfield said: "The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob would be so proud to see how you've supported and cared, and showed your love for a community that really needs us."

Sinfield began his final ultramarathon challenge in Hull on September 27 and visited all 12 Super League clubs along the way.

The 7 in 7: The Grand Finale week ended at Old Trafford earlier where he brought out the trophy ahead of the game between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity.

News.title: Homemade bomb part of alleged plot on Manchester's Jewish community, court told
News.content:
Two Iranian men have appeared in court charged with terror offences over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester with a homemade bomb.

Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, were accused at Westminster Magistrates' Court of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism on or before 20 September.

One of the buildings they are alleged to have carried out reconnaissance at is the Heaton Park synagogue which was attacked on 2 October 2025.

Both men, who had arrived in the UK by small boat, were arrested in Manchester's Northern Quarter on the eve of Yom Kippur - the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

Salehi and Ahmadyan were remanded in custody by District Judge Nina Tempia until 23 October, when they will appear at the Old Bailey in London.

As part of the investigation, searches were carried out at addresses in Epworth Street, Liverpool, and Lancaster Road, Salford.

The Metropolitan Police said the men were alleged to have obtained instructions to make a chlorine bomb, acquired liquids and other components to make an improvised explosive device.

They are accused of using the internet to identify and research potential targets, acquiring images, plans and maps.

Prosecutor Mark Luckett told the court: "Both defendants are accused of preparing acts of terrorism targeting the Jewish community in Manchester through the use of a homemade explosive device.

"The defendants were observed carrying out, what the prosecution say, is a hostile reconnaissance within Manchester's Jewish community, identifying attempted targets such as the Jewish Museum and Heaton Park Synagogue."

News.title: Greens would offer two-year jobs to unemployed under-24s
News.content:
Young people would be offered a guaranteed two-year job within four months of leaving education or training, under a new proposal unveiled by the Green Party.

Announcing the policy at the party's conference in Brighton, co-deputy leader Mothin Ali said there were a million "bored, desperate and lost" young people who were out of work, training or education.

Under the proposed scheme, youngsters would be offered posts in the private sector, with the government paying half their salary.

Ali said an initial pilot scheme - rolled out in areas with the fewest job openings for young people - would create 9,000 jobs, at an overall cost of Â£110m.

The pilot would start in areas such as Rotherham, Ceredigion, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Broxtowe and South Staffordshire, with an ambition to roll it out nationwide.

The party said that a person not in work, education or training would cost the state an estimated Â£240,000 in benefits over the course of their lifetime.

It argued that its policy would reduce spending on welfare and boost tax receipts from employment.

Employers would be exempt from paying National Insurance contributions, but would have to provide in-job training, the party says.

The party is seeking to pitch the plan as more ambitious than the government's own scheme, which subsidises six-month job placements for benefit claimants who have been looking for work for 18 months.

Ali also criticised ministers for previously suggesting youngsters refusing a role under that scheme could lose access to benefits, telling activists: "Threatening young people with cuts to Universal Credit if they don't accept short-term work placements - that's not a youth strategy."

Speaking to BBC News after his speech, Ali said: "If we don't take action now, we're losing a generation of young people."

The number of 16-24-year-olds who are not in employment, education or training has been rising since the Covid pandemic, with figures reaching almost one million.

A long-awaited report into the problem by former Labour minister Alan Milburn is expected to be published this autumn.

News.title: Huge crowds turn out in support of residents over Drumcree parade dispute
News.content:
Rallies were held on both sides of the Drumcree parade dispute on Saturday as the stand-off between Garvaghy Road residents and the Portadown District Orange Lodge continues.

Addressing thousands of people at an event on the Garvaghy Road, First Minister and Sinn FÃ©in vice president Michelle O'Neill said she heard the Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant "talk about being between a rock and a hard place", adding she has "never heard such nonsense, this is between right and wrong".

The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) said anyone blocking the Garvaghy Road will be "treated as participating in an unnotified and therefore illegal protest and that anyone "found to have broken the law will face criminal justice consequences".

Speaking at Drumcree church, Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) MP Carla Lockhart repeated calls for PSNI Chief Constable Jon Boutcher and his officers to "do their job" and facilitate the parade, describing the current impasse as "mob rule".

For most of the afternoon stewards in high visibility jackets kept people off the Garvaghy Road and those attending were told it was important to allow traffic to flow freely.

However, by 15:00 BST the crowd was so large that they were standing on the road as police closed it to traffic.

The fallout over the proposed Portadown District Orange Lodge march - which is opposed by residents of the Garvaghy Road - has lasted since Sunday morning after the Parades Commission's decision that the parade could go ahead with restrictions.

News.title: Police appeal to help find heavily pregnant woman
News.content:
Police have appealed for help in their search for a missing woman who is heavily pregnant.

Leicestershire Police said Charlie Ryan was reported missing on Friday morning, having last been seen in the Groby Road area of Leicester near to New Parks Way roundabout.

The force said the 31-year-old is white, 165cm (5ft 5in), with bright blonde hair. She was last seen wearing a black jacket, grey jumper, black leggings and black shoes.

Officers said they were "extremely concerned" for her welfare and active inquiries were continuing to find her.

Police said inquiries carried out so far indicated she may be in the Northfields area of Leicester.

Anyone who may have seen her or knows where she may be is asked to contact police.

News.title: Watch the moment a landslip leaves Skye drivers facing a 40-mile diversion
News.content:
Drivers on Skye are facing a 40-mile diversion after a landslide led to a road closure.

The ground fell away from the side of the A855 north of Uig onto a local access road on Friday afternoon and an inspection later confirmed it would have to stay shut over the weekend.

The A855 road encircles the Trotternish peninsula in the north of the island and a diversion route is now in place.

No-one was injured by the landslip - which was caught on CCTV from a nearby house - but a group of visiting schoolchildren found themselves temporarily separated from their packed lunches until a local woman volunteered to retrieve them by bike.

The road could have to remain closed into next week as "detailed surveying" works continue, according to local councillor Chrissie Gillies.

News.title: Alison Hammond returns home from hospital after rushing off This Morning
News.content:
"It felt very real to me. I'm really new to panic attacks, so I need to learn more about it," she added.

The Birmingham-born presenter, who also co-hosts The Great British Bake Off, thanked NHS staff and her colleagues at This Morning, including O'Leary.

"It's really warmed my heart actually. I didn't necessarily want to be on the news or anything like that but this is a new world to me," she said.

"I'm going to take stock, take some rest and I'll see you soon."

Friday's edition of the ITV show began at 10:00 BST with Hammond and her regular co-host O'Leary at the helm, before she left at 11:30 during a segment about pets.

O'Leary, 53, addressed her absence when the show returned from a break, saying: "Welcome back to This Morning, Alison is feeling a little unwell, so she's just had to duck out. Hopefully she'll be back."

He later updated viewers that she would, in fact, not be returning, "so I'll be here for the rest of the show".

Hammond rose to fame as contestant on Channel 4 reality show Big Brother before appearing on I'm A Celebrity and Strictly Come Dancing.

She became a co-host in This Morning in 2021, and was part of the team that won a National Television Award for best daytime programme the following year.

She joined Bake Off in 2023 and took over from the late Paul O'Grady on For the Love of Dogs in 2024.

News.title: Tories pledge to build 50,000 new prison places
News.content:
The Conservatives have promised to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales to stop criminals being released early, if they return to government.

The party said it would cost Â£2bn per year to build and run the new prisons, funded by spending cuts including to the foreign aid budget.

On Thursday hundreds of prisoners were released early, under new rules introduced to prevent jails reaching capacity, with around 4,500 due to be freed by next summer.

Labour blamed the previous Tory government for leaving "our criminal justice system at breaking point" and said the party's proposals were not "credible".

The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham, which begins on Sunday.

Prisons in England and Wales have been running close to capacity for years, with the latest government figures showing they are 98% full.

Under the latest early release scheme, eligible prisoners can now be released on a community licence after serving one-third of their jail sentence.

Those excluded include prisoners convicted of murder, manslaughter, a sexual or grooming-related offence, or a driving offence that led to a death.

The government has also effectively scrapped one-year jail terms.

The Tories said they would use extra prison capacity to reverse these measures.

An early release programme introduced by the previous Conservative government saw more than 10,000 prisoners freed early between October 2023 and September 2024.

News.title: Youth charged after shopping centre attack leaves teenager in hospital
News.content:
A teenager has been charged after an attack involving a groups of youths inside a Glasgow shopping centre left another teenager needing hospital treatment.

Video posted on social media shows a young man, who was using a crutch and wearing a medical boot, being knocked to the ground, then repeatedly punched and kicked inside the St Enoch Centre on Friday afternoon.

A second person was also pushed to the ground during the disturbance but security staff intervened.

Police Scotland said a 19-year-old was taken to hospital and a 17-year-old boy was later arrested and charged following investigations.

The attackers had run off by the time officers arrived and the injured man, who was bleeding from a head wound, was initially helped by shoppers and security staff.

Daryl Powell hailed Wakefield’s Grand Final “fairy tale” after a stunning first-half performance saw them sink Warrington 23-10 and claim their first league title since 1968.

Three years after taking charge of the club following their plunge into the sport’s second tier, Powell saw his side out-muscle their opponents in front of a sold-out Old Trafford.

Powell, who fell short with Castleford in the 2017 showpiece, had been tempted to give it one more shot after buying into the five-year vision of Trinity’s new millionaire owner Matt Ellis.

Powell said: “It was a big performance from an unbelievable group of blokes. We’ve had a fairy-tale ending to the season and I wasn’t sure we could do it this year.

“You can’t write this stuff really. We’ve been building for a while, but the last two weeks in particular have been incredible performances from an unbelievable group of players.”

Victory for Powell capped a remarkable personal journey after the 2017 near-miss was followed by a torrid time in charge of Warrington before he resurrected his career in the unlikeliest of circumstances.

“I’ve had some great times in my coaching career, but this is the best,” added Powell. “After 2017 it looked like maybe I’d slip through my career and not win the big game.

“I had a tough time at Warrington and to come back and to do this with Wakefield is phenomenal. For me it’s right up there, being at Wakefield and feeling at home in a place again and coming together to do special things.”

Three converted tries and a Jack Sinfield drop goal sent Trinity to the brink of victory at the break and, despite a rocky period after Corey Hall’s yellow card, there were few signs that Wire were capable of mounting a comeback.

open image in gallery Daryl Powell (centre), Tom Johnstone (left) and Mike McMeeken celebrate with the trophy (Mike Egerton/PA). ( PA Wire )

In contrast to Trinity’s wild celebrations at the final hooter, there was dejection in the Warrington camp as they come to terms with a fifth Grand Final loss – and a wait for a league title of their own that will now stretch beyond 71 years.

Warrington head coach Sam Burgess admitted his side lost the physical battle and left themselves with too much to do, despite a brace of second half tries from Arron Lindop.

Burgess said: “I must pay huge congratulations to Wakefield because they physically just won the ruck and that was the difference between the two teams. We were just surviving.

“I’m not surprised with the spirit we showed in the second half because they’ve showed that all year. It’s about trying to regroup and make sure things don’t fracture. We stuck together and we tried and we just got beaten by a better side.

“It’s not the result we were after. The further you go, the deeper the wound. There are a lot of disappointed men down there, but my overall feeling is proud of the team, proud of the club and proud of the group.

“It’s a little bit hard to see that right now, but I guess in a day or two we might be able to reflect and be a bit more positive, but right now it hurts a little bit.”

The Los Angeles Dodgers are hosting the Atlanta Braves in what is forecast to be the hottest postseason game at Dodger Stadium since 2017.

Shade was at a premium on Saturday for Game 1 of the National League Division Series, which began at 1 p.m. local time. The game-time temperature of 100 degrees was forecast to reach 101 degrees Fahrenheit (38 degrees Celsius), about 20 degrees warmer than the average for early October.

The highest game-time temperature ever recorded at Dodger Stadium is 103 degrees (39 degrees Celsius) twice. The first time was Oct. 24, 2017, for Game 1 of the World Series against Houston. It was equaled on Sept. 8, 2024, for a regular-season game against Cleveland.

The Braves seemingly were unfazed by the blazing sun, cloudless skies and rising thermometer while taking pre-game batting practice. The two-time defending World Series champion Dodgers? They stayed inside.

“Remember, we're from Atlanta,” Braves manager Walt Weiss said before the game. “It's not that big of a factor.”

Braves center fielder Lane Thomas added, "I feel like this is a little cooler 98 than Atlanta.”

Some of their fans agreed.

“It's hot, but it's not bad,” said Helen Greene of Valdosta, Georgia, who was sitting in the sun nine rows behind the visiting dugout with her long hair arrayed under a Braves cap. “In Atlanta, my hair would have been up by now.”

Greene and her husband, Chad, were hydrating with water.

“I'll have beer later,” she said, smiling.

Tickets for Game 1 were still available early Saturday. The lowest get-in price ranged from $56 to $61, depending on the secondary marketplace.

Fans still gathered in the outfield pavilions in hopes of catching a stray ball off the Braves' bats pre-game. But other seating areas were mostly empty 90 minutes before first pitch.

Christopher Hernández of Long Beach and his girlfriend sat in the sun behind the Dodgers dugout with giveaway towels covering their heads.

“We play sports and we know how it feels to be in the heat and we know how to beat the heat, too,” he said, showing off a blue plastic bottle with a fan attached to spritz water. “It's not as bad as people think it is.”

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts planned to keep an eye on his pitchers and catcher Will Smith, who wears a mask and padding behind the plate.

“It’s the same conditions for both teams,” the manager said, “and you’ve got to just stay hydrated and manage it.”

Braves reliever Brent Suter graduated from Harvard in 2012, having majored in environmental science and public policy.

“In the back of my mind, I’m like 100 degrees in October in L.A., that’s definitely not normal,” he said before the game. “Obviously super El Niño is a big thing to do with that. It’s going to be a challenge for both sides to stay hydrated, especially the position players.”

Short heat spells in October are normal for Los Angeles, but the prolonged extreme heat warning — forecast to last at least a week — is keeping temperatures 10 to 15 degrees above normal. The average high in Los Angeles in early October is 81 degrees (27 degrees Celsius).

“Just making sure everyone is hydrated and staying loose and getting electrolytes in us,” Suter said.

Emergency medical teams were in their usual spots around the stadium, staying alert for anticipated cases of heatstroke, dehydration, excessive sweating caused by heat exposure, and the more typical drunkenness.

The Dodgers encouraged fans to wear hats and sunscreen. They were allowed to bring in non-alcoholic drinks of one liter or less in factory-sealed plastic bottles. Empty refillable water bottles were also allowed. Bottle filling stations and water fountains are scattered around the stadium.

President Donald Trump’s new assistant press secretary — a former reporter for Real America's Voice — once posed for a photo with a rifle while wearing a "f*** Joe Biden" T-shirt and was a fan of slain conservative influencer Charlie Kirk.

Beni Rae Harmony, 24, announced on Friday that she will join Trump's White House press team as the new assistant press secretary. Anti-MAGA accounts on Instagram quickly found the photo of Harmony in her anti-Biden shirt, according to The Daily Beast.

The photo was posted by former Republican Virginia congressional candidate Jarome Bell in 2021. The post includes the caption "My campaign Public Affairs Director @beniraeharmony is a beast. This is how we roll."

Harmony's Instagram account liked the post. Bell ran for Congress in 2022 in Virginia Beach.

Harmony will join the White House's communications team following a staff shakeup that included the departure of former Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt in August.

Beni Rae Harmony, 24, will join the White House communications team as assistant press secretary. A photo of her from 2021 was discovered in which she is wearing a shirt with the slogan 'F*** Joe Biden' on the front ( Instagram )

"It's been an honor to report, travel, and cover this historic administration as Senior White House Correspondent for Real America's Voice. My goal has always been to ask questions that matter to real Americans and make sure their voices are heard," Harmony wrote in a post announcing her hiring. "I'm incredibly grateful to President Trump for this opportunity and his trust."

Harmony formerly worked for the far-right broadcaster Real America's Voice, which always airs Steve Bannon's weekday show, The Charlie Kirk Show, and Ted Nugent's Spirit Campfire.

She said she joined the broadcaster after she was suspended from her previous place of employment, WICS-ABC20 in Springfield, Illinois, allegedly for sharing an unprompted on-air tribute to Kirk following his 2025 assassination.

Harmony defended her decision to air the memorial, calling it "non-partisan."

She previously worked at Kirk's Turning Point USA conservative youth organization in 2020 and 2021. Harmony said she considered Kirk a "mentor."

Her LinkedIn profile says she also interned for Arizona Republican Congressman Paul Gosar and former Florida Congressman Matt Gaetz.

Harmony may have caught Trump's eye during a trip to Ireland last month, where she was present as a reporter on Air Force One.

Anna Kelly, the White House principal deputy press secretary, confirmed Harmony's new role in a statement.

“Beni Rae Harmony has been a trusted voice for the MAGA movement as a White House correspondent,” Kelly said. “She will be an outstanding addition to President Trump’s communications team as an assistant press secretary. We look forward to having her on board.”

Georgia, Notre Dame and Alabama remained unbeaten — and mostly untested.

Gunner Stockton threw for 295 yards and three touchdowns, and the second-ranked Bulldogs pulled away late to beat Vanderbilt 38-14 on Saturday. The Bulldogs led 21-14 at halftime but got a lucky — Luckie, really — bounce in the third quarter to help create some cushion.

Tight end Lawson Luckie grabbed a tipped pass from Stockton that was nearly intercepted and turned it into a 43-yard reception that set up a touchdown. Georgia also benefitted from a blocked field goal and a fourth-down stop that came courtesy of an overturned reception.

Meanwhile in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, CJ Carr threw four TD passes, Jonaz Walton ran for 108 yards and the third-ranked Fighting Irish handled the Tar Heels 37-26. It was Notre Dame's 15th consecutive victory — all of them by at least 10 points.

The seventh-ranked Crimson Tide were supposedly on upset alert in Starkville, Mississippi. But Alabama rolled over Kamario Taylor and No. 16 Mississippi State 56-23, sending a clear statement about the team to beat in the Southeastern Conference.

Keelon Russell threw for 285 yards and three touchdowns, Trae'shawn Brown ran for two scores and the Tide scored at least 45 points for the fifth consecutive game to start the season. It's one short of the team record set in 2018. Alabama plays at Georgia next Saturday.

The Alabama-Mississippi State matchup was expected to be a showcase for Taylor, who had been so impressive through four games. But he threw two interceptions, was sacked five times and headed to the locker room with 12 minutes to play with an injury.

No. 4 Miami (at Clemson), No. 5 Ohio State (at Iowa), No. 6 Indiana (at Rutgers) and No. 8 Florida (at Missouri) all were facing road tests later Saturday.

The best of the rest

In the Big 12 Conference, Cincinnati will try to improve to 5-0 for the first time since 2021 with a visit to Arizona, where Noah Fifita already has thrown for 11 touchdowns to increase his career total to 84, most among active FBS quarterbacks.

Since a 28-17 loss at BYU, the Wildcats have come back from early deficits of 10-0 to Northern Illinois and 14-0 at Washington State to win both games by double digits.

Illinois health officials shut down an unlicensed, home-based caterer after a high school football team dinner sickened at least 45 people and forced the school to postpone its homecoming game.

The Rock Island High School football team’s Sept. 24 dinner was held around 5:30 p.m. in the school cafeteria, where about 75 players, coaches and parents were served a taco bar catered by Sunshine and Spice. The Moline-based home operation is about 10 minutes from Rock Island, local health officials confirmed to KWQC.

The menu included fajita chicken, seasoned taco beef, cheese, flour taco shells, cheesy pepper beans, cilantro corn rice and pico de gallo or salsa.

By about 11 p.m., 23 players, five coaches and three parents were experiencing vomiting and diarrhea, football team trainer Kyle Hoffmann reported to Rock Island City Health Inspector Andy Swartz the following afternoon, the news outlet reports.

At least 45 people total eventually reported illness. None required hospitalization, though one player saw a doctor. Most recovered within 24 hours.

open image in gallery Sunshine and Spice, an unlicensed, Illinois home-based caterer, sickened at least 45 people, including 23 Rock Island High School football players, after catering the team’s dinner ahead of its homecoming game ( Google Maps )

The high school postponed its homecoming game until all affected players had been symptom-free for at least 24 hours, as advised by the Rock Island County Health Department and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, per KWQC.

During the investigation, Swartz met with Sunshine and Spice owner Joshua Harris and found that the home-based catering operation was not licensed or food-safety certified. Swartz ordered the business to stop operating immediately and gave Harris information on how to obtain the required licenses, according to the news outlet.

Harris told Swartz that the meal’s ingredients were purchased from Walmart in Moline, Spotted Apron in Geneseo and farmers markets in Davenport and Coal Valley.

Harris said in a statement to KWQC that Sunshine and Spice was sorry for what happened and denied intentionally providing unsafe food.

“First, Sunshine and Spice wants to sincerely apologize and send even more prayers to anyone affected by last week's Rock Island Football Team Meal. We provided a taco bar-style potluck before the team was dismissed to prepare for their Homecoming Game,” Harris said.

He further explained how he prepared the food.

“All of the food purchased from Walmart on Wednesday Night was fully cooked (beef, chicken, rice). We put all of the leftovers in plastic bags provided by the team parents for anyone to take home. We have cooked for numerous parents of the team/school in the past and have no reason EVER to provide a sub-standard meal or purposely attempt any tampering shenanigans.”

Harris continued, “We are saddened by this whole situation. We have been working side by side with the Rock Island County Health Department and Rock Island City/County Law Enforcement Agencies to be a part of their continuing investigations. Again, we want to extend our deepest apologies and continued prayers to those affected.”

Health officials said the investigation remains ongoing and that leftover food from the dinner was seized for testing.

Swartz worked with county health officials and the Illinois Department of Public Health to survey people who became sick. According to the results, obtained by KWQC, the most commonly consumed items were cilantro corn rice, fajita chicken, cheese and flour taco shells:

92 percent consumed cilantro corn rice

88 percent consumed fajita chicken

88 percent consumed cheese

88 percent consumed flour taco shells

83 percent consumed seasoned taco beef

58 percent consumed cheesy pepper beans

58 percent consumed pico/salsa

Rock Island lost their Friday game to East Moline United Football, making their 2026 record 0-7.
