Chad Lowe’s eldest daughter, Mabel, has spoken out about the death of her sister, Fiona.

On Tuesday, Pretty Little Liars actor Lowe and his wife, producer Kim Painter, announced the death of their daughter, Fiona, at age 13.

Her older sister, 17-year-old Mabel, said in a moving Instagram post Saturday: “I love you so much fiona. I wish your short time here was easier, and I hope your mind is at ease now.”

“I will honor you forever and keep your memory alive,” she continued. “I love you; I hope you knew just how much.”

Mabel shared several photos of her childhood with Fiona, including a photo of her sister dancing, and one of them playing at the beach.

Chad Lowe and his wife, Kim Painter, with their daughters, Nixie, Fiona Lowe, and Mabel, in 2023 ( Getty )

American actor Melissa Gilbert commented on the post: “Beautiful, heartfelt tribute, sweet girl. Sending so much love.”

Lowe’s former co-star David Boreanaz said: “Lovely. Two peas in a pod forever.”

In a statement shared with multiple outlets Tuesday, the Lowe family said, “We are deeply heartbroken by the loss of our beloved Fiona. She was a loving young girl who was smart, creative and loved to dance.

“She was adored by her sisters, and she was deeply loved by her parents,” the family said, adding, “In fact, she was the light of our lives.”

“Her passing is devastating for our entire family, and we ask for prayers and privacy at this time. If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, please reach out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988.”

Lowe is best known for his Emmy-winning role in the ABC comedy-drama Life Goes On and for playing English literature professor Byron Montgomery in Pretty Little Liars. He is also the brother of Parks and Recreation star Rob Lowe.

Lowe celebrated Fiona’s birthday on Instagram last year, sharing a picture of his daughter alongside the caption: “Celebrating Fiona officially becoming a teen today!! Keep dancing through life FiBear! Love you soooo much!!”

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week. If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you

Thousands of supporters of Serbia's populist leader, Aleksandar Vucic, packed the largest indoor arena in Belgrade on Saturday for the de facto launch of his campaign for prime minister that will culminate in a pivotal election set for Oct. 25.

The early election, which polls suggest could be tight between Vucic's party and a group of candidates fielded by a student-led protest movement, was called after Vucic resigned as president on Sept. 27, cutting short his second term by more than seven months.

Vucic, who is constitutionally prohibited from running for a third term as president, declared upon resigning that he would lead his populist Serbian Progressive Party in the parliamentary election. If his party wins a majority of seats, the parliament is expected to elect Vucic as prime minister.

Dozens of buses from across Serbia clogged streets around Belgrade Arena on Saturday as supporters arrived at the rally in the capital carrying Serbian flags and banners bearing Vucic’s picture.

The event, televised by dozens of channels across Serbia, capped a week of Vucic touring towns and villages in an apparent bid to shore up his popularity that's been shaken after almost two years of sustained anti-government protests.

The youth-backed movement that led the protests has demanded accountability for the Nov. 1, 2024 train station canopy collapse that killed 16 people in the northern city of Novi Sad.

The movement's struggle for justice over the tragedy and against corruption has grown into a nationwide political force whose electoral arm, the Student List, will attempt to oust Vucic’s government after 14 years in power.

Vucic himself has been either prime minister or president for the past 12 years.

The Student List includes university professors, teachers, experts and others from across the political spectrum. Yet Vucic has accused those behind the movement of seeking to “bring Serbia to a halt,” and claimed, without providing evidence, that it's backed by unspecified foreign agents.

On Saturday, Vucic told his supporters: “Absent an intervention of some (foreign intelligence) service, we will defeat them. And they know that.”

The election is taking place amid heightened political tensions in Serbia, with reports of incidents and physical altercations at campaign events. International observers have described previous elections in Serbia as marred by multiple irregularities and violence.

While formally a candidate for European Union membership, Serbia’s accession process has stalled under Vucic, who maintains close ties with Russia and China.

European institutions have warned of democratic backsliding in Serbia in successive reports tracking the progress of candidate countries. Rights and media freedom groups have separately warned of police violence, arbitrary detentions, unauthorized surveillance and threats against journalists.

News.title: Rees-Zammit taunts Pollock as Bristol outplay Northampton
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Bristol Bears vs Northampton Saints from the Gallagher Prem, with both teams looking to build on winning starts following the opening weekend of action.

Last season’s champions Northampton kicked off their title defence with an emphatic 59-26 victory over a new-look Newcastle Red Bulls outfit at Franklin’s Gardens.

While Henry Pollock’s new cornrow hairstyle was the centre of attention at kick-off, the limelight was soon stolen by Tommy Freeman and James Pater, who both notched hat-tricks for Phil Dowson’s side.

Of 19-year-old full-back Pater, who starts on the bench today, Dowson said afterwards: “He doesn’t let the occasion get to him. He has an incredible skill set, great speed and ability to manoeuvre away from defenders.”

Bristol, meanwhile, began their season with an impressive 34-24 victory away at Sale Sharks, with Pat Lam’s side ensuring Courtney Lawes’s return to the English game was a disappointing one.

Louis Rees-Zammit was operating in his favoured wing position and got Bristol off to a strong start with two tries in the opening 23 minutes, offering Lam hope of a fruitful campaign from the Welshman.

“When you look at our wingers in the past, they scored a lot of tries and Louis is a world-class finisher,” the Bristol director of rugby said. “You get the ball to him in space and you create the opportunity, there’s a good chance he’ll finish it.”

Northampton will be hoping for a repeat of the meeting between the sides at Franklin Gardens in May when they thumped Bristol 94-33, but they have not won at Ashton Gate since 2021.

Both teams have made a pair of changes following their opening-weekend victories, with England international Ellis Genge among the players to drop out after spraining his wrist against Sale.

News.title: Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade
News.content:
We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. With last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we sill did not know.

But here that standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of playing. The potential was unleashed. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the movement of the ball, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the ruthlessness, the control, the power and aggression. This was, unquestionably, the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

It was men against boys. Croatia have an ageing team and are in a transition but they were left looking callow. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture, with Croatia punished for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

News.title: Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying
News.content:
The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

News.title: Bath complete revenge mission on Exeter despite imperious Feyi-Waboso
News.content:
Bath held off a furious comeback from Exeter, led by the irrepressible Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, to avenge their Gallagher Prem semi-final defeat here in June.

It felt as if lightning might strike Bath twice. Once again Exeter overturned a 26-10 half-time deficit, to manufacture a second-half lead thanks to a pair of blistering finishes by Feyi-Waboso. Four months ago, Bath failed to take a drop goal in the closing stages, but this time with the reassuring presence of Finn Russell at fly-half, they kept their cool.

The Scotland playmaker twice sent penalties deep into the Exeter 22 from where Stephen Varney conceded a yellow card and penalty try before Bath replacement Ted Hill powered through a thicket of Exeter tacklers.

“Finn is one of the best 10s in the world and I thought he had a very good game,” Johann van Graan, the Bath head of rugby, said. “His decision making is above most players in the world and I thought that came through tonight.”

Despite the appearance of yet another high-scoring shoot-out, both teams defended with real bite, although Bath struggled to lay a finger on Feyi-Waboso who ended up in a scrap with a fan in the stands here when he was a spectator in May. He exacted a measure of revenge beating eight defenders and carried for 132 metres.

“Manny still needs game time,” Rob Baxter, the Exeter director of rugby, said. “When he’s on the ball, you see something incredible, but it is his ability to get on the ball again. He is just getting his game minutes and match fitness up.”

News.title: FTSE 100 tumbles amid bond market sell-off
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. House prices fell unexpectedly last month as mortgage borrowers prepare for a jump in interest rates.

Typical property values declined by 0.2pc during September, reversing 0.2pc growth in August, according to the Nationwide house price index.

The figure was much worse than analysts had forecasts, with most expecting prices to remain steady.

Over the course of the year to September, the rate of house price growth halved from 1.6pc to 0.8pc, which was the weakest rate since December 2025.

The value of the average home has fallen to £274,251 over concerns the Bank of England is on the cusp of raising interest rates, making borrowing more expensive for mortgage holders.

Money markets indicate there is an 84pc chance policymakers will raise rates from 3.75pc to 4pc in November in an effort to bring down inflation caused by the Iran war energy shock.

Robert Gardner, chief economist at Nationwide, said:“Market activity and house prices have remained subdued in recent months, in part reflecting the uncertain economic backdrop.

“Geopolitical tensions remain high, with the conflict in the Middle East exerting upward pressure on energy prices, fanning inflation concerns.

“This in turn has led to mounting financial market expectations of Bank Rate increases, which has maintained upward pressure on the market interest rates which underpin mortgage pricing.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Polanski urges Miliband to block Rosebank oil field over Israel links | Green leader claims North Sea project is a test of Foreign Secretary’s proposed sanctions regime

2) Netherlands ditches wealth tax over exodus fears | Dutch PM scraps plan to target paper profits, instead introducing a more convention capital gains levy

3) Diesel crisis deepens as UK’s biggest refinery shuts for 10 weeks | Fears of squeeze on supplies after fuel costs rise higher than £2 per litre

4) Debt-ridden France branded ‘the new sick man of Europe’ | Investors hope the European Central Bank sees the struggling country as ‘too big to fail’

5) Britain blocks foreign lawyers after surge in south Asian applicants | Bar Standards Board halts scheme unless candidates have already secured a position

What happened overnight

The cost of government borrowing edged higher in Asia as soaring energy costs sparked inflation fears.

Bond yields, a benchmark for what governments pay to borrow money, surged in September as investors brace for a period where interest rates stay higher for ​longer.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes hit 5.31pc, the ‌highest level since mid-June 2007. The 10-year yield gained 87 basis points in the July-September quarter, the biggest quarterly rise since 1994.

Market focus has been on how long US Treasury yields stay above the psychologically important 5pc level, while some investors even contemplate the possibility of yields breaching 6pc.

Yields in Japan have climbed to multi-decade highs too, while those in Germany, France and Britain have all hit 17 to 19 year peaks.

On Thursday, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government ​bond yield was at 3.11pc, not far from the 30-year high it hit last week.

Asian technology stocks rose after a boost from AI chipmaker Micron, ​although US bonds struggled ‌after their sharpest quarterly sell-off in more than three decades as inflation risks from elevated energy prices linger.

Stalling peace talks between the US and Iran to end the seven-month-long war in the Middle East have kept crude prices aloft.Brent futures surged 42pc in the July-September quarter.

The high-stakes earnings from Micron, a key supplier to AI bellwether Nvidia, signalled strong demand for AI memory chips, with financial commitments under long-term supply agreements at $32 billion, up from $22 billion in June.

That helped push tech-heavy stock markets in Asia higher. Japan’s Nikkei jumped over 3pc, and South Korea’s Kospi reversed earlier losses to gain 1.7pc. Taiwan’s stock benchmark was 0.8pc higher.

News.title: Chewing tobacco killed 250,000 people in one year, study shows
News.content:
Chewing tobacco killed around a quarter of a million people in 2023, with use of the product remaining stubbornly high, according to research.

The smokeless tobacco, which is placed between the cheek and lower gum, is particularly popular in south Asia. It is flavoured and sometimes sweetened, and users often spit out unwanted juices while chewing. It is often viewed as safer than smoking but it is a major cause of stroke, as well as head and neck cancer.

Chewing tobacco is different to white snus or nicotine pouches, which contain no tobacco. These white pouches are also made up of flavourings and sometimes sweeteners, and deliver a hit of nicotine through the lining of the mouth.

Despite a successful fight against smoking over the last few decades, rates of chewing tobacco use have fallen little and it has often been overlooked in tobacco control efforts, researchers point out. In a study published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in the US estimate that 241 million people aged 15 years and older used chewing tobacco in 2023.

Researchers looked at data on use in 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 and found that there was no significant decrease in the number of users of chewing tobacco over that period. And in 24 countries there was a significant uptick in the number of people using the product. Researchers estimate that about one in five men and one in 10 women in south Asia chewed tobacco in 2023.

Bangladesh has seen the biggest increase in the number of people using the product with 15 million new users between 1990 and 2023. Nepal, Madagascar and Yemen also saw increases in the number of users.

In India 105 million people chew tobacco regularly, accounting for just over two thirds of users globally. Historically, Indians would chew paan, tobacco in its raw form which was mixed with betel leaf and areca nut, a mild stimulant. But the use of chewing tobacco exploded in the 1980s when manufacturers began grinding these into a powder and selling them in packets known as gutkha. This was banned in 2012 but is still widely available. Chewing tobacco is also popular in Pakistan, China and Vietnam.

News.title: Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
News.content:
Dame Esther was a vocal supporter of the Assisted Dying Bill, claiming in March that most people “want and need” the right to end their own lives.

When the bill was defeated in the House of Commons in September, as MPs voted 286 to 270 against the legislation, she called it a “tragic day”. The bill would have allowed those with less than six months to live to seek medical assistance to end their lives.

In 2024, she said that she had joined the Dignitas assisted-dying clinic in Switzerland.

Writing for The Telegraph at the beginning of September, Rebecca Wilcox, Dame Esther’s daughter, said her mother was “too ill now to travel to Dignitas as she had planned and paid for”.

Earlier this month, Dame Esther said in a statement that it was too late for her to “buzz off” to the clinic in Switzerland and said Britain’s current laws on assisted dying are “messy and cruel”.

In a final message shared by her family, the presenter said she had been “immensely lucky” for the support she had received from the public, which she said had enabled her “to live such a long and happy life”.

She added: “Sadly, all good things come to an end, as they say. So I particularly wanted to say goodbye and thank you so very, very much. Perhaps I will see you eventually, on the other side. I do hope so. With very good wishes, as ever, Esther.”

News.title: Eight tips to improve your laptop’s performance (and save your sanity)
News.content:
MacBooks and Windows laptops both have modes intended to maximise battery life. Low Power Mode (Mac) and Power Saver (Windows) should be avoided if you want peak performance.

On a Mac, you’ll find the Low Power Mode switch in Settings > Battery. For the best experience, set this to Never, but remember to change it back if you need your MacBook to last longer.

On a Windows laptop, there are two controls you need to consider. Both are found in Settings > System > Power & Battery.

Energy Saver mode uses multiple tactics to reduce battery consumption, including lowering maximum power. Switch this off, and you have access to Power Mode controls.

Your options are Best Power Efficiency, Balanced and Best Performance. While Balanced is the default, I was able to unlock up to 33 per cent more power by playing around with these settings using my own laptop.

To make matters more complicated, some laptops have their own performance modes. Many Asus laptops have MyAsus or Armory Crate, for example. Lenovo has the Vantage app, Dell has MyDell, and MSI laptops have MSI Center.

3. Stop applications from opening on start-up

If your laptop is slow when it first starts up, it may be because a whole bunch of apps have been given the green light to wake up with it.

Some applications such as antivirus software are critical, but most can be toggled off. As an example, I make sure apps such as Spotify, Steam and WhatsApp don’t open on startup; I only launch them when I need them.

On a MacBook, you can see which apps have this permission in Settings > General, under Open at Login. Select an app entry and click the “minus” button to remove it.

On a Windows laptop, you’ll find the list of start-up apps in Settings > Apps > Startup. Each entry has a little on/off slider.

Sports.title: Tax chiefs ‘gathering data’ for probe into Man City after £900m rules breach, ex-chairman of Premier League rival claims
Sports.content:
Next

TAX officials are circling Manchester City in the fallout from its £900million financial rules breach, the ex-chairman of another Premier League club claims.

HMRC’s risk and intelligence service is said to have begun gathering data that might be used in a full investigation into the crisis-hit club’s finances.



The officials, who have powers to examine tax avoidance, evasion and fraud, will look at whether City owes outstanding tax and VAT, according to the source.

The ex-chairman said: “HMRC have been taking a close interest in football for years. They have noted the issues at City and are getting their ducks in a row for a possible escalation against the club.



“They have been carrying out an ‘intelligence project’ where they gather evidence.

“Frankly, it would be negligent if HMRC weren’t looking at the club.”

City was found guilty by an independent commission of breaching football financing rules by hiding £900million in sham deals over nine years.

The club denies wrongdoing and has appealed but HMRC is said to be ready to swoop, potentially hitting the club with monster penalties and fines.

The source says officials are focusing on areas including overseas payments and loopholes in image rights payments, as well as payments to players, agents and managers, such as former team boss Roberto Mancini.

The ex-Premier league chairman claimed: “HMRC will have already mapped out what was declared by Mancini and other staff in their tax returns, as they look to identify potential tax fraud or evasion.”



Tax expert Dan Neidle, who worked for law firm Clifford Chance, has also estimated the club is likely to have failed to pay about £12million in tax because of its payments to former manager Mancini.

He estimated City faced a penalty of up to £24million for off-the-book payments to its ex-boss.

His report said: “There appears to be good grounds for a criminal investigation.”

HMRC declined to comment. City was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Andy Carroll bravely confirms sex abuser was BBC Fame Academy star who brazenly tried to blame football ace for attack
Sports.content:
CARROLL ABUSER NAMED Andy Carroll bravely confirms sex abuser was BBC Fame Academy star who brazenly tried to blame football ace for attack







Next

FOOTBALL’S Andy Carroll has confirmed he was sexually assaulted by a star of BBC show Fame Academy.

Dance coach Kevin Adams was convicted at Chelmsford crown court in 2023 and jailed.



Carroll spoke out after being made aware that Adams’ name was in publicly available court documents. He said: “Now that Kevin Adams has been named in court documents as my abuser, I can confirm it.”

Carroll’s sex attacker brazenly tried to play the victim before he was jailed by a judge.



Dance instructor Adams assaulted the England ace, 37, as he slept naked.

Carroll woke and threw him out, knocking him unconscious when he tried to return.

Yet Adams then told police he had been hit for no reason.

The judge told him later: “You spun a literally incredible tale in which you painted yourself as the victim. You’ve actually started to believe your own lies.”

Ex-Liverpool star Carroll bravely writes of the devastating 2019 attack in autobiography Owning It without naming his abuser.

Today the striker confirms it is Adams, who appeared as a coach on BBC1’s Fame Academy in 2002, and featured on Strictly It Takes Two in 2021.



In November 2023 Adams, now 59, was jailed for 20 months for the assault

Carroll spoke out after being made aware Adams’ name was in publicly-available court documents.

He told The Sun on Sunday: “Now that Kevin Adams has been named in court documents as my abuser, I can confirm it.



“Hopefully now I can finally start to put this chapter behind me.

“I just ask that people don’t constantly share pictures of my abuser alongside me.

“I don’t want to keep seeing his face or being reminded of him every time this story is spoken about. I’m ready to move forward. This had a devastating impact on my life and loved ones.”

In his book, Carroll revealed how he had to give evidence in court, which he found “humiliating and horrendous”.

Before the case, his abuser ran the Kevin Adams Academy, a children’s dance school, in Harlow, Essex, which appears to have ceased operating in 2022.



In September 2023 he was found guilty of sexual assault at Chelmsford crown court.

After sentencing that November, Adams was put on the Sex Offender Register for ten years and banned from Carroll’s village.

Judge Mary Loram told Adams: “You spun a literally incredible tale in which you painted yourself as the victim.



“In your narrative, you were the put-upon reluctant friend doing no more than helping out.

“The end of your unbelievable tale was that you were the victim of the most serious sexual assaults yourself.

“However incredible your account, it seems to me that you’ve actually started to believe your own lies.

“I cannot find a realistic prospect of rehabilitation in your case.”

Details of Adams conviction were not published at the time and he maintained a social media presence showing his flashy lifestyle.



Before his conviction, Adams’ dance academy got Prince’s Trust funding and he shared a selfie with the future King Charles on its website.

The sex attack took place at Carroll’s home, during his second spell with his hometown club Newcastle. The player writes: “Other things I’d quite like to forget but can’t.

“Something happened to me a few years ago that was so traumatic I only decided to include it in this book at the very last minute.

“I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now.



“Me and (current partner) Lou Teasdale spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not.

“I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet. Scary to talk about but it’s made me the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff.

And if me talking about it helps just one ­person then good, it will have been worth it.”

In the book Carroll describes his attacker without naming him: “He was always asking me and my ex to go out with him and even buys me clothes.



“He is divorced with kids but I can’t shift the feeling he likes me more than a platonic way. Whenever I bump into him at parties, he is always with young boys.”

Carroll, who won nine England caps, continues: “I was playing down South somewhere and on my way home this guy texts to ask what I am up to.

“When he texts again to ask if he can come round to watch the boxing, my partner tells me to stop pieing him off (putting him off).

“He takes over the kitchen, ­mixing drinks.

“I start to feel light-headed and think has he slipped me something. ‘Right, time for bed,’ I say to him, ‘I’ll order you a taxi’. ‘Oh no,’ he says, ‘I’ll stay in the spare room’.



Carroll, currently at Dagenham & Redbridge FC, then says he awoke to the friend assaulting him, writing: “I sleep naked and when I wake up this guy is under the duvet.”

Carroll went on to “smack” him as he ordered him out the house.

He writes: “I smack him as hard as I can and he hits the deck.

“I grab hold of his feet and drag him out on the driveway.

“I go back inside, lock the door and call the police and the nanny.



“Then it suddenly occurs to me, what if I killed him?

“He regains consciousness just as the police turn up and immediately starts telling the police I hit him for no reason. As it is the police arrest him and I have to go to the station as well.’

He adds: “What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I’d think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football . . .

“The trauma of what happened to me hasn’t gone away.”

BBC talent show Fame Academy ran for two series in 2002 and 2003 and was hosted by Cat Deeley and Patrick Kielty.



The winner got a £1million recording contract, a London apartment, and a sports car. Tough-talking Adams was the dance coach, choreographer, and fitness instructor for the contestants.

And he judged their movement skills alongside vocal coaches ­Carrie and David Grant.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Adams’ role was scaled back in series two but he later put celebrities through their paces for a Comic Relief Does Fame Academy spin-off.

He had been approached for comment. His social media profile was made private after he was contacted by The Sun on Sunday.

CAMERAS captured the strange action Thomas Tuchel made seconds before full-time during England’s thumping of Croatia.

Sports.title: Chelsea star Estevao endears himself to India after stealing show in Brazil’s 4-0 win over them
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA starlet Estevao will be the next superstar that the world’s most populated country falls head over heels in love with.

He stole the show in Brazil‘s 4-0 win over India with a goal and assist – but in a nation of almost 1.5 billion people, this game was never about the result.



It was about what this game does for Indian football outside of that, for the people here and for the players to test themselves against the world’s best, as they cheered every half-chance louder than any Brazilian goal, and every save the same.

That’s despite most of Kolkata supporting Carlo Ancelotti’s side until they came face to face with their home country.



Brazil’s connection to India is only matched by that of Argentina, after a visit from Pele in 1977 the love of the Selecao echoes throughout street markets and high-end stores alike – it is the individual brilliance of players like him, Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Neymar who capture the hearts of the locals here.

But still, Carlo Ancelotti insists there is “no culture of football” in India.



From what everyone in Kolkata witnessed, he couldn’t be more wrong – and this game will only make the love of football here stronger.

Every single person in Kolkata was tuned in for the visit of the five time world champions – you couldn’t walk a wile without spotting half-and-half shirts and scarfs draped around the shoulders of anyone who could get their hands on one.

Estevao’s powerful 27th minute opener could’ve been prevented by Gurpreet Singh Sandhu, but nerves seemed to get the better of him as the ball slipped away from his palms and into the back of the net.

He was at the heart of anything and everything impressive from Ancelotti’s side, who didn’t really need to shift out of second gear to get the better of the Blue Tigers, with an inch perfect assist for Pedro to make it 2-0 before half-time.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Every touch from the number 11 drew a gasp of air from the Salt Lake Stadium in anticipation of what trick he would bring out next – perhaps his Messinho nickname wasn’t wrong after all.

Chances came and went for Vinicius Junior to make a generation of fans idolise him, but he couldn’t make the impact of the teenage sensation on the opposing wing, or even of ex-Atletico Madrid winger Samuel Lino, who added a third and fourth for Brazil in the second half.

The people of India though remain thrilled, and filled with pride.

They avoided a heavy defeat and proved that young footballers here, in desperate need of some grassroots investment, can compete against the world’s finest.

Sports.title: Inside incredible 85,000-seater stadium that hosted India vs Brazil including helipad and wall for ROCK CLIMBING
Sports.content:
Next

THERE is a football stadium in North East India that you’ve never heard of, and it has some excellent lore behind it.

It’s called the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, AKA the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata, India, AKA “The Mecca of Indian Football“.



On the 3rd of October it hosted the Indian National Team in their biggest ever football match, as they took on Carlo Ancelotti‘s Brazil in a friendly – but that was only to be an added bit of history to this stadium.

The 85,000 capacity ground is a thing of beauty, and used to hold as many as 120,000 spectators before being redesigned in 2014 – it was at one time the second-largest stadium in the world without a racecourse.



Outside the stadium are beautiful sculptures and it even features a rock climbing wall as well as a lake that locals were swimming in before the game.

Half and half Brazil and India shirts and scarfs were being sold for as little as £2.80 outside the ground, with this being such a momentous occasion for the home side.

In terms of food, there is nothing outside the ground – unlike the footy scran we get back home – but local vendors in the street will offer delicious potato dishes with fried pastry and spices, kathi rolls, rice dishes and bhajis too.

It’s a hell of a footballing experience, unlike any other.

The metro line features pictures of football legends of the past like Neymar, Diego Maradona, Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi – as well as some cult heroes including former Chelsea midfielder Oscar and more.

Random, but cool.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In terms of history, the stadium is famed for a few things.

It’s the stadium in which Lionel Messi first EVER captained Argentina, and the same stadium in which England won the u19 World Cup, led by Phil Foden.

Diego Maradona also played there, and goalkeeping legend Oliver Kahn played his last ever match there – a farewell match against local side Mohun Bagan.

It also has some infamous history as the stadium made headlines in 2025, when Lionel Messi visited Kolkata as part of his ‘GOAT tour’.

When it comes to football, few are adored in Kolkata like Messi, and when he visited supporters had paid up to 12,000 rupees (£100) just to get a glimpse of the Argentine great.



However, when he entered the pitch, fans’ views of him were blocked by the fact he was surrounded by celebrities and officials.

Messi stayed on the pitch for just 20 minutes, with a spokesperson for him at the time claiming that he fulfilled the time commitment that had been agreed in advance.

Fans didn’t take well to the brief visit, ripping up seats and throwing items towards the pitch in protest.



The stadium boasts a helipad for VIP arrivals, subterranean reservoirs for emergencies, and a synthetic carpet that can transition to natural grass.

It is a perfect blend of modern footballing technology and enough tradition to make it feel like a ‘proper’ football stadium, as opposed to a soulless bowl.

On Saturday, a lot of Brazil’s travelling squad were visiting India for the first time, including boss Ancelotti.

But one player who has been there before is Vinicius Jr – with the Real Madid superstar previously paying a visit to Goa for the inaugural BRICS U-17 Football Cup – which Brazil won.

Brazil will be completing one hell of an international break after facing India, with the Blue Tigers next facing Uruguay on Tuesday.



Chelsea star Estevao lit up the game with a goal and assist, while Samuel Lino bagged a brace.

Sports.title: Three points from England’s win over Croatia as Thomas Tuchel finally finds perfect attack and blueprint for Euro 2028
Sports.content:
Next

ENGLAND throttled Croatia on their own turf as they drilled the rival outfit for SEVEN goals.

Harry Kane netted twice but there were plenty more goals to share around as poor Slaven Bilic watched his side get dismantled in absolute disbelief.



It was a demolition put on for the school-age crowd, with only children allowed in the Rijeka ground as a result of a supporter ban placed on Croatia following their fans’ antics during their Nations League clash with France last year.

School was in session for the Croatian adults on the field as well, who could apparently use a lesson in defending – no matter how impressive England‘s XI looked going forward.



The former World Cup finalists found themselves 4-0 down at half-time, and conceded almost as many again in the second period as frustration turned to hopeless disbelief.

And there will certainly be things for Thomas Tuchel to chew on from the result as well, including these three things we learned from the Three Lions’ field day in Croatia.



Lions show their teeth

England’s five-star attack looked absolutely unstoppable, with all four of Tuchel’s most advanced starters getting among the goals.

Anthony Gordon especially continued his blistering form this international break, and probably should have added another one or two goals to his solitary finish on the day.

With fans really starting to get behind the Barcelona man there is no doubt that Gordon is the first choice on that left side going forward, while Bukayo Saka is finally starting to look himself again after an injury-riddled recent spell with the national side.

It is worth remembering that despite the scoreline, England’s attack had to battle past a defence which included the likes of Brighton’s Luka Vuskovic, Manchester City‘s Josko Gvardiol and Bayern Munich star Josip Stanisic – hardly easy pickings.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Great Scott

Alex Scott was handed a surprise full debut against Croatia having played his very first minutes for the team just days earlier in the win over Czechia.

But the Bournemouth man more than held his own, shining alongside Elliot Anderson, with whom he won the U21 Euros last year.

What stood out about Scott’s performance was how positive he was when on the ball, looking to play it forward – just as he did in the lead up to the opener, as he played it to Jude Bellingham, who then teed up Kane.

Declan Rice will still remain the first choice at the heart of Tuchel’s midfield, but Scott, 23, has given the German something to think about.



Perfectly balanced

While the attack will receive many of the headlines thanks to the outrageous scoreline, England displayed their most balanced performance in a long time.

Whether it be Scott and Anderson instinctively knowing who should go and who should stay, or Lewis Hall again dovetailing beautifully with Gordon down the left, or Kane and Bellingham’s brilliant double act, England looked complete as a team.

Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa were slightly fortunate that Mateo Kovacic did not tuck away a golden opportunity in the first half, but other than that they proved almost impenetrable.

The aging Croatia side could not keep up with England’s energetic and organised press, which must now be the blueprint for Tuchel building towards the 2028 Euros.

Sports.title: Wakefield claim historic win over Warrington to become Super League champions

Wakefield Trinity were crowned Super League champions for the first time in the club's history with a 23-10 victory over Warrington Wolves in the Grand Final at Old Trafford.

It is the first time Wakefield have made the Grand Final and they achieved their greatest glory on their first attempt.

They also become the sixth winner of Super League, joining Wigan Warriors, St Helens, Leeds Rhinos, Bradford Bulls and Hull KR.

It rounds out a fairy-tale story for Wakefield who were relegated in 2023, returned to Super League in the 2025 season, and have now written themselves into the history books as champions.

Wakefield held a dominant 19-0 half-time lead thanks to converted tries from Cameron Scott, Isaiah Vagana and Jazz Tevaga, Max Jowitt staying calm under pressure with the boot.

The extra point was then added by Jack Sinfield with just minutes left in the first half.

Early in the second half there was drama as Corey Hall was sent to the sin bin for a high shot on Arron Lindop. Lindop scored with Wakefield a player down, and added a second later on, Ewan Irwin converting the first.

However, a try from Trinity winger Tom Johnstone was enough for them to stay far enough ahead and seal immortality.

Johnstone picked up the Rob Burrow Award for his phenomenal display in both attack and defence.

Wakefield complete the fairy tale with stunning Grand Final win

In front of an electric and sold-out Old Trafford, it was a flawless first 40 from Wakefield Trinity.

They thought they had opened the scoring on the sixth minute when Johnstone went over in the corner. However, on review, it was clear he had been held up then forced into touch.

It took only six minutes longer though for the Yorkshire side to get on the board thanks to a sublime no-look, one-handed flick pass from Lachlan Walmsley which sent Scott walking in and with the Jowitt conversion, they had a 6-0 lead.

While it was end-to-end stuff, metres were coming much more easily to Wakefield with their pack proving too strong. That meant every set ended in pressure.

In the 25th minute, a brilliant Jake Trueman pressure kick saw Johnstone jump highest and find Vagana on his shoulder to walk in. Jowitt added the extras once again.

Just over 10 minutes later, Tyson Smoothy went close and then was followed by Tevaga who threw a dummy and then used his power to barrel over. Jowitt stayed perfect with the boot to extend Wakefield's lead further.

With less than two minutes remaining of the opening half, Jack Sinfield used some big-game nous to send over a drop goal to give Wakefield a more than three-score lead, and left Warrington with a mountain to climb at 19-0 down.

There was drama immediately in the second half when Wakefield's Corey Hall was sent to the sin bin for a high shot on Arron Lindop to give Warrington their opportunity to hit back, and they did.

Irwin threw a lovely dummy and then passed to open up the space and with a player advantage, Lindop had all the room to walk over in front of the Warrington faithful. Irwin converted to bring the scoreline to 19-6.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Warrington are back in the game as they score shortly after Corey Hill is sin-binned for a high tackle Warrington are back in the game as they score shortly after Corey Hill is sin-binned for a high tackle

Warrington thought they had gone in again through Matty Ashton just minutes later, but a forward pass ruled out what would have been a score that brought the game right back in the balance

However, with numerical parity restored, it did not take long for Wakefield to get back on top once again and off the back of huge metres from Caleb Hamlin-Uele, they sent it out to Johnstone who used his step to pull off a sensational finish and with a 23-6 lead and 20 minutes to play, the Wakefield end was bouncing.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wakefield are closing in on a Grand Final win after a fabulous try to extend their lead Wakefield are closing in on a Grand Final win after a fabulous try to extend their lead

Warrington would not give up and with eight minutes left on the clock they kept the last tackle alive; Irwin sent over a looping pass and Lindop was in for his second. However, this time Irwin could not convert and the score was 23-10.

However the clock quickly ran away, Wakefield stayed strong, and immortality was theirs as the full-time hooter went and their name was etched onto the Super League trophy.

Jowitt: A rollercoaster of a year for me - highs are worth the lows

Wakefield's Max Jowitt to Sky Sports:

"A million per cent the highs are worth the lows.

"It didn't feel real that we were playing a Grand Final until we got here today.

"A rollercoaster of a year for me personally after dropping down to the reserves, not finding form, but I got my opportunity at the back end of the year.

"For this to be my last game for Wakefield, I will never forget it."

'Emotional' Johnstone: I can't believe it - my dream for the last decade!

Rob Burrow Award winner Tom Johnstone to Sky Sports:

"I can't quite believe it. I keep crying, I can't help myself! Such a special club, it's been the longest week of my life.

"To get out there and get it done, I don't know what to say.

"This club means eveyrthing to me. I've been saying it for a long time. My dream the last 10 years was to win a Grand Final with Wakefield.

"Daryl Powell sold me the dream that we were a club that had aspirations and wanted to win things.

"I believed every word they said and this is where we are now.

"We don't do this without that belief we have. We built our foundation on that."

Powell: We have produced flawless rugby league and will get better

Wakefield Trinity head coach Daryl Powell to Sky Sports:

"It's unbelievable really, the story. Where we've come from and our ability to go toe-to-toe with the best teams in the comp.

"We had a bit of a rocky period with the 10-minute sin-binning, but we were superb today.

"That's a big performance from an unbelievable group of blokes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wakefield Trinity's head coach Daryl Powell reflects on guiding his side to their first Super League Grand Final win Wakefield Trinity's head coach Daryl Powell reflects on guiding his side to their first Super League Grand Final win

"We just kept talking about it, and the players have gradually developed and got better. Then it becomes a reality when they see what they are capable of.

"Last week and the start today, almost three flawless halves of rugby league.

"We went to Wigan last week, and that was a hell of a job to go there and win, and it showed us what we could do.

"We kept that belief coming into this game. We are a proper team and we're going to get better."

Burgess: They beat us physically - it hurts

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess to Sky Sports:

"I don't think I'll have any regrets. We showed a lot of spirit in the second half. We are disappointed no doubt. But regrets? No.

"It was Wakefield's day today .The challenge is to now take that next step. It will be a long few weeks away."

Sports.title: India win Asian Games - but denied ODI sweep over West Indies by superb Hope
Sports.content:
India beat Pakistan in T20 cricket to secure back-to-back gold medals at the Asian Games - but their ODI side were unable to complete a 3-0 sweep of West Indies on the same day after Shai Hope's 162 not out led the tourists to their record chase of 352.

In the Asian Games final in Japan, India smoked 211-6 from their 20 overs, underpinned by Abhishek Sharma's 61 off 28 balls, Tilak Varma's 51 not out from 22 and Shivam Dube's 27 off 15.

Pakistan plummeted to 39-3 in reply and despite Hasan Nawaz's 96 off 51 balls, they could muster only 192-6 and lost by 19 runs.

Image: Abhishek hit seven sixes and three fours in his 28-ball 61

The victory was India's seventh in a row over fierce rivals Pakistan in T20Is and their 14th in the 18 matches between the teams in the format.

Tireless Hope hits brilliant ton as India denied ODI sweep

In New Chandigarh, however, India saw their total of 351-7 eclipsed by West Indies with 10 balls to spare as visiting captain Hope struck his 21st ODI hundred and second in as many matches to secure a five-wicket win after defeats in Thiruvananthapuram and Guwahati.

Hope's 143-ball knock featured 17 fours and and three sixes, with his final maximum, a slog sweep over deep fine leg off spinner Naman Dhir, bringing the scores level before he drove the match-clinching single to long-off.

There was a controversial moment when Sherfane Rutherford was given out caught behind off Dhir for 24, with the on-field decision upheld after a review despite the West Indies batter feeling the spike on Snicko was bat on pad, not bat on ball.

Rutherford's dismissal left West Indies 206-3 after 30 overs but Hope - who kept for 50 overs and then opened the battings - shared half-century stands with Keemo Paul (44) and Gudakesh Motie (19), having earlier put on 109 with Amir Jangoo (67).

India's score, achieved after they had tumbled to 4-2, was based on KL Rahul's 129 not out off 87 balls, plus Rohit Sharma's 92 from 85 deliveries and Ruturaj Gaikkwad's 57 off 69.

Shubman Gill (1) - who hit an unbeaten 223 in the second ODI as India chased down 406 to take an unassailable 2-0 lead - and Virat Kohli (0) fell to successive balls from Jayden Seales in the third over.

Kohli was bowled for a golden duck as Seales flattened his middle stump, moments after Gill had edged behind and been dismissed by a one-handed diving catch from Hope.

Image: Jayden Seales dismissed Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli from successive deliveries in New Chandigarh

T20s up next for India and West Indies

The teams will now meet in five T20s, starting in Lucknow on Tuesday, with Abhishek, Tilak, Shreyas Iyer and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi among the players to fly in for that series following victory at the Asian Games.

Cricket has been part of the Asian Games at every edition since 2010, bar the 2018 event in Indonesia, with India claiming gold on their competition debut in China in 2022 before backing up that success in Japan this year.

The next Asian Games is due to be held in Qatar in November 2030.

Sports.title: Seventh heaven for England as Croatia thrashed in stunning win
Sports.content:
England produced a dominant performance that will live long in the memory to defeat Croatia 7-0 in their Nations League tie in Rijeka.

In what must surely rank as one of England's best away results, Thomas Tuchel's side utterly overwhelmed their opponents. Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored two each but it was a stunning team performance that inflicted Croatia's biggest defeat.

The skipper opened the scoring by firing high into the roof of the net early on after being well fed by Jude Bellingham before Anthony Gordon's ingenuity engineered the second for Bellingham to score himself soon after. England were rampant from the outset.

Image: Anthony Gordon heads in England's third goal of a dominant win

The excellent Gordon had chances of his own before making it three. There had been some disquiet that Jarell Quansah had been preferred to Trent Alexander-Arnold but the Bayer Leverkusen man whipped in a quality cross for the Barcelona winger to nod in a third.

When Bellingham set up Bukayo Saka for the fourth before the break, Slaven Bilic looked shocked. Although Mateo Kovacic did miss a sitter, the score did not flatter England. It was an 'I-was-there moment' for the 100 away fans allowed in the stadium.

Croatia tried to be more aggressive after the break but a sensational team goal underlined England's superiority as Kane latched onto Elliot Anderson's cross to make it five. Saka soon latched onto an error for the sixth and Morgan Rogers capped it off late on.

Image: Harry Kane slides in to score England's fifth goal

Tuchel needed a strong showing during this quartet of Nations League games that concludes with a home game against the Czech Republic on Tuesday. The opening defeat to Spain followed by a win over a Czech side reduced to 10 men was insufficient.

This was as convincing as it gets against a Croatia team, led by Luka Modric, that looked unable to compete with the speed, strength and skill of an England side that included Alex Scott from the start for the first time. This was a significant win in Group A3 too.

With World Cup winners Spain currently boasting the perfect record, there is likely to be only more space available to qualify for the last eight of the Nations League in the spring. This win goes some way to securing that spot for England. A big boost for Tuchel.

Tuchel: It was a complete performance

England head coach Thomas Tuchel speaking to ITV Sport:

"Maybe there were three minutes after 3-0 where we had a big mistake and some easy ball losses but that was a 90-minute performance on a high level from everyone, from the first minute to the last minute, from everyone who started to everyone who came off the bench. It was the highest level and congratulations to the team.

"On an away pitch, very, very impressive. We created so many chances. We were so fluid from the start. I remember looking at the clock and thinking, wow, this has been a good first three minutes and then I looked again and it was a good first seven minutes and it just never stopped.

"We just kept the pace up, played through the gaps and were very, very clinical. We stayed hungry in our counter-pressing and defending so we did the basics right. I loved the attitude. We always played humble. We always got the basics right and that is why it was a complete performance."

Keane: Bellingham can become a great

Roy Keane speaking on ITV:

"Everything you would want. A complete performance in possession. Goal threat. Scored the seven goals. Kept a clean sheet. Hunting in packs when they lost the ball.

"England were clinical as well. Excellent. All the plaudits have to go to England. They were fantastic.

"Bellingham can go on to become one of the greatest players of all time. There's still a lot more to come from him. He's a huge leader for England."

More history for Kane

On the day that the England captain moved within one cap of Peter Shilton's record, Kane scored for the third consecutive game in this Nations League break. With six goals in his last five games for Bayern Munich too, his relentlessness really is remarkable.

Fresh from scoring 73 goals all competitions for club and country last season, Kane has now netted in each of his last six away appearances for his country, with only three men previously having scored in that many consecutive away matches for the Three Lions.

The most recent of those was Stan Mortensen in 1948 and the only man to score in seven matches in a row is Tom Finney. Kane will need to score away from home against Spain next month to match that particular feat. On this form, do not rule that out.

Image: Harry Kane celebrates scoring England's first against Croatia in the Nations League

'No better team in world football to watch'

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett at the Stadion HNK Rijeka:

"England sank Croatia without a trace on the Adriatic coast, with the Good Ship Tuchel now full steam ahead after the World Cup supporter mutiny.

"No one could have predicted a performance of this utter dominance against the team ranked 14 in the world.

"England cut through a woeful Croatia midfield and defence at will, like a red hot knife carves through softened butter, and Tuchel's front men had a field day.

"Two goals for Captain Kane with an assist to boot. Two goals for Saka, which will have been a timely confidence-boost for the Arsenal man. There was a goal and a hat-trick of assists for the irrepressible Jude Bellingham, alongside a goal and an assist for the equally magnificent Anthony Gordon.

"Croatia were simply blown away, and England could have won by more.

"When England are rampaging all over the pitch like this, wining back possession when they have no right to do so, passing forward at every opportunity and finishing ruthlessly, there is no better team in world football to watch.

"Seven-nil in Rijeka does not flatter them. This was a statement victory, and a marker of what they are capable of."

Sports.title: Keane: Bellingham can become one of greatest players ever
Sports.content:
England and Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham can become one of the world's greatest ever players, according to Sky Sports pundit Roy Keane.

The 23-year-old scored one goal and set up three more as England inflicted Croatia's biggest defeat in a 7-0 hammering in front of a reduced crowd in Rijeka in the Nations League.

Bellingham was England's standout player at the World Cup and has become the focal point of Thomas Tuchel's side, registering 13 goal involvements in his last 11 games since the start of the tournament.

Image: Jude Bellingham finished the match with the captain's armband after Harry Kane was subbed off

Keane heaped praise on Bellingham after the win over Croatia and said it was a complete performance from a player who has become a "huge leader for England".

"There's still a lot more to come from [Bellingham]," Keane said on ITV.

"Bellingham can go on to become one of the greatest players of all time.

"His attitude for England recently...I have been praising him for being fantastic in possession, but what he is doing out of possession, that lifts all these players.

"If you have a player who is that good in your team, who is amazing in possession and is playing for Real Madrid and doing brilliant things, but his work rate off the ball, that will inspire all the other players."

Keane said England made Croatia, who are ranked 14th in the world, look like a "Gibraltar-type of team".

On England's performance, Keane added: "Everything you would want. A complete performance."

Saka: 'Special' Bellingham deserved man of the match

Bukayo Saka, who scored two goals for Tuchel's side in Croatia, was in full agreement with Keane as he hailed the impact of England's men's player of the year for 2025/26.

"It was an amazing night for us," Saka told ITV. "We played with high energy and spirit and punished them tonight.

"He [Bellingham] was amazing tonight to be fair. He deserved player of the year and he probably deserves man of the match tonight as well. He was special. Happy to play with him and happy to have him in the England team."

Tuchel concurred with one reporter after the game that Bellingham had gone to to the "next level" but warned that "you can never stand still" in football.

Asked if he felt Bellingham had taken a step up in his performances, Tuchel said: "Yes, at the moment it seems like [that] and you always need to.

"The level that you showed last week is never enough in the next week, that's just the nature of football. We adjusted some things, gave the players a lot of responsibility and they are a group to be trusted.

"It was impressive. It was the first time that this group played like this together again and they were very good and the translation from the last two matches, from the training sessions and the meetings into this match was on the highest level."

Kane & Tuchel on England's formidable front four

Tuchel has landed on a formidable front four of Harry Kane and Bellingham flanked either side by Saka and Anthony Gordon.

All four were on the scoresheet against Croatia, who were completely overwhelmed by England's firepower.

Of the front four, captain Kane told ITV: "There's freedom. All four of us are good players, we can play in the 10 pocket, Ant can play as a No 9, B can come in as a No 10, Jude can play as a No 9, I can play as a midfielder.

"It's so hard for the opposition to pick it up. The bottom line is if you lose the ball, we're all smart enough and good enough to cover in midfield or defence.

"That's the way we want to play. For them it was so hard to pick a man and press."

Explaining why the front four were so impressive, England boss Tuchel added: "The support from the full-backs, of course, and then the movements through the last line were on the highest level today.

"They get better and better. That's why I didn't want to change so much from match to match, to get the fluidity going and to get the movements going and to get the automatisms right within the front four but they are very good together at the moment.

"They enjoy playing together and the work rate is on a high level and the counter-press is on a high level so these are complete performances.

Sports.title: Fury wants Trump for AJ fight ringwalk
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury plans to invite Donald Trump to accompany him on his ringwalk to his long-awaited showdown with Anthony Joshua.

Fury and Joshua, both former heavyweight world champions, have been rivals for years and will finally box on December 11 in Cardiff.

Lengthy and at times fraught negotiations to make the all-British clash have concluded with the two facing off for the first time at a press conference this week.

Now Fury wants US president Trump to join his procession to the ring at the 80,000 capacity Principality Stadium.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua come together in a face-off ahead of their fight on December 11

Fury, who met Trump at the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in June, said: "I'll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we'll see if he's available.

"Probably unlikely because of the situation he's in at the moment, being the President of the United States."

'Warm-up for Usyk'

Fury insists his clash with Joshua is merely preparation for his true priority - a trilogy fight against Oleksandr Usyk, to whom he has lost twice already.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Johnny Nelson takes a look back at the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference and expects things to heat up as the fight gets nearer

He said: "I don't have any intention of retiring after Joshua. I'm using this bum as a warm-up for Usyk.

"This is a bum to me and I can guarantee that on the night when I knock him spark out he won't know what time it is. And then I want the rabbit [Usyk] in New York City.

"This year will be the most active year for me since 2018. This'll be my third fight, I'm literally match fit.

"I've done 12 rounds with a 6ft 8in Arslanbek Makhmudov and I've done seven rounds with another 6ft 7in behemoth in Mariusz Wach. And then I'm going to do whatever rounds with AJ, who's another 6ft 6in guy.

"Let's not pull any punches here. I'm firing on all cylinders at the moment. I feel fantastic. I'm 38 years young."

Sports.title: Kane and Saka double up as England school Croatia in historic Nations League rout
Sports.content:
It had all the edge of a pop concert in the stands but England looked ready to steal candy from a baby. The 6,200 Croatian under-14s allowed inside Stadion HNK Rijeka were invited free of charge and this was a priceless footballing experience. England ripped Croatia to shreds to take a firm grip on second place in their Nations League group, boosting their hopes of reaching next year’s quarter-finals, and anyone supporting the home team could at least find consolation in watching Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham combine to devastating effect.

Perhaps the ticket should have come with an adult age rating. This was grisly viewing for the locals but Thomas Tuchel delighted in England’s most complete performance since surging to a 4-2 win over Croatia at the World Cup. Kane marked his 124th cap with his 88th and 89th international strikes and had plenty of help. Three assists and a goal decorated a scintillating display from Bellingham and Tuchel found satisfaction in the other members of his ruthless front four getting on the scoresheet.

Everything clicked. England could have had double figures against opponents ranked 13th in the world but they settled for seven. Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka were in lightning, goalscoring form on the flanks and another story was an exceptional full debut from Alex Scott. The 23-year-old proved that he belongs, impressing with his tenacity and quality on and off the ball, and made it hard to shake off the sense that Tuchel missed a trick by not taking him to the World Cup.

One gorgeous, defence-splitting ball from Scott to release Gordon emphasised that this is a player with a big England future. This was the Bournemouth youngster’s second cap and it said much about Tuchel’s belief in Scott that he deployed him against Luka Modric, even if the great Croatia midfielder has seen better days.

The occasion was nowhere near as surreal as when England played here with no supporters present in 2018. It was meant to be behind closed doors again – Uefa had punished Croatia after discriminatory and racist fan behaviour during last year’s Nations League quarter-finals – but the rules allow tickets to go to local children and the constant high-pitched cheers were a reminder that much of the crowd were not alive when Modric first faced England 20 years ago.

Tuchel knew youth was on his team’s side. Modric is 41 and, given that he was accompanied by another old timer in Mateo Kovacic, it not a surprise that Scott and Elliot Anderson, resuming their partnership when England won the Under-21 European Championship last year, dominated.

Anderson, Scott and Bellingham were superb. Bellingham, back in the side after being rested during Tuesday’s 2-0 win over Czechia, was still going near the end, sending the England substitute Morgan Rogers through to make it 7-0.

View image in fullscreen England’s Anthony Gordon scores their third goal past Croatia’s Dominik Livakovic. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters

The mind went back to when these sides met in their opening game at the World Cup. Anthony Barry gave an impassioned half-time interview and, having struggled in defence during the first half, England emerged triumphant after producing one of their best spells of attacking football under Tuchel.

Replicating those levels has been hard since then, but this was like Dallas. There was a moment when Bellingham went shoulder to shoulder with Modric and just eased his former Real Madrid teammate aside. England were quicker and stronger. The press was aggressive and Croatia were in damage limitation mode by the time Bellingham made it 2-0 in the 21st minute, stabbing past Dominik Livakovic from close range after Gordon plucked Saka’s cross out of the sky before cracking a low ball into the six-yard box.

Slaven Bilic, back in charge of Croatia for a second spell, was powerless to respond. England led after eight minutes, moving in a blur when Marc Guéhi cut out a loose pass from Josko Gvardiol. Bellingham scanned, turned and chose the logical option. He shovelled the ball through a gap; Kane, free of Gvardiol and Luka Vuskovic, set himself and rammed a shot past Livakovic.

The kids booed and gave a collective thumbs down as England’s captain celebrated, but they were watching greatness. Funny, of course, to think there was a time when Kane and Bellingham barely passed to each other. There is no problem with their relationship these days.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Gordon, again linking well with Lewis Hall, was a constant outlet on the left. He kept bursting beyond Josip Stanisic and now has a goal or assist in each of his last seven England games. It was 3-0 when Jarell Quansah, in for Trent Alexander-Arnold on the right, hit back at criticism of his crossing ability by whipping in a ball for Gordon to head past Livakovic.

Quansah was one of five changes by Tuchel, who also restored Jordan Pickford in goal. Pickford remains the No 1 and made a key intervention at 1-0, rushing out to smother as Ivan Perisic threatened.

View image in fullscreen Bukayo Saka scores from close range as England dominate the first half. Photograph: Darko Bandic/AP

England dozed off after Gordon’s goal. A rare misstep from Anderson led to an opening for Kovacic, who somehow shot wide after rounding Pickford. England responded on the stroke of half-time. Kane dropped back to help out and start a counterattack which ended with Bellingham toying with Croatia before crossing for Saka to score.

The 100 England fans given tickets enjoyed their evening. There was no let-up after the break. Anderson zipped down the right and crossed for a stretching Kane to score.

It was not long before Croatia, who suffered their biggest ever defeat, removed Modric. The night belonged to England’s stars. Kane, who set up Saka to make it 6-0 in the 68th minute will equal Peter Shilton’s appearance record when England host Czechia on Tuesday. The 33-year-old is not slowing down.

Sports.title: Ireland cut short news conference as mood darkens further before Israel game
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland’s press conference on the eve of their second Nations League match against Israel in Serbia was cut short as the head coach, Heimir Hallgrímsson, fielded questions from Israeli journalists.

Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Hungary in their first match on Tuesday after a turbulent buildup in which the Irish squad voted to fulfil the fixture despite unease among the team over the war in Gaza.

During that match the Irish players wore armbands and pointedly lowered their heads while the Israeli national anthem played. There were no handshakes between the captains before kick-off.

With the return leg taking place on Sunday in Backa Topola after the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) refused to host the match at home for security reasons, it was the Ireland manager’s pre-match press conference on Saturday that gave rise to new tensions.

One reporter questioned Hallgrímsson on his thoughts about the incident on Wednesday during a Flydubai flight from the UAE to Israel.

“What do you say about the people that you support? Their ideology is based on murder,” one journalist asked. “Just this week, one of them tried to kill 170 Israeli passengers, including 27 innocent children and thousands of others.”

An Irish press officer replied: “We are not doing any questions like this today. We are doing football questions.”

Another journalist then addressed the Ireland manager: “Your players call our players monkeys during the match …”, only to be immediately interrupted by an FAI official repeatedly insisting “that is completely untrue”, while the microphone was taken away from the reporter.

View image in fullscreen Republic of Ireland players bow their heads and wear black armbands in recognition of all lives lost in the Gaza conflict before facing Israel. Photograph: Bernadett Szabó/Reuters

“Don’t touch me, don’t touch me,” the journalist exclaimed, as the Irish delegation brought the press conference to an abrupt end.

Israeli authorities have condemned the actions taken by the Irish players, with the Israeli foreign minister, Gideon Saar, accusing Dublin of being on “the wrong side of history”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Surviving this, coming out of it together as one would be a massive win for me. That is coming from my heart,” Hallgrímsson said. “All the challenges that this team has gone through, all the criticism. Just surviving as a group after this game, that would be a big win for me and for this group, for the association. There’s been a lot of emotions from the people in Ireland about this, and obviously that affects the players as well.

“We want to do good, but it’s always going to be a challenge when the environment is as noisy as it is. So we try to focus on the football side, and we’ve done a lot of things to help in that area.

“One change that we’ve done in the last games is before we go on to the pitch, we do a little prayer and a huddle with the players and all the staff, just to cool our heads before we go on to the pitch.

“Conor Coventry has taken that part, so he is now called Brother Coventry in the squad. But it’s really good when you go into a high-intensity and big-pressure game like we’ve been doing, to start the game with cool heads.”

Sports.title: Zigiotti Olme capitalises on Liverpool mistake to keep Manchester United moving up WSL
Sports.content:
Julia Zigiotti Olme’s sixth-minute lob proved enough to earn the Manchester United coach, Eva Olid, a second Women’s Super League victory of the season with a 1-0 home win over Liverpool.

Zigiotti Olme capitalised on a mistake by Liverpool goalkeeper, Khiara Keating, and, despite some late pressure by Gareth Taylor’s side, United held on to make it back-to-back league wins.

After a shaky start under the new head coach, Olid, the Spaniard has now masterminded four consecutive victories in all competitions and United are unbeaten in five matches.

This was United’s 250th match since the team reformed in 2018 and Olid watched her side mark the occasion with the breakthrough after six minutes.

It was a moment to forget for England goalkeeper Keating after her pass out from the back was intercepted by Zigiotti Olme, who composed herself and chipped home in superb fashion.

Liverpool pushed for a leveller and drew a double save from the United goalkeeper, Phallon Tullis-Joyce, midway through the first half. Cornelia Kapocs had a low effort saved by Tullis-Joyce, who got up quickly to deny Beata Olsson on the rebound as well.

United’s Jess Park hit the crossbar before half-time with a left-foot strike from the edge of the box before Keating saved at her near post from Andrea Medina on the rebound. Liverpool’s best chance of an equaliser came 20 minutes from time when Jenna Clark found herself free at a corner but she could not direct her header on target.
