Sports.title: Haas admit set-up mistake on Bearman’s car made one session a “total waste of time” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Oliver Bearman revealed his qualifying performance was compromised because Haas set his car up incorrectly for Friday’s second practice session.

“My car, to be honest in FP1 it was okay, in FP2 we really struggled,” he explained. “We did a mistake with the set-up and basically it was as if we didn’t run in FP2. It was totally a waste of time.”

Bearman was 16th in the second practice session, three-tenths of a second slower than team mate Esteban Ocon. He said the mistake with his set-up left him without valuable reference information for the rest of the weekend on his first visit to Sepang.

“Going into FP3 with just pretty much two push laps, you don’t have enough time to fix mistakes that we’ve done in previous days,” he said. “So that meant I went into quali basically like this and just guessing what to do with the car, with my driving and everything.”

The “incredibly high” tyre degradation made it harder to make up for lost time, said Bearman. “It means that every new tyre you get one push lap on it.

“So if you say that I’ve had four push laps on the new soft heading into quali, well the one on FP2 was a total waste of time, so that meant the two on FP3 were also pretty much a waste of time because we were trying to recover. So we’re just very behind.

“That’s not our true pace, that’s not our true potential, but it’s really not far from it, if I’m honest.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

A heavy lock-up at turn one left him heading to elimination in the first round of qualifying. “In my second run I locked the front-left which is the outside front into turn one, which is super-unusual and weird and usually tells you something’s up with the brakes so we need to look into that,” he said. “So I came into my final run with a lack of confidence, I definitely left some lap time on the table.”

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu admitted the team slipped up on Friday. “Operationally, we made a mistake on Ollie’s car in FP2, so that meant in the session he couldn’t get any information, and he couldn’t recover in FP3 with him because the tires only last one lap.

“Unlike Baku, where you could keep running and recovering, it wasn’t the case here, so it goes to show that everything counts. As a team, even though it’s tough, there are lots of specific things we need to look into.

“I’m confident that when we look into it and understand it, we can put a solution in place, like we have done every other time. It’s very tough, but that’s what we’ve got to focus on.”

Sports.title: Mercedes expected to gain three-tenths from upgrade but lost five – Wolff | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes suffered an unexpected setback in Malaysia as their upgrade for the W17 failed to deliver.

The runaway leaders in the constructors’ championship produced one of their weakest qualifying performances of the season at Sepang. Andrea Kimi Antonelli was half a second slower than pole-winner Max Verstappen while George Russell was two tenths of a second further behind.

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said they expected the team’s long-awaited upgrade, one of few major packages they have introduced, would be worth around three tenths of a second.

“You’re expecting three tenths to kick in and it looks like [we’ve gone] three or four or five tenths backwards,” he told Sky. “It’s the first time we miss out on the top three, and by quite a chunk. So it’s odd, but I guess we will find a solution.”

Wolff said the unusually abrasive track surface at Sepang has complicated the team’s efforts to understand their new package.

“It’s very difficult to understand,” he said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we didn’t see all year.

“But then you can say it’s very hot and the Tarmac is very different to all the tracks. It looked really good in the morning. We seem to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

He said the team has identified two clear problems with their car performance this weekend. “It looks like we are very draggy because it’s the first time that we’re losing a lot of time on the straights to, especially, Max,” he said.

“Then through the low speed, turn two, we are not able to turn the car. There’s just too much understeer. So overall, things we haven’t seen we haven’t seen all year.”

However he believes there are further problems the team needs to solve. “Something else is going on and we have to understand,” he said. “This is now [about] working through the data and putting our heads together because we still believe that the upgrade works we just need to understand why not here.”

Sports.title: Verstappen takes first pole of 2026 ahead of Hamilton and Antonelli in Sepang | 2026 Bahrain GP in Malaysia qualifying
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen dominated qualifying at the Sepang International Circuit to claim his first pole position of the season.

Lewis Hamilton will join him on the front row of the grid for Formula 1’s first race in Malaysia for nine years. The pair will start in the same order they finished the last race at this track.

The threat from Mercedes failed to materialise as Andrea Kimi Antonelli compromised his session with his latest track limits breach and George Russell never figured in the fight for pole position.

Antonelli, who has had multiple penalties for track limits breaches this year, made life difficult for himself when he strayed beyond the exit kerb at turn six on his first lap in Q2. With Pirelli’s soft tyres only good enough for a single flying lap on the highly abrasive Malaysian track, Antonelli had to take a second fresh set to ensure he reached Q3, where unlike most of his fellow front-runners he would not have the benefit of a second set.

Verstappen’s first run in Q3 put him comfortably ahead, while Isack Hadjar backed him up in second place. Antonelli did his sole run in the gap between the others taking to the track and initially slotted into third place.

With his final run, Verstappen cut another tenth of a second off his best time so far, leaving the benchmark at a 1’35.130. His original run would have been quick enough for pole, as only Hamilton could get within three tenths of a second of him.

Hadjar qualified third but his grid penalty will drop him to eighth on the grid. Both Mercedes drivers will be among those to benefit, Antonelli moving up to third, Russell seventh. The two championship leaders will be separated by Charles Leclerc’s Ferrari and the two McLarens.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The two other drivers with grid penalties dropped out in Q2: Franco Colapinto and Arvid Lindblad Racing Bulls used Lindblad to give his team mate a tow down the back straight – some compensation for crashing into his team mate in Baku last week – and Liam Lawson duly took 10th place. However he was eliminated by a superb final lap from Gabriel Bortoleto.

The Audi driver claimed a place in the final 10 having been the only Audi driver to progress through Q1. Like Ferrari, both their drivers used the medium rubber, but a poor final lap by Nico Hulkenberg meant he went no further.

The Aston Martin drivers revelled in their latest car improvements to achieve the team’s first double Q2 appearance of the season. It comes five months after the FIA changed its Additional Development Update Opportunity regulations to help its power unit supplier Honda.

Carlos Sainz Jnr, the only Williams driver to reach Q2, split the two AMR26s. Alexander Albon continued his run of Q1 eliminations this season after locking up and running wide at turn 14.

Both Haas drivers went out in the first round. Oliver Bearman went deep at turn one on his first attempt while Esteban Ocon was one of the first drivers to complete his final run and felt he had left the pits too soon. The Cadillac pair were slowest.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Ferrari in Todt’s time had more problems than Vasseur faces | Briefs
Sports.content:
One thing all Ferrari team principals have in common is the intense scrutiny they face from the media and the passionate Italian tifosi.

Current team principal Frederic Vasseur has experienced that again in the past week, prompting the team to reiterate its support for him.

Vasseur is trying to put Ferrari back on the path to victory. The man who most recently achieved this successfully was Jean Todt in the mid-nineties. And as reader @Tifoso1989 explains, he arguably faced a much tougher task:

The management and the way the team was being run were clearly a mess that’s precisely why Vasseur was brought in but I wouldn’t say Ferrari’s underlying technical organisation was collapsing. The F1-75 is the clearest evidence of that. Ferrari produced the best all-round interpretation of the ground effect regulations straight out of the box. It was quick in qualifying, strong in race pace, and competitive across different types of circuits. It was the benchmark early in the season until the TD039 came in and Red Bull got the RB18 down to the minimum weight around Hungary. Whatever happened afterwards, you don’t produce a car like that if the entire technical organization is collapsing. And Ferrari had already spent years, particularly in the period before the budget cap, investing heavily in its infrastructure to sort out the wind-tunnel/track correlation problems that had plagued them. They had also invested in a new state of the art simulator from Bristol-based Dynisma, which was already being used in the development of the F1-75. On top of that, they were making extensive use of AWS for advanced analytics, machine learning and AI, allowing them to run simulations much faster and extract more data from the car development process. So I think there’s an important distinction here. The management was dysfunctional. The technical foundations weren’t. That’s actually part of my argument about Vasseur. He didn’t inherit the Ferrari of the early 1990s that Todt inherited. He inherited a team with enormous resources, modern facilities, a sophisticated simulation and data infrastructure and, as the F1-75 demonstrated, the ability to produce a genuinely excellent F1 car. His job was to take those resources and turn them into a properly functioning championship operation. And that’s why I’m much less sympathetic to the argument that Ferrari simply needed several years to rebuild from the ground up. The foundations were already there when Vasseur arrived.

Sports.title: Bilal Fawaz Stops Eithan James In Eight Rounds
Sports.content:
Bilal Fawaz (13-1-1) retained his British and Commonwealth junior middleweight titles with an eighth-round stoppage of Eithan James (17-3) tonight at Utilita Arena in Birmingham. The finish came at 1:14 of the round, earning the 38-year-old champion the £5,000 knockout bonus Eddie Hearn had offered before the fight.

Fawaz landed a heavy right hand that dropped James near the ropes, then scored another knockdown before the referee ended the contest. For James, it was his first stoppage defeat, with all his previous professional fights having gone to decisions.

The ending came almost immediately after commentator Darren Barker suggested Fawaz was feeling the pace. That observation offered James some encouragement, but Fawaz still had enough power to end the fight suddenly. Any prospect of the younger challenger taking advantage of a tiring champion disappeared with the right hand.

James, 26, entered with considerably more experience going the distance than dealing with a fight-ending crisis. His record showed he could complete rounds, but Fawaz forced a different test in the eighth. Once the champion hurt him, James could not get through the follow-up and recover between rounds.

For Fawaz, the result gives him a successful defense against a challenger 12 years younger. His age will remain part of the discussion when tougher opponents arrive, particularly if he begins to tire during longer fights. Against James, however, he retained the punching power to settle the contest before it reached the championship rounds.

Hearn’s bonus added a financial reward to the finish, although keeping both titles was the larger achievement. Fawaz left Birmingham with his belts after turning a moment when his stamina was being questioned into the decisive attack.

James now has a different kind of defeat to recover from. Previous points losses allowed him to finish the fight; this time, Fawaz’s power took that option away.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker vs. Conor Wallace Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker faces Conor Wallace in a 12-round IBF light heavyweight final eliminator today, October 3, at Utilita Arena in Birmingham, England. Boxing News 24 will update this page with results as the fights finish.

Undercard results

Bilal Fawaz (13-1-1) retained his British and Commonwealth junior middleweight titles by stopping Eithan James (17-3) at 1:14 of round eight in Birmingham. A heavy right hand sent James to the canvas near the ropes, and another knockdown brought the referee’s intervention.

The 38-year-old Fawaz delivered the finish just as commentary suggested he was beginning to feel the pace. James suffered his first stoppage defeat, while Fawaz earned the £5,000 knockout bonus Eddie Hearn had offered before the fight.

English super featherweight champion Ibraheem Sulaimaan retained his title with a hard-fought unanimous decision over Sonny Hardy after 10 rounds at Utilita Arena Birmingham. The scores were 97–93, 97–93 and 96–93, moving the Birmingham southpaw to 12–0 and handing Hardy his first defeat at 12–1.

Sulaimaan started quickly, but Hardy pushed him through a difficult stretch in the middle rounds, knocking his gumshield out during one exchange. The champion also had a point deducted before recovering his momentum in the eighth and finishing strongly over the final three rounds. Several ringside observers scored the contest considerably closer than the official judges, with some favoring Hardy.

Aaron Bowen (9-1) captured the Midlands Area super middleweight title with a unanimous decision over Klinton Baptiste (5-1) at Utilita Arena in Birmingham. The scores were 99-91, 99-92 and 98-92 after 10 rounds.

Bowen controlled the fight, catching Baptiste with clean right hands against the ropes and pressing for a stoppage. Baptiste fought with one eye closed for roughly half the contest but lasted the distance without a reported knockdown.

The punishment prompted ringside criticism that his corner should have intervened, although his durability kept Bowen from securing the finish. Bowen earned a clear victory, while Baptiste’s resistance made the closing rounds harder than the wide scores might suggest. Baptiste looked gone on a couple of occasions, but surprisingly, he stayed in there.

Super featherweight Adam Maca (7-0, 6 KOs) stopped Rogger Rivera (3-6, 2 KOs) at 2:56 of round two in their scheduled six-round contest. The 19-year-old unloaded with power shots until referee Chris Dean stepped in to end the fight. It was Maca’s sixth stoppage in seven professional outings.

The teenager produced another impressive finish, but he is making this level of opposition look too easy. Rivera offered little opportunity to assess how Maca handles resistance or adjusts when his power alone cannot settle a fight. Maca looks ready for better opposition that can extend him and give him more to solve.

Harley Burrows stopped Matias Ezequiel Herrera at 1:24 of round two in their scheduled six-round middleweight contest on the Ben Whittaker–Conor Wallace undercard in Birmingham. The 20-year-old southpaw pressured Herrera from the opening bell, mixing punches to the head and body.

Burrows trapped the Argentine against the ropes in the second round and punched through his high guard until referee Ryan Churchill intervened. Herrera had not been knocked down before the stoppage, which drew some ringside criticism for being slightly early. Burrows’ attack was wild at times, but his sustained pressure kept Herrera struggling to find room to respond.

The DAZN broadcast starts at 2:00 p.m. ET / 7:00 p.m. UK, with a subscription required. That is the card’s start time; Whittaker and Wallace fight later in the evening.

Whittaker has a chance to move within reach of a world title shot, but he must first get through Wallace over the scheduled 12 rounds. British title fights involving Sean Bruce and Bilal Fawaz feature on the undercard.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Expects Teofimo Lopez To Abandon Title
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez could give up his WBA welterweight title to pursue Ryan Garcia rather than fight Jack Catterall. Tim Bradley expects him to choose the bigger payday, viewing Catterall’s southpaw style as a dangerous obstacle to that opportunity.

Lopez has until the close of business Eastern Time on October 22 to reach an agreement with Catterall. The WBA ordered the fight on September 22 between its “super” champion Teofimo and “regular” champion Catterall, who is also the mandatory challenger.

Bradley doubts Teofimo will take that route.

“Hell yeah he gonna duck,” Bradley said during a panel discussion at Sean Zittel and 2 more on YouTube. “Jack Catterall fight is a hard fight for him. I think that’s a hard fight. It’s another southpaw … that jab, Catterall jab, good counterpunching. Teo got to go look for him.”

That is the difficulty Bradley identifies: Teofimo would have to create the exchanges against someone comfortable waiting to counter. Chasing Catterall could leave him reaching with punches and entering off balance, giving the challenger opportunities to score and move before Lopez can answer.

Ryan offers a different incentive. His name would help sell the event, and Teofimo could pursue that payday without first risking a defeat against Catterall. Bradley suggests Teofimo could decide to abandon the belt if that is what it takes to get Ryan.

However, October 22 is a negotiation deadline, rather than an automatic date for Teofimo to lose his championship. If the camps cannot agree, or either side walks away, the WBA can order a purse bid. Bradley’s prediction goes further, anticipating that Lopez will ultimately choose Ryan over fulfilling the mandatory.

Giving up the title would also remove a potential belt from the Ryan matchup. Lopez would be trading his position as champion for the earning potential of the opponent.

For Catterall, the immediate question is whether Teofimo will negotiate the ordered defense. For Teofimo, Bradley sees a choice between protecting a lucrative opportunity and taking a fight that could spoil it.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Seeks Shakur Fight To Answer Doubters
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield wants to make Shakur fight through pain, targeting his arms and shoulders when clean head shots aren’t available. His proposed approach is to punish the defense itself until openings appear.

There’s an understandable reason Schofield wants this fight so badly. Their canceled February 2025 meeting left him facing accusations that he wanted out. For fans who still suspect he feigned illness, another callout won’t settle anything. Getting into the ring with Shakur would give him the opportunity to answer them.

Schofield was reported ill and hospitalized before that scheduled fight. That does not establish that he fabricated an illness to avoid Shakur.

“That’s who I want before I finish my career,” Schofield told Fight Hub TV about Shakur. “I’m throwing to break bones. Like I ain’t even going to lie, in sparring I was practicing like breaking shoulders. Like I was hitting shoulders, hitting like forearms. I was just hitting anywhere I can. You know, I don’t care.”

The thinking is straightforward: if Shakur makes his head difficult to hit, Schofield wants to make blocking punches costly. Sustained attacks to the arms could make holding the guard and returning punches harder as the rounds progress.

Executing that against Shakur would require more than aggression. Schofield would need to cut off his exits, stay balanced while punching, and avoid spending entire rounds striking the guard while taking clean counters. He also argues that opponents need several approaches, recognizing that pressure alone might not be enough.

First comes Lucas Bahdi. Schofield’s next fight is scheduled for October 10 in Chicago for the vacant WBA lightweight title, giving him an immediate opportunity to advance his championship ambitions.

Schofield acknowledges Bahdi’s patience and knockout power but wants a stoppage himself. That ambition brings its own danger: forcing a finish could create the opening Bahdi needs.

Beating Bahdi would strengthen Schofield’s position to pursue bigger fights. Settling the doubts surrounding Shakur still requires a fight that actually happens.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Ticket Sales Revive The Klitschko Blueprint
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel’s reported 25,000 presale ticket sales give Frank Warren a financial reason to continue arranging manageable defenses in Germany. If Nelson Hysa attracts that level of demand, tougher opposition becomes less urgent from a business perspective.

The November 28 fight in Düsseldorf offers an early indication that Kabayel’s popularity can sell a stadium event without an established heavyweight rival.

“25,000 tickets sold in 24 hours presale for Agit Kabayel vs Nelson Hysa in Germany next month!” Warren posted on X. “Presale still open for the World Heavyweight title fight not to be missed.”

There are echoes of the Klitschko approach: build the evening around the champion, with the challenger supplying an unbeaten record and an optimistic knockout promise. Wladimir’s defense against Francesco Pianeta in Mannheim demonstrated how a less accomplished opponent could become part of a major German boxing occasion.

Warren’s figures suggest Kabayel may be developing similar commercial freedom. Overseas criticism of Hysa’s credentials has less financial consequence if local supporters keep buying seats.

That would represent a change from the fights that established Kabayel internationally. He stopped Arslanbek Makhmudov and Frank Sanchez in Riyadh, beating unbeaten contenders whose reputations made those victories meaningful. Those performances supplied evidence of his ability under pressure.

Hysa, 25-0 with 23 knockouts, offers attractive promotional numbers. At 42, however, he faces a substantial increase in opposition. Beating him would provide Kabayel with another successful defense while revealing comparatively little about his chances against the other champions.

The business calculation also extends beyond the stadium. DAZN lists the event as pay-per-view. German ticket buyers may embrace a homecoming spectacle, while international viewers could require a more competitive matchup before paying. No broadcast sales figures are available to establish that demand.

A profitable German base could help Kabayel negotiate better terms for future unifications, including offers from Saudi Arabia. He would have a credible alternative to accepting whatever purse is offered abroad.

The sporting cost comes if comfortable defenses become the routine. Kabayel has already shown he can beat dangerous contenders. Spending more of his prime proving he can sell tickets would delay the fights needed to establish how far that ability can take him.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua Sacrifices Millions For Tyson Fury Fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua accepted a pay cut of at least £10 million to bring his December 11 fight with Tyson Fury to Britain, according to Eddie Hearn. The promoter believes fighting in Cardiff gives Joshua an edge, but the expected post-midnight start and Fury’s own British following complicate that calculation.

Joshua has secured familiar surroundings at the Principality Stadium. What he has not secured is a convenient fight time or a crowd certain to favor him.

“To keep it in the UK he’s got to turn down eight figures plus,” Hearn said, as reported by BoxingScene. “AJ goes to me ‘whatever you think’ and I’m like ‘no, no, no, it’s your money. I can’t make that decision for you.’”

Hearn recommended Britain because he believed it improved Joshua’s chances. Joshua accepted the sacrifice, moving the event away from a reported November 20 date at Madison Square Garden.

Staying in Britain removes transatlantic travel, but a bout beginning after midnight still requires unusual preparation. Joshua and Fury will need to be ready to perform late into the night, with the exact ring-walk time still to be set. The location offers familiarity but doesn’t eliminate the scheduling challenge.

The crowd could also be divided. Fury has his own British following, making it difficult to treat Cardiff as a straightforward home advantage for Joshua. Both men could receive substantial support.

There is a financial argument for Joshua’s decision. Beating Fury could generate a lucrative rematch and strengthen demand for his next fight, helping him recover the money surrendered here. That potential return depends on winning. Paying more to secure a preferred location does not guarantee a better performance.

British ticket buyers face their own tradeoff. They get the fight on home soil, but the expected late start accommodates American viewers on Netflix.

Turki Alalshikh claimed switching from New York to Cardiff meant losses of £53 million for the event, separate from Joshua’s reduced purse. Wembley’s 11 p.m. curfew complicated plans, while Cardiff offered a retractable roof and roughly 80,000 capacity.

Joshua has paid a high price for the venue. Whether it gives him the edge, Hearn anticipates, will only become clear once the fight begins.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Prepares For Christian Mbilli’s Relentless Pace
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is working on his stamina for Christian Mbilli, whose punch output threatens to make his October 31 return a demanding one. At 36, coming off a defeat, elbow surgery, and more than a year outside the ring, Canelo faces an opponent capable of making him work when he would prefer a breather.

The timing makes this dangerous. Canelo has years of experience finding openings against aggressive fighters, but exploiting those openings requires him to keep answering. Mbilli’s willingness to throw repeatedly could turn Canelo’s pauses between attacks into stretches where the challenger is being outworked.

“We know he’s a fighter with a lot of stamina, who throws a lot of punches,” Canelo said to ESPN MX. “We have the experience. Obviously, we’ve been working very hard on having the stamina ourselves to be able to respond in the same way.”

That acknowledgment gets to the toughest part of this matchup. Canelo can land the cleaner, harder shot in an exchange and still spend the rest of the minute defending. If Mbilli keeps attacking after being countered, Canelo will need more than occasional eye-catching punches to control rounds.

Body punching offers Canelo a way to slow that pace. Mbilli’s aggression should give him opportunities to counter downstairs, but he has to take them early and consistently. Waiting for the perfect opening while absorbing combinations would allow Mbilli to dictate how much work each round demands.

Age and accumulated wear make that harder to sustain. Surgery does not establish that Canelo will return diminished, but this will be his first fight since the procedure. A high-output opponent is a demanding test of whether he can repeatedly punch, defend and reset under pressure.

Canelo argues that Mbilli has never faced anyone with his experience. That may help him anticipate attacks. The question is whether he can keep producing the answers for twelve rounds when Mbilli refuses to give him time off.

Sports.title: Sandor Martin Favors Ryan Garcia Against Isaac Cruz
Sports.content:
Sandor Martin favors Ryan Garcia against Isaac Cruz in a potential welterweight fight, questioning whether Cruz could overcome Ryan’s physical advantages after moving up from 140 pounds.

Martin believes Cruz could drop Ryan, but reaching him would be the harder part. Cruz would have to cross a taller opponent’s punching range repeatedly, making the quality of his entries more important than simply maintaining pressure.

Cruz is one of the options Ryan is considering for his next fight in December, although Ryan has yet to choose an opponent. Ryan’s drawing power gives him greater control over that decision, leaving Cruz waiting to see whether the opportunity materializes.

“Pitbull’s knockout power, despite him being a powerful puncher, decreased at 140,” Martin said in to Luis Parra. “Can a punch from Pitbull put Ryan Garcia on the canvas? I think so. Now, will he have the tools to land that punch? We have to see it in the ring. I think Ryan Garcia starts as the favorite because of his physical advantage, but Pitbull has his chances.”

Marching straight ahead would invite Ryan’s left hook. Cruz would need to feint, draw the lead punch, and move underneath it, then cut off Ryan’s retreat rather than follow him around the ring. Predictable timing would give Ryan repeated opportunities to land his best shot.

Ryan’s upright exits could give Cruz an opening. If Ryan pulls straight back without moving far enough to escape, another step could bring Cruz into position to attack the body. Staying close would force Ryan to defend combinations instead of setting his feet for another hook.

That makes the first exchange crucial. Ryan could punish a careless entry, but throwing his opening punch would not finish the defensive work. If Cruz gets underneath it, Ryan would need to turn away or tie him up before the pressure becomes sustained.

Cruz’s footwork would also affect his stamina. Chasing would consume energy without guaranteeing chances to punch; forcing Ryan toward the ropes would create more useful exchanges. Martin’s preference is understandable, but Cruz’s chances would depend on making Ryan fight at close quarters often enough to overcome those physical advantages.

Ghana News.title: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike’s failed execution
Ghana News.content:
The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday.

Governor Bill Lee announced the change on Saturday, sharing the news in a joint statement with Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada.

Strada said that his stepping down is "in the best interests" of the state, and called the ongoing investigation into the incident "entirely appropriate and necessary".

Pike, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, survived two injections and is now in critical condition at a Tennessee hospital as her lawyers seek to commute her sentence.

"Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment," Lee said.

Lee has ordered an independent review into Pike's attempted execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.

Attorney's for Pike called the resignation "justified" but said "it does nothing to help Christa now".

"What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person," Pike's legal team wrote in a statement. "We hope the Governor's call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee's entire death penalty system."

Pike is being treated at a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, where doctors are attempting to clear the drugs used during the execution from her body, according to legal filings.

She was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance. While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.

As of Thursday night, she was unconscious, intubated and on a ventilator.

The state's Department of Correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".

Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her failed execution.

Pike's attorneys previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.

The attempted execution went ahead after multiple failed, last-minute legal challenges by Pike's lawyers.

The US Supreme Court rejected two separate efforts to stop the lethal injection.

Tennessee's governor also denied a clemency request from Pike, the only woman on the state's death row.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer in 1995.

She was sentenced to death the following year after a media frenzy around the killing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

Ghana News.title: Free SHS suffering under NDC gov’t- Dr Bawumia
Ghana News.content:
New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has raised concerns about the management of the Free Senior High School (SHS) programme under the National Democratic Congress (NDC) government.

He criticised the administration over what he described as a deterioration in students’ feeding arrangements, difficulties with the placement of BECE graduates and the continued use of the double-track system.

Dr Bawumia made the comments on Saturday, October 3, when he addressed the NPP’s National Delegates Conference at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi.

He said the government had promised to improve the provision of meals to students under the Free SHS programme, but claimed that conditions had instead worsened.

“Free Senior High School is suffering under the NDC. After they promised to improve meals for students, today it has deteriorated,” he said.

Dr Bawumia also drew attention to challenges he said some parents were facing in securing placements for their children after they completed the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE).

According to him, some BECE graduates were being left out of the placement process, while parents seeking admission for their wards were being told that the students did not qualify for placement.

He said the situation was creating frustration for families seeking to secure places for their children in senior high schools.

The NPP flagbearer further criticised the NDC government for not scrapping the double-track system, which was introduced following the expansion of enrolment under the Free SHS programme.

Dr Bawumia said the NDC’s approach to the programme was not surprising to him, arguing that the party had previously opposed and criticised Free SHS.

“I believe many Ghanaians are not surprised by the way the NDC government is managing the Free SHS programme. They never believed in it. They bastardised it for years. They called it 419, election after election, until they realised its impact on every household in Ghana,” he said.

He maintained that the programme would operate more effectively under an NPP administration, pointing to the party as the initiator of the policy.

“Free SHS would be truly functioning as intended if its initiator, the NPP, was in office,” Dr Bawumia added.

The Free SHS programme was introduced in 2017 under the NPP administration and has since significantly expanded access to public senior high school education.

Ghana News.title: NSA cannot manage all Ghana’s sports facilities alone – Ampofo Ankrah
Ghana News.content:
Former Director-General of the National Sports Authority (NSA), Yaw Ampofo Ankrah, says the authority needs additional support to effectively manage Ghana’s sporting facilities.

Ampofo Ankrah was asked to step aside as NSA Director-General by President John Dramani Mahama on October 1, 2026, amid an ongoing investigation into visa-related allegations linked to the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Reflecting on his time at the NSA, Ampofo Ankrah told JoySports that the authority faced significant challenges in managing the country’s stadia and other sporting facilities and could not be expected to handle them all on its own.

“After a year and six months, it is clear that we at the NSA need help. It would be a great mistake to say that the NSA has to manage all these facilities on its own, which is what has been happening.

“However, I did not come into office to find a maintenance fund or a maintenance department,” he said.

Ghana News.title: MoH announces mop-up recruitment for health professionals
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Health has announced a nationwide mop-up recruitment exercise to fill vacancies created by applicants who failed to report to their assigned districts and health facilities.

The exercise is scheduled for Monday, October 5, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. GMT, according to a statement signed by Tony Goodman, Spokesperson for the Ministry of Health.

The recruitment will cover vacancies for nurses and pharmacy professionals across teaching hospitals, Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG) facilities and the Ghana Health Service.

For nurses, the available positions include 266 vacancies in teaching hospitals, 133 under CHAG and 30 under the Ghana Health Service.

The ministry has also announced 36 vacancies for pharmacy professionals, comprising five pharmacist positions and 31 pharmacist technician positions.

According to the ministry, the exercise is aimed at replacing applicants who failed to report to the districts and facilities to which they had been assigned.

“The Ministry of Health wishes to inform the general public and all prospective applicants that it will undertake a nationwide mop-up recruitment exercise to replace applicants who have refused to report to their various selected districts and facilities,” the statement said.

Prospective applicants have been directed to access the Ministry of Health’s recruitment portal, mohrrecruitment.com, to submit their applications.

Applicants who require assistance may contact the ministry on 0557208487 or 0557385895.

The ministry urged eligible applicants to take note of the recruitment date and time and complete their applications through the designated portal.

Ghana News.title: Turn Saltpond history into economic opportunity – Stakeholders
Ghana News.content:
The President of the Mfantseman-Saltpond Development Alliance (MSDA), Ernest De-Graft Egyir, has called for the establishment of a National Political History and Heritage Centre at Saltpond to help preserve Ghana’s political history and turn the town’s historic sites into opportunities for tourism, education, research, and economic development.

He made the call at a Founders’ Day commemoration held at Saltpond on the theme: “Saltpond Heritage, Ghana’s Future, Turning History into Opportunity.”

Mr Egyir said the proposed centre should go beyond a conventional museum to serve as a national institution for learning, remembrance, research, tourism and civic education.

He said it should document Ghana’s journey from colonial rule to self-government and independence, while preserving political archives, photographs, oral histories and other records associated with Saltpond and the country’s independence struggle.

“History must become knowledge, knowledge must create opportunity, and opportunity must contribute to development,” he said.

Mr Egyir said the initiative should also promote investment, enterprise, employment and community development, adding that Saltpond was appropriate because of its historic landmarks and association with Ghana’s political development.

He cited Canaan Lodge, where the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) was formed in 1947, as one of the landmarks that could form part of the proposed heritage development. Historical records confirm that the UGCC was launched at Canaan Lodge, Saltpond, on August 4, 1947.

He said the centre should be linked to a wider heritage corridor connecting historical sites with tourism, education, hospitality and local enterprise.

Mr Egyir stressed that the initiative should be national rather than partisan and should present Ghana’s political history comprehensively and responsibly.

“We don't want NDC and NPP in this initiative to develop Saltpond. But it must tell Ghana's story responsibly, comprehensively, and with respect for the different people and movements that contributed to this independence of ours,” he said.

He called on the government, the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, the Ghana Tourism Authority, traditional authorities, universities, historians, development partners, the private sector and the diaspora to support the initiative.

Mr Egyir said MSDA had already begun work towards the vision, including feasibility studies and efforts to acquire land for a Saltpond Centre of Excellence.

He also announced that the Odambea Festival had been moved to the third week of August to provide a fixed and convenient period for greater participation by visitors and dignitaries. He expressed appreciation to the traditional leaders for responding to their request and restoring the festival to the third week of August.

The Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority, Mr Gilbert Abeiku Aggrey Santana, said Saltpond’s historical significance should not end with annual commemorations but should be converted into a sustainable heritage and tourism opportunity.

He said the town played an important role in Ghana’s political awakening, particularly through the activities of the UGCC and other nationalist movements.

Ghana News.title: Ampofo Ankrah opens up on ‘constant and unrelenting’ pressure at NSA
Ghana News.content:
Former National Sports Authority (NSA) Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah has spoken about the intense pressure that comes with leading the authority, describing the demands of the role as constant and unrelenting.

Ampofo Ankrah was appointed Director-General by President John Dramani Mahama on March 13, 2025, succeeding Seth Panwum Boyoyo.

During his tenure, Ampofo Ankrah and the NSA faced criticism over several issues, particularly the management and condition of sporting facilities across the country.

Speaking to JoySports, Ampofo Ankrah acknowledged the demands of the position, stressing that the role leaves little room for excuses.

“It’s different when you’re put in a position where the pressure is constant and unrelenting. There are no excuses. What I’ve noticed about the NSA is that there are no excuses,” he said.

Ampofo Ankrah was asked to step aside on October 1, 2026, pending investigations into allegations surrounding a visa facilitation arrangement linked to the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

The NSA has denied the allegations, while investigations into the matter continue.

Ghana News.title: I expect to win NPP Vice Chairman race – Nana B
Ghana News.content:
NPP Vice Chairman aspirant Henry Nana Boakye says he is confident of securing victory in the party’s National Delegates Conference, praising the security personnel for maintaining peace and controlling the crowd at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi.

Speaking to JoyNews at the congress, Nana B said the event had so far been peaceful and commended the security officers for their efforts in managing the large gathering of party supporters and delegates.

“It has been peaceful, and I applaud the security for how they have controlled the crowd,” he said.

He expressed optimism about winning the vice chairman position, citing his years of service, dedication and leadership within the party.

“I am expecting obviously to win and become vice chairman. I have worked hard, and I believe that the party today will be a celebration of long service, dedication, leadership of courage, fearlessness and experience,” he said.

Nana Boakye said he remained hopeful of a positive outcome and expressed confidence that, by God’s grace, he would emerge victorious at the end of the election.

Ghana News.title: NDC’s failed 24-Hour Economy has become 24-Hour demolition – Dr. Bawumia
Ghana News.content:
The 2028 presidential candidate of the New Patriotic Party, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, has delivered a damning assessment of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) government's two years in office, declaring that its much-touted 24-Hour Economy has become a 24-hour demolition exercise.

Addressing the National Delegates Conference in Kumasi, Dr. Bawumia said the government is struggling to fulfill many of its lofty promises to Ghanaians, particularly the youth.

"The NDC promised Ghanaians and the youth of this country in search of jobs a flagship 24-hour economy with one job, three shifts and 3 people (1-3-3). Nearly two years have passed and the jobs have not come or even showing any signs of coming," Dr. Bawumia said.

"The young graduate and artisan who voted for the NDC because of this sweet promise of a dramatic job boom through the 1 job 3 shifts, 3 people offer under the NDC is still waiting for his or her shift," he said.

"Sadly, the promised 24-hour economy jobs have now turned into 24-hour demolition of buildings for a so-called 24-hour markets even the NDC cannot explain," he added.

Failed promises

Dr. Bawumia listed a litany of what he described as failed promises, saying the Women's Development Bank, which was supposed to empower market women, has not opened its doors to a single woman almost two years on.

He also accused the government of worsening the cost of living. According to him, instead of the promised reduction in electricity tariff under the 24-hour economy, there has been a dramatic increase, crippling households, small businesses and industries.

"Today, the barber shop owner, the hair salon operator, the bread baker and many young businesses who were promised better electricity tariffs are now striving to survive because much of their sales are going into electricity bills under the NDC government," he noted.

He added that transportation, spare parts, fuel and rent costs continue to rise, arguing that even though inflation has declined to 5% on paper, the real cost of living has increased massively.

Dr. Bawumia said the government's only lifeline has been the relative stability of the Cedi, which he attributed to the NPP's Domestic Gold Purchase Programme, recalling that in June 2021, on his recommendation, the Bank of Ghana launched the programme to protect the currency from global shocks.

"Records show how the programme saved our economy from serious crisis and revamp of the cedi. And the programme is today the major support behind the stability of the cedi, and with it the easing of inflation and interest rates that this government now celebrates. Ironically, key officials of the government today opposed the policy when it was introduced, vehemently claiming it was not feasible," he said.

He warned that "a good tool in careless hands becomes an expensive one," alleging that the government is making unprecedented losses on the programme.

He further accused the government of abandoning crucial NPP legacies projects like Agenda 111 district hospitals, which he said would have provided access to healthcare and jobs if completed.

He also accused the NDC of making unrealistic promises to end galamsey in months and restore polluted water bodies.

"Ghanaians are reminded every day of how the NDC and its senior officials, many of whom are cabinet ministers and top CEOs today, lambasted the NPP government and told Ghanaians that they possessed the magic to end galamsey instantly if voted into office. Today, under their watch, in nearly two years, galamsey has grown embarrassingly worse," he noted.

On Free SHS, he said the programme is suffering after the NDC promised to improve it.

"After they promised to improve meals for students, today it has deteriorated. Many of our young BECE graduates are being deliberately cut off from Free SHS and what frustrated parents are told by the government is that their wards have deservedly failed," he said.

He reminded delegates and the nation that the NDC never believed in Free SHS and bastardised it for years until they saw its impact.

On cocoa and other promises, he said: "The promises to cocoa farmers to increase the cocoa price to GH¢6,500 has turned out to be a scam. The promise of automatic posting of teachers and nurses... has turned out to be another scam. Even their much-touted ‘Nkoko nkitikiti’programme has failed."

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Remains of Bulgaria’s Czar Samuel return ‘home’ after 1,000 years
World.content:
The emperor is a symbol of Bulgarian national identity whose repatriation stoked tensions with Greece.

More than 1,000 years after his death, the remains of medieval ruler Czar Samuel have arrived in Bulgaria.

A symbol of Bulgarian national identity, Samuel was a warrior emperor who battled the Byzantine Empire to expand his kingdom before suffering defeat and dying soon after in 1014. His supposed remains were discovered in a Greek border area in the 1960s.

The coffin and remains were flown on Saturday to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia, on board a military aircraft that was surrounded by air force fighter jets.

Thousands of people poured into a public square to honour the czar’s arrival, which capped years of fraught negotiations between Bulgaria and Greece until an accord was reached this week.

Bulgarian politicians across the spectrum paid tribute to the medieval ruler, listening to the national anthem and a 21-gun salute.

“Today, we Europeans are learning to read history with a desire to belong not only to our homeland, but also to the culture that unites us across the entire European continent,” Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.

“That is why Europe must not reopen old wounds but must work for peace as the supreme good,” Radev continued, referring to the centuries-old rivalry between neighbouring Greece and Bulgaria.

Crowds cheered as fighter jets performed a flypast.

Martin Nestorov, a 42-year-old software engineer, told the AFP news agency he attended the ceremony “to welcome Czar Samuel back to Bulgaria, where he belongs”.

“I am here because I am Bulgarian, and a Bulgarian is returning to his homeland,” added Tsanka Zlatkova, 65, a retired art historian.



A procession brought the remains to be laid in the Church of Saint Sofia, a sixth-century basilica that is the capital’s namesake and where church officials say Samuel was baptised.

Competing claims

The handover of Samuel’s remains is part of a broader accord between the Greek and Bulgarian culture ministers.

In exchange, Greece is slated to receive 48 objects that Bulgarian troops pillaged from churches and monasteries in Greece during World War I.

Speaking before the handover, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said he hoped the ceremony would boost Greece’s campaign to repatriate the Parthenon Marbles, a collection of 2,500-year-old marble sculptures taken from the Acropolis in Athens and later displayed in the British Museum.

“The global community is essentially re-evaluating its longstanding stance on protecting cultural heritage,” Mitsotakis said, adding that historical heirlooms “cannot be treated as the spoils of war”.

Bulgaria is not the only country to have claims on Samuel. A huge statue of the czar stands in the North Macedonian capital of Skopje, with Macedonians claiming him as “their” ruler.

In 2022, a bilateral commission recommended presenting Samuel as the head of a state that “most contemporary historiographers consider to be the Bulgarian Empire”, based in what is currently North Macedonia.

World.title: Is the CJP changing India’s political landscape?
