WASHINGTON, DC – JUNE 22: U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks before signing an executive order in the Oval Office of the White House on June 22, 2026 in Washington, DC. President Trump signed two orders on quantum computing. Andrew Harnik/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Andrew Harnik / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP)

US President Donald Trump has called on Congress to introduce mandatory prison sentences for people convicted of defrauding Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security, while proposing personal financial liability for state and local politicians who knowingly fail to stop fraud.

Trump made the call in a video posted on Truth Social on Saturday, saying the proposed legislation would eliminate probation as an option for people convicted of stealing from federal benefit programmes.

“Today, I’m calling on Congress to pass legislation to address fraud in Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security programs,” Trump said.

“First, Congress must impose mandatory minimum sentences on fraudsters who steal from critical benefit programs designed to take care of the sick, feed the hungry, care for our children, and protect our senior citizens, retirees.”

He said people convicted of stealing from the programmes should face lengthy prison terms, with tougher penalties based on the amount stolen.

“Under our proposal, probation is no longer an option for the fraudsters. If you steal from the American people, you will go to prison, and for a long period of time,” he said.

“And the more you steal, the longer you’ll stay in that prison. Not only that, but if you’re a convicted fraudster who gets caught stealing from the American people a second time, your sentence will be doubled.”

Trump also proposed doubling the sentence of convicted fraudsters who are caught committing the offence for a second time.

“If you’re a convicted fraudster who gets caught stealing from the American people a second time, your sentence will be doubled,” he said.

The president further proposed making state and local politicians personally liable for losses caused by fraud if they knew about it, had the power to stop it but failed to act.

“Under our proposal, if a state or local politician knows about fraud and has the ability to stop it, but does nothing about it, they can be personally liable for the full loss of the American taxpayers’ money that they should have stopped and they should have saved,” Trump said.

Trump did not provide specific sentencing ranges or explain in the video what legal standard would determine whether an elected official knew about fraud or had the ability to prevent it.

The proposal comes amid stepped-up federal efforts by the Trump administration to combat fraud involving government benefit programmes.

“This legislative proposal will make fraudsters think long and hard before they keep stealing from the American people and will make crooked and corrupt politicians think also long and hard before they ignore fraud that they can stop and that they should stop,” Trump said.

He ended the video with a warning: “So from now on, fraudsters, we’re watching you.”

World.title: 2027 Polls: CSOs demand stringent action against vote-buying
World.content:
…as FG okays quarterly policy dialogue

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA — Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) on Friday identified vote-buying as a major problem that the Federal Government must find ways to tackle ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In separate presentations at the 2026 National CSOs Summit held in Abuja, representatives of various organisations working to promote credible, transparent and inclusive elections in the country decried the repeated failure to prosecute individuals previously arrested for vote-buying.

They said the country’s electoral process would continue to be undermined unless stringent measures were adopted to ensure the prosecution and conviction of offenders, thereby serving as a deterrent to others.

In his remarks, the Executive Director of the Value Rebirth and Empowerment Initiative (VREI), Pastor Edewor Egedegbe, argued that a credible and peaceful election requires informed citizens.

He maintained that reports of inadequate funding for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) “raise serious concerns about preparations for the election, which is just months away.”

He added that late funding not only disrupts the planning process but also increases the risk of avoidable failures.

Insisting that the electoral body had not done much in terms of voter enlightenment, Egedegbe said INEC must also open its books by publishing what it has received so far.

“It should start procurement of needed items and embark on the training of essential manpower.

“Democracy succeeds where citizens participate in the process without fear or intimidation,” he added.

For his part, the Executive Director of the Peering Advocacy and Advancement Center in Africa (PAACA), Chief Ezenwa Nwagwu, highlighted the importance of encouraging citizens to register and obtain the Permanent Voters Card (PVC), which he said carries more value than a bank Automated Teller Machine (ATM) card.

“This is what we should be emphasising. The cost of electricity is embedded in the PVC, so also is the cost of education and everything about life in the country.

“It is not about asking people to take money from candidates and vote their conscience. When you sell your PVC, it diminishes your citizenship.

“The fact that you think the law does not work in the country does not mean that you cannot be used as an example to show how the law works,” Nwagwu stated.

He blamed the recurring cases of vote-buying during elections on what he described as “the pauperisation of citizens.”

“Until we realise the powers we have as citizens, we will continue to shortchange ourselves.

“We should always ask ourselves this question: if votes don’t count, why then do politicians place value on your votes?

“As we move towards the 2027 general elections, we as citizens have to re-examine ourselves and take over the power of polling units from the politicians. The citizens must drive the process,” he insisted.

Meanwhile, the federal government said it had approved the establishment of a quarterly civil society policy dialogue forum to institutionalise citizens’ participation in policy formulation, implementation and evaluation.

The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, who represented President Bola Tinubu at the summit, said the forum would provide a structured platform for evidence-based advocacy and ensure that community-level concerns were reflected in government decisions.

He also pledged the FG’s commitment to expand civic space for social accountability, including greater collaboration with accredited CSOs on public finance transparency, budget tracking and monitoring of humanitarian and grassroots interventions.

“This administration firmly believes that no nation can achieve inclusive, equitable and sustainable development without a vibrant, credible and responsible civil society operating within an open and enabling civic space,” he added.

The National Convener of the CSOs Summit, Ambassador Kunle Yusuff, who is the Director-General of the Civil Society Organisations on Community Advancement and Humanitarian Empowerment Initiative (CSCHEI), said the aim was to galvanise the various organisations to brainstorm on the way forward as the nation braces for another round of elections.

Yusuff said the summit was proposing a sustainable partnership compact through which the government, civil society and the private sector could work jointly on national priorities rather than operating from positions of suspicion.

According to him, the proposed framework will provide a mechanism for monitoring government policies, budgets and electoral promises, while ensuring that information generated from communities reaches relevant authorities.

World.title: Netanyahu invites ‘true hero’ Indian flydubai captain to Israel
World.content:
This handout photograph released by the Israel’s Foreign Ministry on September 30, 2026 shows Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, the captain of flydubai flight FZ 1073. Israel’s leader credited the pilot and passengers of a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight with averting catastrophe on September 30 after they overpowered a co-pilot who allegedly tried to crash the aircraft, forcing an emergency landing. The Indian embassy said Machchhar was being treated at a hospital in Saudi Arabia and India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi described him as a “HERO” in a social media post on October 1. (Photo by Israel’s Foreign Ministry / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE – MANDATORY CREDIT “AFP PHOTO / Israel’s Foreign Ministry” – HANDOUT – NO MARKETING NO ADVERTISING CAMPAIGNS – DISTRIBUTED AS A SERVICE TO CLIENTS

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday invited to Israel as a guest of honour the Indian captain of a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight who offered a dramatic account of how he saved the plane after being attacked.

Netanyahu said he wanted Captain Smit Machchhar and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, one of Israel’s key international partners, to light a flame at a national ceremony for Israel’s Independence Day next May, saying the role was usually reserved for Israeli citizens.

“You are a true hero of the brave peoples of India and Israel and you are a hero of the entire world,” Netanyahu said in a video his office released of his telephone conversation with the hospitalised captain.

UAE investigators have said that the co-pilot planned the “terrorist act” by attacking Machchhar with an axe.

Asked how the attack unfolded, Machchhar said the co-pilot had asked to take time to pray, as devout Muslims do five times a day.

“A lot of locals, they do pray, which is not out of the ordinary. While he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back,” Machchhar said.

“Suddenly after I think I would say about four to five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head. My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something is not right.

“But then after that the blows kept coming one after the other. That’s when I realised that it’s not the aircraft, it’s the other guy who was in the cockpit with me.”

While saying his memory was not entirely clear due to his injury, Machchhar said he managed to pull open the cockpit door “but I think he shut it back closed.”

“I had that one last fight left in me,” Machchhar explained, saying he knew he faced certain death if not.

“That’s when I pushed against everything. I gave everything that I had and just went for the door and opened the door and thankfully people were waiting.”

AFP

World.title: Tinubu Eulogises Elder Statesman, Lt Gen Alani Akinrinade, At 87
World.content:
.Felicitates house member Kabir Bichi on 45th birthday

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has eulogized elder statesman and former Chief of Army Staff, Lt General Alani Ipoola Akinrinade (rtd), on his 87th birthday on October 3, 2026.

A ciivil war hero, General Akinrinade served as Chief of Army Staff and later Chief of Defence Staff before retiring from the military.

The President, in a release issued on Saturday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, described General Akinrinade as a towering statesman, a gallant soldier, and a principled patriot who has dedicated his entire life to the service of Nigeria.

Tinubu noted that General Akinrinade’s legacy is etched in gold in the annals of the nation – from his distinguished military career, which culminated in leading the Nigerian Armed Forces, to his courageous role as a leader of NADECO during the struggle for the restoration of June 12 and democracy.

According to the President: “General Akinrinade stood on the right side of history. When it was dangerous to do so, he chose democracy over dictatorship, the people over power.

“He is one of the heroes who made the Fourth Republic possible. Nigeria will forever be grateful for his courage and sacrifice.”

Tinubu commended the General for his continued service to the nation as an elder statesman and for being a voice of wisdom, moderation, and unwavering commitment to national unity.

The President prayed for robust health, peace of mind, and many more years of impactful life for General Akinrinade.

He wished the General a happy and fulfilling 87th birthday celebration.

Also, the President rejoiced with Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Appropriation, Hon. Abubakar Kabir Bichi, on his 45th birthday.

Tinubu described Hon. Bichi, who represents Bichi Federal Constituency of Kano State, as a vibrant, resourceful and dedicated lawmaker whose commitment to legislative duties and national development stands out.

The President, in eulogising Hon Bichi said:

“As Chairman of one of the most strategic committees of the House, Hon. Bichi has demonstrated uncommon capacity, grit, and leadership in steering the consideration, scrutiny, and passage of the nation’s annual budget, a role central to implementing the Renewed Hope Agenda.

“I commend him for his effective representation of his constituents and his impactful interventions in education, infrastructure, and youth empowerment, which have endeared him to his people.

“Bichi has distinguished himself since his first election to the House in 2019, where he served as Chairman of the House Committee on Works in the 9th Assembly and now as Chairman of Appropriation in the 10th Assembly.

“As he marks his birthday today, I urge him to rededicate himself to serving his people and his fatherland.

“And I pray to Almighty God to continue to bless him with good health, wisdom and strength”.

World.title: Fuel Subsidy Removal, FX Policy Aimed At Addressing Longstanding Structural Challenges, Says Group
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

A support group, the Atiku Bagudu Grassroots Network for Tinubu 2027, has explained that the removal of fuel subsidy, foreign exchange reforms and ongoing fiscal and tax reforms were difficult decisions but necessary measures which were aimed at addressing longstanding structural challenges in the Nigerian economy.

The group named the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Atiku Bagudu, as its patron and also endorsed President Bola Tinubu for a second term, declaring its intention to mobilise 19 million votes from the 19 northern states for his re-election.

The group gave the assurance after a meeting in Abuja attended by delegates representing the 19 northern states.

At the meeting, members reviewed the administration’s policies and programmes and discussed strategies for grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

It added that its decision to support Tinubu’s re-election was based on administration’s efforts to reposition the economy, strengthen infrastructure and implement reforms aimed at creating a more sustainable fiscal foundation for the country.

Its convener, Hon. Ali Oriri in a statement issued yesterday said the network would build a strong grassroots structure across the North to mobilise support for Tinubu and secure the group’s target of 19 million votes.

He said the 19 million-vote target was achievable with effective coordination and sustained mobilisation across the region.

The convener stressed that the group would take its campaign to communities across the North, engaging traditional, religious, youth and community leaders as part of its grassroots mobilisation strategy.

Oriri urged members of the network in the 19 northern states to strengthen their structures and commence sustained engagement with voters ahead of the 2027 election.

He added that the group would also continue to explain what it described as the benefits and long-term objectives of the administration’s reforms to citizens at the grassroots.

He explained, “The removal of fuel subsidy, foreign exchange reforms and ongoing fiscal and tax reforms were difficult decisions but necessary measures which were aimed at addressing longstanding structural challenges in the Nigerian economy.”

The group also cited ongoing investments in roads, rail, power, housing, agriculture and other sectors as reasons for seeking continuity under Tinubu.

It was of the opinion that continuity was important to allow the reforms to mature and translate into broader economic opportunities and improved living conditions for Nigerians.

World.title: MPB Announces Implementation of New Pension Rates, Payment of Arrears to Military Pensioner
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Military Pensions Board (MPB) has announced the implementation of the newly approved pension rates following the adjustment arising from the new minimum wage.

According to a statement by the Public Relations Officer of the Military Pensions Board, Squadron Leader Aliyu Mohammed, the applicable arrears have also been processed and will be paid into the accounts of all pensioners with effect from today, 2 October 2026.

The Board appreciates the patience, understanding and cooperation demonstrated by military pensioners throughout the implementation process.

The military said it remains committed to the timely payment of pensions and the continuous improvement of pension administration in recognition of the invaluable service and sacrifices of Nigeria’s military veterans.

World.title: H1 2026: NGX Grants Access Holdings Filing Extension Deadline
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Access Holdings Plc, yesterday said it has received approval from the management of the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) to further extend the filing deadline for its Interim Audited Financial Statements for the half-year (H1) ended June 30, 2026.

The Company Secretary, Access Holdings, Mr. Sunday Ekwochi, in a signed statement stated that the extension aimed at enabling the company to conclude the requisite regulatory approval process ahead of the publication of the financial statements.

“The company will publish the results promptly upon receipt of the required approval. NGX had previously approved an extension of the filing deadline to September 30, 2026.

“As the regulatory approval process remained outstanding at that date, the Exchange granted a further extension to enable the company to complete the process.

“Access Holdings remains committed to fulfilling its regulatory obligations and maintaining timely and transparent communication with shareholders, investors and other stakeholders,” the statement stated

He added that Access Holdings would continue to keep the market informed of any material developments relating to the publication of its H1 2026 results.

Between December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026, the stock price of Access Holdings has appreciated by N9.40 per share or 44.76 per cent to N30.40per share from N21.00 per share it opened for trading.

World.title: Piggyvest Platform Mobilises Savings, Investments from Over 9m Nigerians, Celebrates 10th Anniversary
World.content:
Dike Onwuamaeze

In a country with a record low savings and investments, the Co-Founder/Chief Executive Officer of Piggyvest, Mr. Somto Ifezue, has announced that the company has mobilised over nine million Nigerians and transformed them to committed savers and investors for assured financial freedom.

Ifezue announced this last month during the company’s ‘Open House’ event at the National Theatre, Lagos, to mark the 10th anniversary of Piggyvest, a saving and investment digital platform.

He said, “We are trying to transform Nigeria into more of a productive country. And in order for it to be productive, there has to be savings and investments internally.

“So one of the things we have done at Piggyvest, which we are proud of, is that we have reduced a lot of frivolous spending from our customers. Before, they would just go and buy things based on impulse.

“Today, our customers are using Piggyvest to limit their unplanned spending. We are helping people to save, invest and achieve financial freedom.”

He also said that the Piggyvest has completely rebuilt and refreshed its app to make more robust and simpler for its next generation of users’ financial journey with additional savings and investments features.

A Co-Founder and Chief Marketing Officer of Piggyvest, Mr. Joshua Chibueze, said that Piggyvest wants to use its 10th anniversary to become the financial platform for Nigerian households.

Chibueze said, “What we are aiming to achieve is how to go deep into the Nigerian household, whether it is your mother, brother, sibling or cousin” by creating “a safe, secure place where Nigerians can easily participate in high-yield investment opportunities.”

World.title: The Real Cost Of Kwara’s Elephant Projects
World.content:
By Adeniyi Ìṣhọlá

Last week, the Kwara State Government inaugurated the Kwara Revenue House amid fanfare. The building is undeniably imposing, flashy, grand, and visually striking. It beautifies its surroundings and generates strong political optics for an administration that has become remarkably adept at constructing magnificent but irrelevant and wasteful projects in strategically visible locations.

But beyond the aesthetics and the optics, what real, tangible, and measurable value does the Kwara Revenue House deliver to the average Kwaran? This is a question the government has conspicuously failed to answer. And it is a question that, when asked about project after project executed by the Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq administration, produces the same uncomfortable silence.

Was there really a need for this elaborate Revenue House? The Kwara Internal Revenue Service (KWIRS) exists to collect taxes and generate revenue for the state. Its effectiveness is determined by the quality of its systems, the capacity of its personnel, the robustness of its technology, and the strength of its compliance framework — certainly not by the size or grandeur of the building it occupies. Does the size of a revenue agency’s headquarters even determine how much revenue it generates? The answer, obviously, is no.

Consider this: the Lagos State Internal Revenue Service (LIRS), which generates more than ten times what KWIRS generates annually, does not need a structure of this scale to demonstrate its capacity to collect taxes. If Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial capital and its highest-generating state, can run a world-class revenue agency without an ostentatious headquarters, what precisely justifies Kwara building one?

The Abdulrazaq government has not told Kwarans how much the Revenue House cost. That alone is a scandal. Public funds were committed to this project over a period of at least three years, yet the total expenditure remains undisclosed. Also, there is no record that the project was subjected to competitive public tender. The contract was awarded in secrecy, the cost has been kept from public view, and when concerned Kwarans began asking questions, the government responded not with transparency but with deception.

The government specifically claimed that the Revenue House was built with savings from consultancy fees that would otherwise have been paid. That claim deserves scrutiny, particularly against the information emerging from KWIRS’ own budgetary allocations. Available budget figures cited in the course of writing this piece indicate that more than N16 billion was allocated to consultancy payments over a three-year period by KWIRS, an amount that is larger than what the agency budgeted for salaries of its staff. If the Revenue Service is still budgeting billions of naira for consultants, Kwarans want to know what exactly were the consultancy savings that supposedly financed the Revenue House.

KWIRS is not only still paying consultants. It is paying them at an escalating and alarming rate. The government’s claim of building the Revenue House from consultancy savings is not a misstatement. It is a deliberate lie, a calculated attempt to prevent Kwarans from asking how much of their money was spent on a building whose cost has been hidden from them. The government must come clean. It must disclose the exact amount spent on the Revenue House. If consultancy savings truly financed the building, let the government publish the figures: how much would have been paid to consultants, how much was actually saved, when were the savings made, and how much of those savings was spent on the Revenue House?

If the Revenue House represents one dimension of the Abdulrazaq administration’s crooked spending priorities, the renovation of Kwara Hotel represents its most extravagant and indefensible project. The numbers tell a story that no amount of government spin can sanitise.

When the project commenced, the government told the public that the renovation would cost N17.8 billion. That figure was already outrageous and difficult to justify. In just little over a year, the renovation cost ballooned to N27 billion, which is N9.2 billion above the already controversial initial announced cost. With no disclosure from the state government, public discussions are now putting the eventual expenditure at N30 billion or more.

It is important to recall that when the Kwara Hotel renovation project was originally put out to bid, companies that participated in the initial bidding process submitted quotations in the range of N3 billion to N3.5 billion. How then does a project estimated at N3.5 billion by professional construction companies end up costing N27 billion within a two-year period? What additional works justified the escalation? What variations were approved? What is the final contract sum? How much has actually been paid? And what is the projected final cost? These are questions agitating the minds of this writer and other concerned Kwarans.

The government’s communication machinery has attempted to justify these costs with figures that have proven to be false. One of the governor’s spokespersons, Ibraheem Abdullateef, recently appeared on a radio programme and claimed that the renovated hotel has ten lifts, each costing between N600 million and N1 billion. This was definitely a fabrication, constructed on the spot to make the exorbitant N30 billion renovation cost reasonable. It is also inconceivable that a hotel of Kwara Hotel’s size and configuration would require ten lifts, Governor Abdulrazaq’s aides would say anything, no matter how ridiculous, to defend their paymaster.

Beyond the dishonesty, there is the fundamental question of economic sense. How sound is it for a state grappling with a significant infrastructure deficit to spend N30 billion renovating a single hotel? How telling is it that the two most expensive projects this government has undertaken are the renovation of a hotel and the construction of a revenue agency’s building? What does that say about a government’s sense of priority? Is a renovated hotel truly the best use of N30 billion in a state where several critical roads are in disrepair, where hospitals are understaffed and ill-equipped, where schools sit in dilapidated conditions, and where Kwarans are forced to travel outside the state to access CT scan and MRI services because the state cannot provide them?

The Revenue House and the hotel renovation do not exist in isolation. They are part of a broader and deeply concerning pattern of capital-intensive, optics-driven spending that has defined the Abdulrazaq administration’s approach to governance from its earliest days.

On the same Ahmadu Bello Way in Ilorin where the Kwara Revenue House and the renovated Kwara Hotel stand, the state government has been constructing an International Conference Centre (ICC) for more than four years. The facility, which includes conference halls and a hotel, has consumed billions of naira and remains uncompleted. One must ask the obvious question: why is the government building another hotel inside the ICC while simultaneously spending nearly thirty billion naira to renovate Kwara Hotel, located less than 500 metres away? What gap does the ICC hotel fill that the renovated Kwara Hotel cannot?

If that duplication were not enough, the government has also committed to spending N10 billion to build a Convention Centre in Ilorin—yet another capital-intensive facility whose construction is proceeding even as the International Conference Centre remains unfinished. Why build a convention centre when a conference centre is still under construction? What is the difference in their intended functions? What economic logic justifies this apparent multiplication of similar facilities at enormous public expense? These are questions of basic fiscal responsibility and common sense that the government must provide answers to.

Let us, for a moment, consider what the resources committed to these projects could have delivered if invested in the areas where Kwarans need help most urgently. Imagine what the billions of naira wasted on these projects could mean if directed towards projects with direct and measurable impact on ordinary people.

These huge funds could have resurfaced hundreds of kilometres of urban and rural roads across Kwara, connecting communities, reducing transport costs, and opening up economic opportunities for farmers, traders, and small business owners. It could have equipped and fully staffed dozens of primary healthcare centres across the state, reducing maternal and infant mortality rates that continue to define health outcomes in Kwara. It could have provided CT scan and MRI machines to state hospitals, ending the heartbreaking reality of Kwarans travelling to other states for basic diagnostic services at higher costs and greater risks. It could have built and equipped schools, provided scholarships, funded agricultural programmes, created jobs for restless young people, and invested in the kind of infrastructure that generates economic activity and improves lives across generations.

Instead, the funds went into a hotel renovation, a grandiose revenue house, a conference centre, a convention centre and a visual art centre that has remained shut after more than two years of its completion. These are mostly irrelevant projects concentrated in a single corridor of the state capital, designed to impress visitors and generate political talking points, but offering little to nothing to the farmer in Baruten, the patient in Ekiti, the student in Irepodun, or the trader in Ilorin’s markets who struggles daily with the accumulated consequences of eight years of misplaced governance priorities.

Were these the best possible use of Kwara’s resources? The Abdulrazaq administration must justify, with credible economic arguments rather than political talking points, why a state with Kwara’s infrastructural deficit and developmental needs chose to spend its resources on monuments rather than on the people. Because at the end of the day, the true measure of a government is not the grandeur of the structures it leaves behind. It is the quality of the lives it improved while it had the power to do so.

*Isola writes from Ilorin

World.title: NGO Offers Succour to 500 Traders Affected by Market Demolition In Anambra
World.content:
David-Chyddy Eleke in Awka

A non-governmental organisation (NGO), Hamilton and Thelma Ezeonu Foundation, has offered assistance to over 500 persons whose shops were demolished in Anambra State in an ongoing road construction by the Anambra State government.

The demolition, which affected close to 200 buildings and shops in Afor Nnobi market in Idemili South local government area of Anambra State also displaced traders whose shops were located in the area, throwing their families into penury.

The founder of Hamilton and Thelma Ezeonu Foundation, Mr. Hamilton Ezeonu who was on ground to commiserate with the victims, stated that the purpose of the gathering was to console them over their losses and to assist them to enable them start life and businesses all over again.

“What we have just given you is our own little way of contributing to your livelihood, so that you can rent shops and start life again, so that all of you who have lost your means of livelihood can start all over again, and will be able to fend for your families.

“One of our main purposes is to assuage your loss for what happened at Afor Market. When I heard about the incident, I could not sleep for nights, because, you lost your means of livelihood.

“What I did was to call Governor Charles Soludo to arrange meeting with other leaders of Nnobi. This is because, I could not sit somewhere while my people are suffering. We cannot abandon you. Your issue is very personal to you,” he said.

The beneficiaries were empowered with bags of rice and cash to ameliorate their plights and cushion the hardship in the country.

His wife and co-founder of the NGO, Dr. (Mrs.) Thelma Ezeonu also consoled the shop owners, assuring that the intention of the government was good and that once the rebuilding was concluded, the foundation would help further.

Beneficiaries who were mostly aged women thanked the foundation for coming to their aide and bringing them succour in times of hardship.

World.title: Omotola: Election May Be Won by Vote Concentration, Not Number of States
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

The Publisher of an online newspaper, Politico.ng, Lai Omotola, weekend said a presidential candidate may win more states in the forthcoming election and still lose the overall contest.

He said vote concentration and turnout in areas of electoral strength would be critical to the outcome.

Omotola, who spoke at its October edition of the 2027 presidential election projection press conference in Lagos, explained that the ability of political parties and candidates to mobilise voters in their strongholds would be more significant than merely winning a large number of states.

He cited Lagos State as an example, noting that although the state has a large number of registered voters, achieving 50 per cent turnout would be difficult, unlike some areas where voters traditionally turn out in large numbers and vote as communities.

According to him, “It is not only for you to win election with maybe 10 votes, 20 votes, or 30,000 votes and say you are winning this election. This election has to be won in landslide, where your strength is.”

He added that his organisation; Political Intelligence Group ( PIG), had figures from its research but was not ready to make them public, urging politicians to study their own data and electoral calculations carefully.

Omotola also called for the use of opinion polls to better understand voters’ preferences, but cautioned that polls should not be treated as foolproof predictors of election outcomes.

He said polling should examine different demographic groups, including young people, older voters, urban and rural populations, and their respective concerns.

According to him, “Young Nigerians are particularly concerned about access to education and financial independence, while older people are more concerned about pensions and gratuities, and working-class adults are interested in employment opportunities and economic activity.”

He, however, observed that Nigerian politics had yet to become predominantly ideological, saying ethnicity, religion, economic conditions and insecurity continued to influence electoral behaviour.

On the influence of economic hardship on voters, Omotola said hunger and poverty remained important factors, but argued that voters’ decisions could also be shaped by community leaders and other influential figures.

He further alleged that vote buying could influence electoral outcomes, claiming that some voters might accept between N20,000 and N50,000 because of their economic circumstances.

Omotola also said political parties should pay greater attention to the difference between campaign promises and the realities of governance, particularly when making promises on issues such as fuel subsidy, minimum wage, employment and social welfare.

Reacting to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s position on restoring fuel subsidy, he said any proposal to reintroduce subsidy should be accompanied by a clear explanation of how it would be funded.

He described campaign promises as forecasts that could only be tested against the realities of government finances after a candidate assumed office.

Omotola, who is also the Convener of the Renewal Group, said politicians should therefore explain the sources of funding for their proposed programmes rather than merely announcing figures and policies.

He also questioned the feasibility of some campaign promises on wages, arguing that proposed increases in workers’ salaries would have wider implications for government expenditure and the private sector.

According to him, Nigeria’s fiscal position requires political leaders to demonstrate adequate knowledge of public finance and how government revenue, recurrent expenditure, debt servicing and infrastructure spending interact.

“Being stubborn and having good intention can never replace knowledge,” he said, arguing that Nigeria needed leaders with the knowledge required to develop sustainable solutions to its economic challenges.

On the role of ethnicity and religion in Nigerian elections, Omotola said their influence remained evident in the way politicians engage religious and community leaders during campaigns.

He noted that politicians continued to visit churches and mosques because they recognised the importance of such institutions and their leaders in mobilising voters.

He also said recent legal disputes involving politicians who changed political parties or lost party tickets were unlikely, in his assessment, to significantly alter the broader electoral calculations, as affected politicians would continue to pursue their cases through the courts.

Emphasising on the electoral map which he presented, the Convener projected that the ruling party would win 19 states if the 2027 presidential election were held in October.

The projection also showed the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) increasing its projected number of states from 8 in September to 10 in October, while the African Democratic Congress (ADC) dropped from 9 to 8 states.

Omotola said the monthly projection was designed to help political parties identify their areas of strength and weakness rather than serve as a prediction of the final outcome of the 2027 election.

According to him, the October map was based on political developments and activities recorded across the country in September and reflected what the electoral landscape could look like if the election were conducted in October.

Omotola, however, stressed that the projection was premised on the assumption that the election would be conducted freely and fairly, noting that violence or large-scale electoral malpractice could significantly alter the projections based on current observations.

World.title: ‘God fetched him’: EC school mourns matric learner who drowned at KZN beach
World.content:
Hoër Landbouskool Marlow in Cradock, Eastern Cape, is mourning the death of matric learner Jonathan Bradfield who drowned at KwaZulu-Natal’s Mtunzini Main Beach this week.

The 19-year-old had been swept out to sea, presumably in a rip current, when the tragedy struck during the school holiday.

TEEN DROWNS AT MTUNZINI BEACH

On Thursday, matric learner Jonathan Bradfield was swept out to sea during a trip to the Mtunzini Main Beach in KZN.



The tragedy occurred during a school holiday trip to KZN with his girlfriend and her family.

The KZN surf rescue network – comprising the National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI), Mtunzini Community Police Forum, Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife rangers and IPSS Medical Rescue – were immediately activated.

Their search-and-rescue operation also used a drone, a boat, and a jet ski.

According to NSRI Richards Bay station commander Norman Rautenbach, the teen was swimming with his girlfriend when she left the water. Upon looking back, she noticed Jonathan experiencing difficulty in the water before he disappeared in the surf zone.

Jonathan’s body was later discovered.

EC SCHOOL MOURNS MATRIC LEARNER’S DEATH

Jonathan Bradfield’s school, Hoër Landbouskool Marlow, shared a heartfelt tribute to the blonde-haired matric learner.



The agricultural school shared: “Our hearts go out to Johny’s father, brother, his family, friends, classmates, and everyone who loved him and walked with him part of his life’s journey.

“Johny will be remembered for much more than just his time in a Marlow jacket. He was a friend, a classmate and a Wolram – a young man with a deep-rooted faith, a beautiful heart and a special place among those who knew him. He was much loved among the staff who got to know him through his Marlow years. His place and the memories he leaves behind will forever be a part of our school community”.

Jonathan’s aunt, Sharon Bradfield, also posted several emotional Facebook posts.

Some of the tributes included those from the teen’s school friends. One spoke of the “golden boy” and his strong Christian faith.

It read: “Johnny was a child of God. I will forever admire his boldness for his Christianity.

World.title: Clever cogs: Kia Seltos 1.5 CRDi X-Line review
World.content:
Sitting at the top of the range is the new Kia Seltos 1.5 CRDi X-Line for R614 995. The Korean firm is now officially the fastest-growing non-Chinese brand in the country. And it is the Indian-built Seltos that’s currently the most valuable nameplate in its vast compact SUV range.

Fitting for a flagship, the Kia Seltos 1.5 CRDi X-Line comes wrapped in an exclusive matte Dark Gun Metal Grey finish over black alloy wheels. And with the new design language, it is a truly handsome, head-turning beast …

KIA SELTOS 1.5 CDRI X-LINE

We really approve of this interior, both intuitive and styled with a touch of flair. Image: Ray Leathern

Built on Kia’s K3 platform and borrowing styling cues from the larger Telluride, it follows the marque’s ‘opposites unite’ philosophy. Therefore, square and tough on the outside, smooth and inviting once you’re in. Flush-fitting door handles clean up the profile nicely, and the twin dashboard screens now merge into a single seamless display spanning driver and passenger. Boot space grows to 563 litres, a genuinely useful 103-litre jump over the outgoing model.



Under the bonnet of this test unit is the 1.5-litre turbodiesel, which produces 85 kW and 250 Nm. It’s an engine that trades outright revs for easy, low-down pull. However, when asked to pick up its skirt off the line or for an urgent overtake, it is found wanting. As a result, the zero to 100 km/h time of 12 seconds sounds about right. On the fuel economy front, Kia claims 5.3 l/100 km mixed. However, during our daily use we returned 6.5 l/100 km. The smaller unit has to work pretty hard, especially up hills, so a more powerful oil burner would be more economical.

WHERE IT EARNS ITS PRICE TAG

Borrows a lot of its styling inspiration from the big Telluride sold in the USA … USA! Image: Ray Leathern

However, the standout is how well its semi-autonomous systems are calibrated. Beyond the expected six airbags, traction control and ABS with EBD, the X-Line’s active driver aids are genuinely impressive for a (relatively) affordable family SUV. Adaptive cruise control paces you smoothly against traffic ahead, active steering holds you confidently within your lane, and blind-spot monitoring paired with rear cross-traffic alert keeps you aware of what’s happening behind you.

And what sets these systems apart isn’t just that they exist, it’s how well they’re tuned. They intervene smoothly rather than nervously, and they behave with a level of polish you’d expect from cars costing several times more. We’ve said it before about Kia’s approach to driver assistance tech, and the new Seltos only reinforces it. The Koreans truly have mastered the intuitive usability of this tech, more so than the others.



THE VERDICT

Square stance, matte paint finish and extra attention to the C pillar make it a standout in the compact SUV segment. Image: Ray Leathern

As mentioned, the Kia Seltos 1.5 CRDi X-Line tops the diesel range at R614 995. This pushes it well clear of the equivalent GT-Line CRDi at R544 995B. But don’t forget that petrol-powered LS derivatives open the range from as little as R389 995. For that money, distinctive styling, a genuinely spacious cabin, and a well-mannered drive are guaranteed. But you will lose out on the brilliant semi-autonomous tech.

Unfortunately, for the diesel hypermilers out there, we would have loved to test the range of the CRDi to the full. But for whatever reason, our test unit arrived with less than half a tank of diesel. Perhaps recent record fuel price hikes are to blame !? Nevertheless, it’s a real shame, because everything about the way the easy-going CRDi carries itself suggests it would have been a great loping road-tripper. But that’s an evaluation we’ll have to circle back to one day, perhaps when the fuel price returns to normal …

World.title: This 200-year-old town is the last on the West Coast with property below R650 000
World.content:
In 1826, when British Navy Admiral Robert Lambert ventured up the Cape Coast, he may not have known he would be discovering what would later be known as the Diamond of the West Coast.

Today Lambert’s Bay is beloved for its crayfish, white sandy beaches, dolphins, whales, birds, and wildflowers.

But it is also one of the last towns along the West Coast with affordable property.



Affordable Property in Lambert’s Bay

Among the 41 sales recorded by the Western Cape Deeds Office, the average sale price for a property in Lambert’s Bay as of September 2026 was R970 000.

This makes Lambert’s Bay cheaper than Elands Bay, Velddrif and Strandfontein, where the average sale price ranges from R1.42 million to R1.73 million.

Currently, a handful of listings advertise 2-bedroom flats in Eureka Sentrum (Apartments) for R630 000.



Studio flats in the same building are listed for R420 000.

These flats are a 1-minute walk from Meeuland Beach.

Buyers are getting a bargain.

The typical price per square metre for a 2-bedroom in the Western Cape is R29 591, but these flats start at R10 161 per square metre.



Other properties in the area include a 988-square-metre corner plot listed for R450 000.

Buyers can get a 3-bedroom double-storey home listed for R1.8 million.

These listings mean Lambert’s Bay has the cheapest seaside residences on the West Coast.



Living in Lambert’s Bay

Lambert’s Bay is a 3-hour drive (258 kilometres) from Cape Town via the N7 and R364.

The short distance makes it an easy weekend getaway.

But it could also become a permanent residence.

The town has a primary and high school.

It has a population of 8 911, according to the 2022 census.



Yet life in Lambert’s Bay is quiet.

The town has a small shopping district with a handful of national retailers, including a Spar and OK Foods.

On the last Saturday of every month, the community meets at a farmer’s market opposite Muisbosskerm.



The coastal town is safe.

Crime in the area is declining.

According to the South African Police Service (SAPS), crime dropped 15.5% in the first quarter compared to the same period last year.



A Look at Lambert’s Bay

Lambert’s Bay Harbour. Image: Pexels

Lambert’s Bay Pelicans. Image: Wikimedia Commons
