World.title: ‘Control yourself’ - Pastor Mboro calls on men in fight against GBV
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Pastor Paseka Motsoeneng warns that gender-based violence and femicide have reached a crisis.

Speaking during a GBVF march in Kempton Park, he urged the government to act and called for stronger community safety measures.

“They (Men) should stop being easily provoked. And you need God and the fruits of the spirit.

“No matter how they dress. I saw another woman was wearing shorts. Even if the thighs can shine like that, even if they go naked, control yourself. We don’t even have to put rules about what they must wear and what they must do. If they take their breasts out, no problem. Let’s protect women and fight this thing,” he said.

Motsoeneng said the number of women killed in Ekurhuleni is less than the reality of women dying every day in South Africa.

“These are just the numbers that are discovered in the media. Every week women are dying and some they wake up; their parts are gone. There is also a spiritual thing in this thing.

There are human sacrifices, the blood of the women, their cry and the children. Every time they do this, it extends their power.

Religious leaders in Ekurhuleni joined the growing call to end South Africa’s gender-based violence crisis.

Demonstrators, including civil society and faith groups, gathered at the Kempton Park Civic Centre to demand greater police accountability and action.

The demonstration follows the discovery of at least 11 women’s bodies in Ekurhuleni since July, three of whom remain unidentified.

World.title: Zille launches controversial M1 bridge campaign
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - DA Johannesburg mayoral candidate Helen Zille has sparked controversy with a campaign spotlighting the city’s crumbling bridges.

She staged her warning on a dilapidated stretch of the M1, calling it a potential safety hazard for motorists.

“You can see behind me a bridge that is crumbling and in fact the bridge on the off-ramp is even in worse condition. Now the city has done an audit of bridges about eight years ago in which the audit warned them that the bridges would have to be seen to very quickly because they were rapidly becoming unsafe because of lack of maintenance.

“This is one of them, but there are many others around Joburg. Some are in an even worse condition. In fact, the city's own statistics say that 78 percent of bridges are in need of urgent maintenance and repair. They're either bad or very bad in their condition and this is serious for motorists because they and pedestrians often don't realise the state of the bridges that they drive over and under and that creates a potential hazard.

Johannesburg Metro Police spokesperson Xolani Fihla said the DA would be fined for placing posters on bridges, which is not permitted.

He added JMPD would consult the IEC to explore further action.

“Political parties need to adhere to municipal bylaws.

“We will remove those posters on the bridge. This will definitely be taken forward,” Fihla said.

Zille conceded that the DA did not seek official approval for the event but insisted it’s vital to alert drivers to the risk posed by Johannesburg’s neglected bridges.

“Pointing out to the public that bridges are dangerous is certainly not a gimmick, it's a public service. This is an event organized by the national DA in concert with the provincial DA. We didn't specifically seek permission, but we are warning motorists that this is a very dangerous bridge and that they need to know it.

World.title: ‘Andile Lungisa not entitled to public office’ - ANC
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC said Andile Lungisa, who hopes to become Mayor of Gqeberha, isn’t entitled to public office.

This follows Lungisa’s urgent court bid after the party dropped him from its list of potential councillors.

The High Court in Johannesburg heard the case this week. In a statement, the ANC called the legal fight "sorrowful”.

The party pointed to Lungisa’s criminal record as the key issue.

In 2018, he was sentenced to two years in prison for assaulting DA councillor Rayno Kayser with a jug.

The ANC said this record rules him out of public office.

Judgment has been reserved in the matter.

World.title: Young Men Movement calls for everyday action against GBV
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Young Men Movement founder Kabelo Chabalala has said that inconsistent leadership can undermine the fight against gender-based violence.

He stressed the need for sustained plans and commitments that outlast political changes, urging a year-round focus on GBV.

“I think the biggest challenge in this country is also how we are structuring approaches. A lot of these issues continue to manifest in the different parts of our country also because of the problematic discontinuation of who is in leadership from a political perspective.

“We are heading towards 16 days of activism. We're going to see some talks and a little bit of promises around action, and then we're going to move on into December. We forget that women are being killed every day in this country.

“It's not a Kempton Park problem. It's not a September, October problem. It's an everyday problem that requires us to work around it and around the clock every day without having to pause even for a moment.”

World.title: Gauteng e-panic safety under scrutiny
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Gauteng e-panic button data breach matter will soon be escalated to the Premier's office.

A security flaw that exposes sensitive personal information has caused panic among users.

It seems the app has exposed victims' reports, names, and locations.

The Gauteng Legislature e‑Government Committee said the app is not safe to use.

Committee chairperson Mbali Hlophe said the breach was serious.

“It's very alarming and I must indicate that for us, we are more sensitive because of all the stuff that's taking place on the string of women that have been lost and killed and so forth. So, I mean, you can imagine what this then means, because it means the victims and the perpetrators of them would have access to this.

“We want to have a report on the access logs, so they must be able to indicate from 2024 when this was first launched to date. Two years later, how many people have had access to this? Are there any foreign people that have had access to it? If this student was able to log in, who else could have?

“There could be criminal syndicates who have been viewing all this information throughout. We just need that surety. And it's certainly what society would also want. But in addition to that, because this information has now been exposed, they do need to report it to the information regulator and also to inform the individuals that have utilized this app, especially those whose information has been compromised in line with the POPIA Act, they do need to inform them.

World.title: Love triangle murder ends in life sentence
World.content:
KU GOMPO CITY – The East London Regional Court has sentenced a 30-year-old man to life imprisonment for the murder of a man he believed his girlfriend was cheating with.

Sibusiso Dolongo murdered Siphenathi Gqonono because he thought he was sleeping with his girlfriend.

The court heard that three days before the murder, Dolongo’s girlfriend spent the night at Gqonono’s home after a night out at a local tavern.

When she returned home the following morning, Dolongo told her he had heard at the taxi rank that she had slept with Gqonono. For the next three days, he interrogated and assaulted her.

Although she denied the allegation, Dolongo armed himself with an unknown weapon and instructed her to take him to Gqonono’s home, as he did not know where he lived. When they arrived, Dolongo told her to knock on the door and call Gqonono’s name.

Gqonono came outside and, without saying a word, Dolongo stabbed him eight times before fleeing the scene.

Gqonono’s sister found him outside their home, bleeding profusely. Before he died, he told her that he had opened the door for Dolongo’s girlfriend before he was attacked.

Eastern Cape NPA spokesperson Luxolo Tyali said police investigations led them to the girlfriend and subsequently to Dolongo’s arrest.

“During the trial, Regional Court Prosecutor Thokozani Ndzama presented evidence from the girlfriend, her sister and Gqonono’s sister. Court Preparation Officer (CPO) Maki Mengi supported the witnesses. Dolongo raised an alibi defence and called his other girlfriend as a witness.

“During cross-examination by the State, however, she changed her version, saying she had been coerced and threatened by Dolongo. She told the court that she had not been with him on the night of the murder. The court accepted the material aspects of the State’s case and rejected Dolongo’s alibi.

For sentencing, the State submitted a Victim Impact Statement from Gqonono’s sister, prepared by the CPO, outlining the effect of his death on his family.

“The court agreed with the State that the manner in which the offence was committed demonstrated premeditation and that there were no compelling and substantial circumstances to justify departing from the prescribed minimum sentence.”

The Director of Public Prosecutions in the Eastern Cape, Advocate Samkelo Mtwana, welcomed the sentence and commended all role players whose dedication helped ensure that the perpetrator was held accountable.

“This sentence sends a clear message that those who commit violent crimes and show complete disregard for human life will face the full might of the law,” Mtwana said.

World.title: Eight life terms plus 46 years for Eastern Cape serial rapist
World.content:
MTHATHA - Thabile “Bhino” Nyakiso (32) has been sentenced to eight life terms for a series of rapes committed in Tsolo between 2016 and 2017.

The Mthatha High Court sentenced him to 15 years’ imprisonment for each of the counts of robbery with aggravating circumstances and 12 months’ imprisonment for common robbery.

Acting Judge Fikile Ntayiya recommended that Nyakiso not be considered for parole until he has served 30 years of his sentences.

Evidence presented in court showed that Nyakiso and another unidentified person committed rapes and robberies around Tsolo, targeting women walking at New Homes and Crossbow townships.

Eastern Cape NPA spokesperson Luxolo Tyali said during some of the attacks, Nyakiso robbed victims of money, bank cards and cellphones.

“The victims did not know him. Forensic DNA profiling linked him to swabs collected from them. He had been arrested in connection with a separate rape case in Butterworth, more than 150 kilometres from Tsolo.

“During the trial, Nyakiso pleaded guilty but questioned the DNA evidence's accuracy. State Advocate Avumile Bikitsha called a witness from the National Forensic Laboratory as part of the State’s 45 witnesses,” he said.

The court heard the first victim was a 16-year-old girl who was attacked on 19 June 2016. On 22 July 2016, Nyakiso attacked a 22-year-old woman near the Tsolo Circuit office.

On 18 November 2016, he raped another 16-year-old victim multiple times near New Homes township.

“While giving evidence, she told the court that during the ordeal she asked Nyakiso how he would feel if someone did the same to his sister. This did not stop him from continuing the attack.”

On 27 May 2017, a 26-year-old woman was raped in her rented room at Kobi Flats in Tsolo. On 1 August 2017, Nyakiso raped two victims, aged 29 and 39, on separate occasions. He then attacked an 18-year-old woman near Crossbow Township on 12 August 2017, a 24-year-old woman in the same township on 21 September 2017, and another victim on 6 November 2017, where the 27-year-old was raped in her house in New Homes Township.

“For sentencing, the court agreed with the state’s submission that society did not deserve people like Nyakiso in its midst. The judge noted that Nyakiso, who has another rape case pending before the same court, was inhumane and had shown no remorse for his offences.”

The Director of Public Prosecutions in the Eastern Cape, Advocate Samkelo Mtwana, said the sentence reaffirmed the prosecution’s firm stance against violent crime. He commended the prosecutor and investigating officer for their meticulous collection and presentation of evidence.

World.title: Motsoaledi backs news health DG
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Health Minister, Dr Aaron Motsoaledi has praised the credentials of the department's new director-general, Thembisile Xulu.

She takes the reins from Professor Nicholas Crisp.

Motsoaledi said she has her work cut out for her as the implementation of the National Health Insurance gains momentum.

“We are very excited that we have got the DG, firstly, who is a female, but who is also medically trained as a doctor, but who also worked in several areas, the most recent of which was the CEO of South African National AIDS Council, which, as you know, consists of 18 sectors.

"She's bringing a wealth of experience to the department. Her work is cut out, but generally the most important thing we want her to do is to strengthen the healthcare system, strengthen its infrastructure, make sure that all the posts that are essential and filled up, then it will give us power to move forward on other programs and initiatives."

World.title: Kericho Annex Prison under scrutiny over death of remand prisoner
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Brenda Chemutai, 19, who allegedly committed suicide inside the Kericho Annex Prison where she was awaiting trial for an offence of being in possession of bhang that was seized in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer. [Courtesy]

Questions are mounting over security and accountability at Kericho Annex Prison following the death of a 19-year-old remand prisoner in a suspected case of suicide.

Her family is demanding answers about how she obtained a bedsheet and why they were not notified until nearly 10 hours after the incident.

Brenda Chemutai was reportedly found hanging from a double-decker bed at around 9 am when her fellow cellmates were having breakfast on Friday.

The cell had eight inmates, who had gone for breakfast, according to a police report.

However, her relatives state they were not informed until about 7 pm, after her body had already been taken from the prison and transferred to the Kericho County Hospital Mortuary.

The delay has raised serious concerns for the family, which calls for authorities to clarify what happened between the time Chemutai was discovered and when her next of kin were contacted.

Kericho East Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) officer, Kennedy Apindi, said police have launched investigations following reports from prison officials that the incident was a suicide.

He mentioned that preliminary information indicated Chemutai allegedly used a bedsheet.

The family, however, insists that investigators determine when she was found, who discovered her, when the incident was reported to police, who authorised her body’s removal, and why her relatives were not notified immediately.

“We had spoken with Brenda. She was expected to be released around December, and by January we would all have been together at home,” said her sister, Phyllis Cherotich.

Cherotich added that the family had seen no signs indicating Chemutai intended to take her own life.

"Her death has shocked us deeply. She never mentioned any plans of this nature. We want to understand how this was possible given the level of security at the facility," she said.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged use of a bedsheet have also raised questions for the family.

Her uncle, Michael Rono, questioned how such an item came into Chemutai's possession while she was in a remand facility.

"I am deeply surprised. When one enters the prison, one is carefully searched. Where did the bedsheet come from? We ask the government to ensure justice is done," Rono said.

Chemutai had been in remand since 2024, with her relatives saying she was arrested while still a minor and had spent nearly two years awaiting the conclusion of her case.

She was being tried for the offence of possession of bhang in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer.

Her death has consequently brought renewed scrutiny to not only what happened inside the prison but also the circumstances that led to her prolonged detention.

Youth activists from the Voice of Youth Organisation, led by Kelvin Kipchichir, have joined the family in demanding investigations into both the death and the case that resulted in Chemutai's detention.

Kipchichir claimed Chemutai was arrested alongside other suspects in a vehicle allegedly linked to an Officer Commanding Station serving in Kakamega.

According to the activists, police recovered 32 rolls of bhang from the vehicle, while some of the suspects allegedly fled, leaving Chemutai behind.

The claims have not been independently established.

Kipchichir questioned why Chemutai remained in custody for such a prolonged period and called for scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the vehicle and its alleged connection to the police officer.

“We are concerned that an OCS in the National Police Service could allow a vehicle to be used by an individual with a known criminal record,” he said.

He called on the Ministry of Interior to establish who owned or controlled the vehicle and under what circumstances it was allegedly being used.

The activists said the vehicle was still at Kericho Police Station.

For the family, the tragedy has been compounded by personal loss. Chemutai's father died while she was in remand, while she leaves behind a young child.

Relatives said detectives had informed them that the person alleged to own the bhang had since been arrested and was being held in Kisumu.

But the immediate question for Chemutai's family is what happened during her final hours.

They want a clear account of the period between the reported discovery of her body at about 9 am and the notification of the family nearly 10 hours later.

They also want investigators to establish how the bedsheet allegedly used in the incident came into her possession and whether prison officers followed all required procedures after she was found.

The activists are calling for the inquiry to extend beyond the death of Chemutai to her arrest, the length of her detention and the handling of the case against her.

The family has demanded a transparent and independent investigation, saying it wants answers on how a teenager who entered the justice system while still a minor ended up dead in remand custody.

The family says it wants those questions answered before proceeding with burial arrangements.

World.title: Pregnant woman found dead by roadside in Kirinyaga with head, hip injuries
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The National Police Service (NPS) has launched investigations after the body of a pregnant woman was found by the roadside in the Itangi area of Mwea East Sub-County, Kirinyaga County.

The woman, identified as Catherine Njeru, was found early Friday morning along the Piai-Itangi Murram Road with visible injuries to her head and hip.

In a statement, NPS said the incident is being investigated as a suspected murder.

"The NPS condoles with the family, relatives, and friends of the deceased and commits to expeditious and conclusive investigations to ensure that any person or persons responsible for this barbaric crime are brought to justice," read the statement.

Police have urged residents of Itangi to remain calm and refrain from speculation as the investigation continues.

Anyone with information that could assist the investigation has been asked to report to the nearest police station or a law enforcement officer.

The matter is being investigated by Kirinyaga County Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) officers, local Sub-County police and Central Regional Police Command, led by the Regional Criminal Investigations Officer.

According to NPS, the Inspector General of the National Police Service has also been briefed on the incident and directed the Director of Criminal Investigations to expedite the probe and establish the facts surrounding the woman's death.

World.title: Ruto downplays rivalry over oil refinery in East Africa
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Nigeria President Olesugun Obasanjo, Ali Dangote, President William Ruto and Uganda President Yoweri Museveni during launch of the Lamu Refinery on September 30, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has played down suggestions of rivalry between Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania over competing refinery projects, saying East Africa’s growing demand for petroleum products can support several facilities across the region.

Speaking during a media interview at State House Mombasa, Ruto said Kenya had no objection to Uganda and Tanzania pursuing their own refinery projects, arguing that the different facilities could complement rather than compete with one another.

“There is no bad blood at all. There is no problem,” Ruto said.

His remarks came a day after he presided over the groundbreaking of the Lamu refinery project, which the government is positioning as a major component of a wider industrial complex on the Kenyan coast.

Ruto said he had discussed Uganda’s plans with President Yoweri Museveni and agreed that Kampala could proceed with a smaller refinery without threatening Kenya’s investment in Lamu.

He said Kenya would even be prepared to buy petroleum products from Uganda if they could reach the Kenyan market at competitive prices.

“If it is manufactured there in Uganda and the oil from that place is near Busia, and it can reach Busia at a lower price, we will buy oil from anywhere and bring it to Busia,” Ruto said.

The President argued that the size of the regional petroleum market meant there was room for more than one refinery.

“This one in Lamu cannot serve all of us; it will be necessary to expand,” he said, adding that East Africa had “enough opportunity” for multiple facilities.

Ruto also extended the same approach to Tanzania, saying Kenya could participate in a refinery project in Tanga if it is eventually developed.

“Even if the one in Tanga is built, we as Kenya will go and buy some shares there. There is no problem,” he said.

The comments point to a regional energy market in which petroleum products could move across borders depending on availability, transport costs and prices. Rather than treating refinery projects as competing national investments, Ruto said the facilities could strengthen economic cooperation within the East African Community.

The President said the Lamu refinery would also address some of the challenges Kenya faces from dependence on imported refined petroleum products.

“Lamu will give us an opportunity to have fuel without the fluctuations that we have now,” he said.

He linked the proposed refinery to the need to reduce Kenya’s exposure to international oil price shocks, disruptions caused by instability in oil-producing regions and costs associated with transporting petroleum products over long distances.

Ruto said local refining could reduce expenses related to insurance and transportation while providing Kenya with greater access to locally processed fuel.

However, he said the larger economic opportunity would extend beyond the refinery itself. The government plans to develop industries around the facility, including petrochemical, chemical and plastics manufacturing.

The refinery could also provide raw materials for industries producing fertiliser and bitumen, potentially reducing reliance on imports of some petroleum-based products.

The broader development is expected to create opportunities for employment, investment and trade while strengthening Lamu’s position as an industrial and logistics centre.

Ruto said Kenya’s policy would be guided by competitiveness, allowing businesses and consumers to obtain petroleum products from whichever regional facility can supply them efficiently and at favourable prices.

The President maintained that Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania therefore did not need to view their refinery plans through the lens of rivalry.

Instead, he said, multiple facilities could create a larger and more integrated petroleum market capable of serving the needs of East Africa.

World.title: Outrage as KDF officers detain human rights team along Malindi-Lamu highway
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Activists clashed with police at a Gamba roadblock after being stopped en route to Lamu. [Vocal Africa]

Six members of Muslims for Human Rights (MUHURI), including five staff and a board member, were detained by Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) officers along the Malindi-Lamu highway, prompting condemnation from human rights organisations.

The incident occurred on Monday as the team travelled from Lamu to Mombasa after a field mission. The officers reportedly intercepted them between Gamba and Minjila, detained them for about two hours, then released them.

The Kenya Human Rights Commission (KHRC) and MUHURI said the officers covered their faces and refused to identify themselves when the human rights team challenged them.

The five staff members were identified as Francis Auma, Abdulrahman Mwanga, Fredrick Okado, Lathan Yusuf and Mohamed Abdla, while the board member was identified as Khelef Khalifa.

In a joint statement, the two organisations said the officers' actions violated a High Court ruling by Justice Bahati Mwamuye requiring security personnel to wear clearly visible name tags or identifiable service numbers on their uniforms.

The ruling also prohibits security officers from wearing hoods, balaclavas or face masks to conceal their identities.

"We call on the KDF and other security agencies to comply with the court order. Officers who violate the directive should be held accountable and face legal consequences," the joint statement read in part.

The organisations also demanded immediate compliance with a recent court order lifting the dusk-to-dawn curfew that had been imposed for more than a decade along the Minjila-Lamu highway.

They argued that the curfew had created conditions for arbitrary stops, harassment and detention of travellers using the route, citing the detention of the MUHURI team as an example.

The organisations urged security agencies to respect court orders and protect the rights of travellers using the highway.

However, a senior Anti-Terror Police officer aware of the incident told The Standard that the officers from the Border Police Unit (BPU) manning such roadblocks and tactical borders conceal their faces to protect their identities.

"In high-risk areas prone to insurgent or terrorist retaliation, including Kanyoyo in Kitui heading to Garissa, Moyale and Lamu, anonymity is framed as a matter of personal and operational survival," she stated.

World.title: Kalonzo signals at working with Ruto if 2027 poll is free and fair
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County on September 27, 2026. [Clinton Ambujo, Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has signalled that the Opposition could accept the outcome of the 2027 General Election and consider working with President William Ruto if he wins through a free and fair contest.

Speaking at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County, Kalonzo said the political class must commit itself to democratic competition and be prepared to accept the verdict of voters.

“If you beat us, we will have to consider if you have behaved yourself, and if we beat you, we have to look at all these things,” he said.

The Wiper leader also called for stronger democratic institutions, warning against political confrontation that could deepen divisions in the country.

“We have a nation here. We have to make this country truly democratic. I do not think we have a shortcut,” he said.

Kalonzo used the church service to make a broader appeal for a united and effective Opposition, saying political leaders had a responsibility to work together in the national interest.

“Kenya needs a functional official opposition; one that is united and does not thrive on disunity. As leaders, we have a responsibility to work together and play our part in fixing this nation,” he said.

He said he had remained in the Opposition even when some political allies moved into government.

“I have stood in the opposition all these years. Even when others joined government, my brother Eugene Wamalwa and I remained steadfast, and we will continue to stand firm,” he said.

Kalonzo also turned his attention to Parliament, claiming that the National Assembly had been “captured” and challenging lawmakers in both Houses to exercise their constitutional responsibilities.

“The National Assembly has been captured. Let this message reach every leader in the National Assembly and the Senate: you have the power to change things, not just to complain later,” he said.

He urged legislators to defend the interests of the people who elected them and to put the country ahead of political considerations.

The former Vice President also defended retired President Uhuru Kenyatta against claims that he is financing the Opposition ahead of the 2027 contest.

Kalonzo argued that presidential campaigns have historically relied on networks of political allies and supporters rather than family resources alone.

“But here we are saying, please let Uhuru rest; he is a retired President. Stop saying he is our financier,” he said.

Kalonzo cited previous presidential campaigns involving Uhuru, former President Mwai Kibaki and Raila Odinga, arguing that major political campaigns require support from friends and associates.

“Even when Uhuru was running for President, or Kibaki and even Raila, no family has enough resources to support a presidential campaign. It is friends who support you,” he said.

He warned that Kenya was at a delicate political moment and urged leaders to avoid actions that could deepen instability.

“We should not allow the country to get to a worse situation than where it is. We are on the edge of a cliff; the country is at a crossroads,” he said.

World.title: ODM delegates reject Sakaja using the party for gubernatorial bid
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi ODM chairman George Aladwa addressing the media over the upcoming ODM nominations in Nairobi. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Nairobi ODM delegates have resolved to reject and lobby against attempts by some people in President William Ruto's broad-based government to give Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja the ODM ticket in the 2027 gubernatorial race.

Party members, delegates and branch chairpersons met in Makadara, where they agreed that ODM be allowed to field their own candidates instead of the party allowing UDA leaders to vie on the party ticket.

They also resolved to back Makadara MP George Aladwa. With Tutam songs renting the air during the meeting, they also agreed to back President Ruto's re-election.

"Aladwa should be the party's candidate for Nairobi governor, and every candidate should seek the seat through their own political party," said an agitated delegate from Kasarani.

They insisted ODM should not allow an outsider to join the party and use its ticket to contest for the gubernatorial seat, arguing that the ODM ticket should be reserved for a candidate who enjoys the support of its members.

"We will not allow someone from another party to come and vie using ODM while we have our own members. As a party our only candidate is Aladwa," said delegate chairs.

They added that their position follows a series of meetings held across all 17 constituencies in Nairobi, with Makadara being the final constituency to hold its meeting.

They further argued that the Nairobi gubernatorial seat requires a leader with experience and leadership skills, warning ODM members against supporting candidates they believe lack the necessary political and leadership experience.

They also sustained their criticism towards former president Uhuru, alleging that he is undermining the party and dividing it, and they will not allow it.

George Aladwa backed the ODM members' position, saying every politician seeking elective office should do so through their own political party.

The delegates maintained that ODM should protect its identity and ticket, insisting that candidates from outside the party should not be allowed to use the ODM ticket to pursue elective positions when active and loyal members are sidelined.

The delegates are calling on ODM to ensure that the nomination process is free, fair and transparent, giving party members an opportunity to choose the candidate they want to represent them.

World.title: Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya's first commercial drilling
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya’s first commercial drilling. [Courtes]

Kenya has moved closer to commercial oil production after a 1,500 horsepower drilling rig arrived at the Port of Mombasa ahead of its deployment to the South Lokichar Basin in Turkana County.

The GW70 rig, leased by Gulf Energy E&P BV from Great Wall Drilling Company, docked at Kilindini Port on Friday aboard MV Transit Sedanka after sailing from Duqm Port in Oman.

It is expected to be transported to Turkana, where drilling is scheduled to begin on November 1.

“All workstreams at Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ are running to a tight project management schedule, and the project remains on course for First Oil production in December 2026,” Gulf Energy Chief Executive Officer Paul Limoh said.

The arrival marks a step in the commercial development of the South Lokichar Basin, more than a decade after oil was first discovered in Turkana in 2012.

The first phase of the project is expected to produce about 20,000 barrels of crude oil per day, with output projected to rise to 50,000 barrels per day in the second phase.

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) says Kenya is targeting first oil in December 2026, while the first crude exports through the Port of Mombasa are expected in the first quarter of 2027.

The GW70 will undergo commissioning and acceptance checks before drilling begins. Gulf Energy has contracted Baker Hughes for integrated well services and SLB to provide an early production facility for the first phase.

World.title: Two more suspects arrested over lawyer Kyalo Mbobu murder
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads.

Detectives have arrested two more suspects in connection with the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu, as an intelligence-led operation targeting people linked to the September 9, 2025 murder intensifies.

The two boda boda riders Nicholas Lemiso Naula and Noah Kipkirui Langat were arrested in Nairobi’s Central Business District, following sustained efforts by detectives to trace individuals suspected to have been involved in the killing.

According to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Lemiso is a boda boda rider who allegedly ferried the main suspect, Police Constable Julius Cheruiyot, to and from the scene of the murder, while Langat was arrested over alleged surveillance on Mbobu before his killing.

"With three suspects now in custody, detectives are intensifying the hunt for other persons suspected to have played a role in the meticulously planned killing," DCI stated.

His arrest comes shortly after detectives arrested Cheruiyot in connection with the killing.

“The dragnet over the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu has widened, with detectives arresting a second suspect as an intelligence-led operation targeting persons linked to the murder intensifies,” DCI said.

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads and seek to identify and arrest other people who may have been involved. The DCI said the operation remains active as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding Mbobu’s murder.

“The DCI is leaving no stone unturned in its efforts to unravel the full circumstances surrounding Lawyer Mbobu’s murder and bring all those responsible to justice,” the agency said.

World.title: Anthropic says its AI models pose ‘existential risk to humanity’ in leaked IPO filing: report
World.content:
Anthropic says its AI models could pose a “catastrophic or existential risk to humanity” and can “resist shutdown,” according to an initial public offering prospectus obtained by Reuters.

Anthropic is pursuing an IPO some time in the next year that many expect to value the five-year-old company at approximately $2 trillion. The company’s Wall Street debut will follow a June public offering by SpaceX, which owed much of its $2 trillion opening day valuation to its own AI efforts. OpenAI, the other leading American AI company, has announced plans for its own public offering.

The Anthropic IPO could raise tens of billions of dollars for the cash-hungry company. But the company behind Claude also warned in the prospectus that its AI models can have “self-preserving behaviors” and have attempted to “conceal or manipulate information” and engaged in behavior “resembling blackmail” according to the report.

The run of AI public offerings not only gives individual and institutional investors a chance to cash in on the AI boom, but also provides more transparency about their businesses. Yet the IPOs come amid growing concerns about AI’s advancement and capabilities.

An AI agent from OpenAI, Anthropic’s chief rival, broke into an Australian healthcare database, the country’s prime minister revealed last week. OpenAI also disclosed Friday that its agents probed three US government websites without authorization, but in that case did not obtain non-public data.

In a prospectus, companies typically offer investors lists of risks they face, such as lawsuits and competitive pressures, when laying out the case for investing in the company. But the hazards are never this stark. Anthropic dedicated 80 pages to its risk factors in the leaked prospectus, significantly more than the 48 pages it spent detailing its business, according to Reuters.

Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment from CNN.

The prospectus is likely to feed growing concerns about the risks posed to humanity by AI. Earlier this month, former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon received widespread attention when he left the company and posted on X that “the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

Anthropic is one of the leading companies in AI development, and its CEO Dario Amodei responded to Coxon’s post with a 3,800 word essay calling for a slowdown and guardrails on the development of AI. He also told CNN’s Anderson Cooper that he agreed with Coxon more than he disagreed. Amodei wrote in his essay that the risks are serious, even if the benefits could change humanity for the better.

Some in the industry, however, including the CEO of Hugging Face, which was breached by OpenAI’s AI models when they acted without authorization during a test, believe the fears are overblown.

President Donald Trump is set to meet with executives from the industry Tuesday, including Amodei, in a summit aimed at coming to a consensus in the industry. Trump has repeatedly resisted calls to regulate AI and has dismissed concerns as a “hoax.”

AI giants need to raise a great amount of money to fund their costly development plans, and the massive amount of AI spending among big tech companies on computing infrastructure and talent has sent jitters through Wall Street.

The leaked Anthropic IPO filing sheds light on its financials, revealing that the company lost $42 billion in 2025, according to Reuters. The company plans to spend $518 billion on cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in coming year, and said that nearly a quarter of its revenue last year came from two customers.

Anthropic was last valued at $965 billion in May.

World.title: Terrorist images found on Flydubai suspect’s social media
World.content:
The pilot suspected of having attacked another pilot aboard a Tel Aviv-bound Flydubai flight on Wednesday was removed from a previous job at Oman’s national airline last year following concerns about his extremist views, two sources familiar with the matter told CNN.

The pilot is an Omani citizen named Hamam al-Hammami, according to the two sources and an Israeli official. Saudi state media also identified al-Hammami. He was born in the United Arab Emirates to an Omani father and Syrian mother and has spent several years of his life in the UAE, one of the sources added.

A LinkedIn profile bearing the name Hamam al-Hammami said he worked at Oman Air for seven years, leaving in February 2025, before joining Royal Air Maroc in June 2025 and departing in January 2026. The page made no mention of Flydubai. One of the sources confirmed that the profile belongs to the Flydubai pilot in Wednesday’s incident. The profile has since been deleted and CNN has reached out to LinkedIn for comment.

The second source, a diplomat from the region, told CNN the suspect was removed from flight training because of the concerns over his radical views and was given another role at Oman’s national airline.

On Thursday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the suspect was believed to have undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination.”

The Israeli official told CNN that al-Hammami had worked for Flydubai for only eight months. A fourth source said the alleged assailant had previously worked for Royal Air Maroc.

The revelations will raise concerns about the importance of background checks in aviation hiring. CNN has reached out to Oman Air, Royal Air Maroc and the Dubai government’s media office for comment.

Flydubai said it could not provide comment while the incident remained under investigation.

Threatening mutilation and death

Only two posts were made to the LinkedIn profile, and both were published in quick succession on Wednesday, about nine hours after the incident.

It is unclear who published the posts or whether they were scheduled in advance.

The first post featured a series of clips filmed in the cockpits of a Boeing 737 Max aircraft. The aircraft that diverted to Saudi Arabia in Wednesday’s incident was a Flydubai 737 Max 8.

In one clip, which CNN geolocated to Dubai International Airport, the person filming zooms in on a plane that belongs to the Israeli airline El Al.

In the video, the cockpit screen showed the flight number – OMA624 – and date, October 11, 2023. The flight number corresponds to a flight that typically travels from Dubai to Muscat. The date matches the period of time he worked at Oman Air.

In other clips in the video, more planes from El Al, as well as one from Arkia, another Israeli airline, are shown.

The video ends with a photo of Ayman al-Zawahiri, who led al Qaeda after the death of Osama Bin Laden, and a photo of Humam Khalil Abu-Mulal al-Balawi, who killed nine people, including seven American CIA officers and contractors, in a 2009 suicide bombing, and was loyal to al Qaeda.

The second post features an AI-generated image depicting Islam’s three holiest sites – in Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem – linked by a continuous glowing trail. A defiant poem recited in the background speaks of rejecting humiliation, not fearing death and defending one’s dignity.

Al-Hammami’s LinkedIn page said he studied at Buckinghamshire New University in England. A source at the university confirmed to CNN that a man by that name had completed a three-year distance learning course, graduating with a degree in aviation management in 2023.

The same two videos were posted around the same time on an Instagram account bearing the same name and pictures, before that account was also deleted. CNN has reached out to Meta for comment.

Passengers who were on the Flydubai aircraft bound for Israel from the UAE are greeted by friends and family as they arrive at Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv on September 30. Ammar Awad/Reuters

‘Ruined women’

A CNN analysis of al-Hammami’s deleted Twitter account shows him as deeply religious and misogynistic.

In deleted posts, al-Hammami discussed the difficulties his mother faced in finding him a prospective wife who would accept his conditions that she wear a niqab, a face covering, and stop working after marriage.

“They all refused. Then my mother told them, ‘My son is a pilot,’ and they all suddenly agreed,” the post from February 2022 said.

The posts also railed against mixed-gender workplaces, saying they had a corrupting effect on women.

“How many respectable, religious girls have been ruined in mixed-gender work environments and manipulated?” a post from January 2022 said.

The nearly 3,000 deleted tweets, published between 2021 and 2022, were analyzed and sorted using an AI-powered semantic search model.

Questions are mounting over how a citizen of Oman, which does not recognize Israel, was permitted to serve as a pilot on a flight to Tel Aviv, despite Israel’s stringent aviation security measures.

An Israeli official told CNN on Wednesday that several Israeli agencies – including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the Transportation Ministry – were investigating how the Omani pilot came to be part of the flight crew.

The pilot attempted to carry out a “terrorist act” by attacking his colleague with a crash axe inside the cockpit and trying to take control of the plane, the United Arab Emirates attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said on Saturday, according to state news agency WAM.

UAE authorities have jurisdiction to investigate the incident because the aircraft is registered in the country, and UAE law applies to crimes committed aboard its planes even when they occur outside the country’s territory, WAM said.

Netanyahu told CNN’s Jim Sciutto late on Wednesday that the assailant had been interrogated in Saudi Arabia, where the plane was diverted, with Israel involved in the investigation.

“I spoke to the president of the United Arab Emirates, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed, and he agreed that Israel would join the interrogations,” he said.

CNN’s Jeremy Diamond, Mostafa Salem, Andrew Carey and Billy Stockwell contributed to this article.

World.title: Netanyahu shared new intelligence on Iran’s nuclear ambitions with UAE leader, source says
World.content:
Jerusalem —

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu showed UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed new Israeli intelligence indicating Iran is resuming progress on its nuclear program during a visit to the country on Sunday, an Israeli source with knowledge of the meeting told CNN.

Among the information shared by Netanyahu were details of new construction at the Pickaxe mountain site — about 140 miles south of the capital Tehran — seen as a key location for possible Iranian efforts to rebuild its nuclear program.

On Sunday, an Israeli source familiar with the visit told CNN that the unannounced meeting was dominated by discussion of Iran, an arena where the two countries have deepened their cooperation, including during the current Iran war.

WAM, the UAE’s state news agency, confirmed that Sheikh Mohammed and Netanyahu held a meeting in the country, marking the first time the Emiratis publicly acknowledged a visit by Netanyahu.

The two leaders “discussed bilateral relations between the UAE and Israel and ways to strengthen and further develop them,” WAM reported.

The Israeli Prime Minister’s office said that the meeting focused on “strengthening relations between the two countries and regional challenges.”

The visit included Netanyahu’s wife, the head of the National Security Council, the head of the Mossad, a military secretary, and a political adviser, the office said.

The meeting was also attended by a senior Saudi security official, two sources with knowledge of the visit told CNN. According to one source, the talks also discussed recent regional developments, including the Houthi militia in Yemen, the vital Bab al-Mandeb waterway at the mouth of the Red Sea, as well as the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi officials have denied anyone attended the meeting.

The source added that Netanyahu told the meeting that Israel assesses Iran could initiate an attack in the region in the coming weeks.

The rare trip came exactly one month before Israel’s October 27 election and against the backdrop of heightened political controversy in Israel over reporting by Haaretz and The New York Times alleging that Sheikh Mohammed had warned Netanyahu of a major Hamas operation days before the October 7, 2023, attack.

The Atlantic separately reported that Egypt’s intelligence chief Abbas Kamel flew to Israel on September 26, 2023, to warn that Gaza would “blow up.” And on Sunday, The Wall Street Journal reported that there were at least three Egyptian warnings conveyed to Israel about Gaza, the last one in a phone call to Netanyahu, just days before the attack.

‘Hostile states’

Netanyahu has repeatedly denied receiving any warning and has dismissed the reports as fabricated lies meant to damage him electorally.

“I never met or spoke to the Egyptian intel chief before Oct. 7, no warning was conveyed to me,” the prime minister posted on X on Monday. “Foreign and hostile states and actors including Arab states are behind the false blood libels.”

But his rivals have used the allegations to make accountability for the failure to prevent the October 7, 2023, attack a central campaign issue.

People walk past a television channel  featuring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, right, and his main rival, opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot, ahead of Israel’s general election, in Ramat Gan, Israel, on Wednesday. Oded Balilty/AP

After initial reports of a warning from Sheikh Mohammed, the UAE’s Foreign Ministry said earlier this month that it “does not comment on media stories or speculation regarding conversations between government leaders,” but it did not deny the call. “When necessary, all relevant intelligence has been and continues to be communicated between the relevant entities,” the statement said.

At the time, an Israeli source familiar with the matter said Netanyahu’s office tried to get the UAE to deny the report, but the UAE only agreed to issue a statement about intelligence sharing.

Netanyahu’s Likud party subsequently issued a statement, posted on the prime minister’s X account, alleging “blatant foreign interference” in Israel’s elections by UAE-based Palestinian politician Mohammed Dahlan. The party provided no evidence for the claim.

Neither Israel nor the UAE mentioned the reported October 7 warning in their Monday statements about Netanyahu’s trip.

Netanyahu’s rivals, meanwhile, have seized on the reported warning to renew their attacks on his handling of the events leading up to October 7.

Gadi Eizenkot, currently polling as the prime minister’s main challenger in Israel’s upcoming elections, said Saturday that the revelation about the warning “leaves no room for doubt: Netanyahu led, with blindness, arrogance and irresponsibility, the State of Israel to the greatest disaster in its history.”

In May, Netanyahu’s office said the prime minister had secretly visited the UAE in March, during the early days of the Iran war, calling it a “historic breakthrough.” The UAE foreign ministry, however, denied his claim at the time as “completely unfounded.”

During the war, Israel is also said to have deployed an Iron Dome missile defense system to the UAE and Israeli officials have said security cooperation between the two countries reached unprecedented levels.

CNN Eyad Kourdi contributed to this report.

World.title: UK charges 2 Iranian men over alleged Yom Kippur terror plot in Manchester
World.content:
Two Iranian men have been charged with terror offenses over an alleged plot to attack the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the latest in a wave of antisemitic attacks in the UK this year.

London’s Metropolitan police named the suspects as 36-year-old Salam Ahmadyan of Liverpool and 34-year-old Rahman Salehi of Salford, who were arrested on September 20, on the eve of the holiest day in Judaism, a year after a deadly synagogue attack in Manchester. They were charged on Friday with “engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts,” police said.

Authorities also said the two men are allegedly in contact with a third person who may be in Iran in relation to the alleged plot.

“These are extremely serious charges and allegations and have come about from a joint CTP (Counter Terror Policing) investigation, working closely with our partners in the security services,” said Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, Senior National Coordinator for CTP.

Evans said the investigation helped disrupt what is believed to have been a plot targeting the Jewish community, but that authorities do not believe there to be an ongoing threat to the public related to the attempted attack.

The charges come a year after a deadly car ramming and stabbing attack outside a Manchester synagogue killed at least two people. They also come just a day after another Iranian national with dual British citizenship was arrested on suspicion of terror offenses linked to an alleged plot to target a UK airbase used by the US military in Fairford, western England.

A person lays flowers at the scene outside the Manchester synagogue, on October 3, 2025, where multiple people were killed on Yom Kippur in what police have declared a terrorist incident, in north Manchester. Phil Noble/Reuters

The 25-year-old was arrested in Westminster, London, after UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there are “strong indications” Iran was involved in the incident – something the Iranian government has denied.

Authorities have said the airbase incident is not believed to be connected with the latest attempted attack on Manchester’s Jewish community.

“This week also brought into sharp focus some of the wider threats being projected into the UK from Iran,” Evans said. “While this incident and the investigation into the RAF Fairford incident are not connected in any way, I want to reassure the public that CTP, working with our national security partners, are using the full range of our capabilities to protect the UK from any hostile acts.”

The UK has seen a wave of antisemitic attacks this year, including assaults on synagogues and other communal buildings. The British government subsequently announced extra police forces to protect Jewish areas across the country.

“We know how concerning this news will be to Jewish communities in Greater Manchester, and beyond,” Greater Manchester Police Deputy Chief Constable Terry Woods said. “We know this is particularly acute on the calendar anniversary of last year’s terrorist atrocity at the Heaton Park synagogue, and during the Jewish High Holy Days.”

Woods said the “ongoing and robust” policing plans across Jewish communities would remain in place as authorities work closely with community leaders and British Counter-Terrorism Police.

World.title: Karim Abdel-Aziz and Yasmine Sabri celebrate premiere of “Matloub A’iliyan” in Dubai
World.content:
The cast and crew of the film “Matloub A’iliyan” (Family Wanted) celebrated its premiere in Dubai ahead of its theatrical release in Egypt on October 7 and in the Gulf region on October 8.

The event was attended by the film’s stars – Karim Abdel-Aziz, Yasmine Sabri, and Mostafa Khater.

The film is a comedy-thriller centering on an Interpol agent who undertakes a complex joint mission with a female colleague.

The cast also includes Sarah Baraka, and Sami Maghawry, alongside several other actors and guest stars, such as Ahmed Fahmy and Nesreen Amin.

The film is written by Sherif al-Leithy, directed by Moataz al-Touny, and produced by Synergy Plus (producer Tamer Mursi).

World.title: When does Winter Time 2026 begin in Egypt?
World.content:
As October draws to a close, interest has risen regarding date of the clock change in Egypt for 2026—specifically, when Daylight Saving Time ends and Winter Time begins.

Winter Time 2026

Daylight Savings Time began on Friday, April 24 pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 24 of 2023 regarding the Daylight Saving Time system.

When are clocks set back by 60 minutes?

In Egypt, the transition from Daylight Saving Time to winter time is scheduled—in accordance with the law—for the end of the last Thursday in October.

Upon the switch to winter time, clocks are set back by 60 minutes, reverting to standard time from the daylight saving time observed previously, during which clocks had been advanced by one hour.

For mobile phones, the clock can be set automatically by accessing the settings, selecting “Date & Time,” and enabling the automatic date and time setting feature.

If the clock does not update automatically, the user can check the time zone settings, ensure that automatic updates are enabled, and adjust the clock following the switch to winter time.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Egyptian, Italian special forces conduct joint training exercise
World.content:
Egyptian Thunderbolt Forces and the Italian Special Forces conducted a joint training exercise, codenamed (4IT-EGY-T-), as part of the Armed Forces’ efforts to strengthen military cooperation with their counterparts in brotherly and friendly countries. The exercise lasted several days and was held in Italy.

The activities included a number of tactical and specialized exercises, including training on safe movement techniques in mountainous areas and dealing with rugged geographical terrain, as well as training in mountain-climbing skills and rapid descent from elevated areas in unusual environments and weather conditions.

The training also covered first-aid and medical evacuation procedures in various emergencies.

The exercise aims to exchange expertise, hone the combat and specialized skills of the participating personnel, and enhance their levels of efficiency and readiness to carry out special-skills missions effectively and proficiently.

World.title: US aircraft carrier en route to the Middle East – what is Trump planning?
World.content:
The Wall Street Journal reported that the US Department of Defense has deployed the aircraft carrier Theodore Roosevelt and its strike group to the Middle East, at a time when US President Donald Trump is hinting at intensifying strikes against Iran following the midterm elections.

The newspaper revealed that the carrier and its strike group—carrying approximately10,000 troops—departed San Diego on Sunday.

The group is sailing toward the region to join the aircraft carriers George H.W. Bush and George Washington, which are already stationed there.

Replacement

Political science professor Areej Gabr said that the deployment of this aircraft carrier to the Middle East is intended to replace another carrier whose mission has concluded.

Speaking on the Al-Qahera News channel, Gabr explained that the move also serves to signal an increased military buildup in Iran’s vicinity and demonstrates full American army readiness, suggesting that the US is on the verge of resuming military confrontation.

Regarding US capabilities, she added that the military currently requires a higher level of readiness—particularly concerning interceptor missiles—meaning this period can be viewed as a preparatory phase leading up to the post-midterm election period.

Gabr noted that, regardless of the election results, a military campaign is likely to take place—possibly early next year—to align weather conditions with specific weather-dependent military objectives.

She said that this situation also reveals the US has suffered a setback on the diplomatic front.

World.title: SN Brussels Travelers from Liberia, Sierra Leone Face Tougher Scrutiny as Europe Hunts ‘Bolle Jos’
World.content:
MONROVIA – For many Liberian and Sierra Leonean families, the SN Brussels flight is more than a ticket. Brussels Airlines, still called “SN” by most travelers here after the carrier it succeeded in 2007, is the plane that brings a mother home for Christmas, carries a student to a European campus and returns a trader with goods for a Waterside shop.

By Rodney D. Sieh, [email protected]

It is also, investigators in Monrovia and Brussels now say, a route drug networks have tried to exploit.



Caught at the carousel

On July 31, Belgian customs officers were checking passengers off a Brussels Airlines flight from Freetown when they stopped a 22-year-old woman from Anderlecht, according to the Halle-Vilvoorde prosecutor’s office and Belgian media. Her two suitcases held 51 kilograms of cocaine.

She had not been on the plane. Investigators believe she was sent only to collect the bags and are still trying to establish how she got into the baggage reclaim hall. A judge later moved her from detention to electronic monitoring.

Weeks earlier at Roberts International Airport (RIA), Liberian security officers flagged six cargo boxes labeled as Maggi cubes and lappa. Inside were 198 compressed plates of cocaine. The Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA) said at the time the shipment, valued at US$19.2 million, was bound for Brussels Airlines’ Europe-bound operations. A Justice Ministry charge sheet later listed London as the final destination.

This week, those two scenes met in a single policy fight in Europe. And the people likely to feel it first are not the kingpins, but honest passengers queuing at RIA and Lungi.

‘Chubby Jos’ next door

The man at the center of Europe’s anger lives one border away. Jos Leijdekkers, known in the Netherlands as “Bolle Jos” (Chubby Jos), is that country’s most wanted criminal. Dutch media placed him in Sierra Leone in early 2025.

In the Netherlands he was sentenced to 24 years in prison for cocaine trafficking and an attempted assassination. In Belgium, his sentences across several cases total more than 100 years, Dutch public broadcaster NOS reported. In May, a court in Dendermonde, Belgium, sentenced him in absentia to eight years for his role in moving 11 tonnes of cocaine from Sierra Leone to the Port of Antwerp in October 2023, hidden in palm kernel meal. Twenty accomplices were also convicted.

The Economist’s 1843 magazine reported on September 18 that he lived in Sierra Leone under the name “Omar Sheriff,” posed as a wealthy investor and kept bodyguards from Ghana and South Africa.

Dutch media have reported that he has a relationship, and a child, with a daughter of President Julius Maada Bio. FrontPageAfrica has not independently confirmed this.

No treaty, no handover

The Netherlands and Sierra Leone have no extradition treaty. The Dutch formally delivered an extradition request anyway, and Freetown has yet to sign off on it. Van Weel said in June that Sierra Leone keeps telling him the procedures are under way.

That patience has run out. On X on Thursday morning, Van Weel announced that “the EU will no longer provide budget support to the authorities of Sierra Leone this year.” He told the Dutch daily De Telegraaf a day earlier that the suspension, about €18 million for 2026, was because Sierra Leone is not cooperating on the extradition. The Netherlands also wants a planned €22.5 million for next year held back.

The freeze hits money paid straight into the state budget. Development and humanitarian aid are excluded, so Europe is aiming at the government, not at Sierra Leoneans in need. Van Weel has called it bizarre that Europe should support a country sheltering one of the world’s biggest drug criminals.

Speaking to NOS in Luxembourg on Thursday, Van Weel welcomed the Commission’s decision. “It sends a very clear signal from the European Commission that Sierra Leone must stop harboring this criminal,” he said.

Asked whether the measure was too harsh on an impoverished country, Van Weel turned the question back on its government. Leijdekkers, he said, causes “immense destruction, including for the people of Sierra Leone.”

“They could resolve this within 24 hours by arresting and extraditing this man,” he said.

If the aid freeze does not work, Van Weel warned, “we will continue to increase the pressure through other channels.” He added: “We are fully committed to bringing this criminal to the Netherlands.”

The Dutch have also worked through Sierra Leone’s neighbors. Van Weel told De Telegraaf in July that Liberia and Ghana are aware of the risks and frustrated by Freetown’s refusal to act.

Ghana has already moved. In September, its Narcotics Control Commission arrested three men accused of representing Leijdekkers’ network there, after French customs seized nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine in Dunkirk. The drugs, valued at about €225 million, were hidden in a container of plastic waste shipped from Ghana.

The Economist estimates about a third of the cocaine reaching Europe now passes through West Africa. Liberia is on its route map.

Liberia’s own test

Liberia’s record this year shows how close the trade has come to home.

Police charged five men and the cargo firm Global Logistics Services (GLS) on July 4 over the June RIA seizure of about 237.6 kilograms. Among them was Michael U.S. Browne, whose release from prison after a 2024 drug charge the Senate has ordered investigated.

Prosecutors allege GLS operations manager Paul Jamaal King organized the shipment and then tried to recover it after it was flagged, including by offering money to airport security. King has pleaded not guilty and is presumed innocent. In July, the Monrovia City Court found probable cause and sent him and six co-defendants to Criminal Court “C” for trial. Days later, the case appeared stalled because certified records had not reached the court.

Investigators followed the airport leads to the VOA community on the RIA Highway. On July 22, joint security forces arrested two foreign nationals and uncovered a suspected cocaine cache officials valued at up to US$50 million.

When the guards are the thieves

On Tuesday, a jury in Kakata convicted two LDEA agents posted at RIA, Special Agent Joe Logan and Agent Lovette Flowers, along with Nigerian national Tony Obi. Judge Roosevelt Z. Willie of the 13th Judicial Circuit sentenced each to 20 years, the maximum.

Prosecutors said the agents took four of 14 seized plates of cocaine and sold them, and that the network paid about US$10,000 in bribes to LDEA officers. The case began in July 2025 with Quita Dolo Kosso, who landed at RIA from Thailand on a Kenya Airways flight with about 3.4 kilograms of cocaine. She pleaded guilty and is serving five years.

The lesson for travelers is uncomfortable. Drugs can be caught at the gate and still leak out the back door. Europe has noticed both.

Brussels takes aim

Van Weel is in Luxembourg, where EU justice and home affairs ministers meet Thursday and Friday. The agenda covers migration, the EU drugs strategic framework and how the geopolitical climate is affecting Europe’s security. He wrote on X that talks would include “the safety of Europe and the EU-sanctions regime for organized crime.”

He is urging ministers to adopt the regime swiftly, Politico Europe’s Playbook reported. He told Playbook the Bolle Jos case calls for measures against all organized criminals Europe cannot immediately detain, “not only against him,” and said he hopes the regime is concluded by year’s end.

An EU diplomat with the Dutch delegation told OCCRP that cross-border networks can be “very effective” when based in a third country whose authorities will not cooperate or extradite. “The standard criminal law approach isn’t achieving the results we want,” the diplomat said. “That is why there is a push to expand that toolkit.”

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the package in her 2025 State of the Union address, and the EU Council mandated work on it. On July 9, the Commission and the EU’s foreign policy chief proposed a regime covering drug trafficking, migrant smuggling, human and firearms trafficking and money laundering. It would freeze assets, impose trade restrictions and bar listed people from entering or transiting EU states.

It still has to be agreed, and adoption needs the backing of all 27 member states. Earlier efforts stalled because national police feared sanctions could tip off suspects and spoil investigations. Van Weel said support is stronger now.

What it means for SN Brussels passengers

Sanctions target kingpins, their financiers and fixers, not ordinary travelers. But passengers on the Monrovia–Freetown–Brussels line already live with the side effects, and those are likely to grow.

Tighter checks on arrival. The 51-kilogram arrest came during a targeted customs check of passengers off the Freetown flight. Expect more of those, and more bags opened.

Networks recruiting the young. This week, Belgian and French authorities announced 21 arrests in a ring that used Brussels Airport. It recruited “extractors” through social media, bought tickets just to reach baggage halls and paid airport workers to pull drugs from suitcases before they reached the carousel.

Your bag, someone else’s crime.

The RIA cases show cargo and luggage can be tampered with by insiders. Lock and label bags, and refuse parcels from anyone, even relatives, without seeing what is inside.

Travel bans for facilitators. Once adopted, the EU regime could bar listed people from entering or passing through Europe. Anyone working for a front company, freight forwarder or fixer tied to a listed network risks being swept up.

A reputation tax. Every bust adds to the suspicion attached to a Liberian or Sierra Leonean passport at a European counter. Honest travelers pay that bill in delays and questions.

For now, the man Europe most wants sits a short flight from Monrovia, beyond reach. Van Weel insists Freetown could change that in a day. The question for Liberia is whether it is seen as part of the problem or part of the fix. The 20-year sentences handed down in Kakata this week were a start. The next test is the US$19.2 million trial.
